title: G1C.3: Auth/session consolidation design
description:
DESIGN ONLY - no implementation in this slice.

INVARIANT: one browser session authority (Clerk) -> one backend authenticated identity -> current_user.id established exactly once.

Sequenced so each step is independently revertible and none is a big-bang:

STEP 1 (zero behaviour change). Rename the concept, not the mechanism: introduce a single accessor in lib/ that returns the Clerk token, and route the 20 localStorage reads in agentSlice.ts and apiManager.ts through it. The key stays for now. This collapses 20 read sites to 1 and is pure refactor - tests should not change.

STEP 2. Delete the four unreachable thunks and their three localStorage writers from agentSlice.ts, plus ApiManager.login/signup/getGoogleLoginUrl/handleGoogleCallback. Dead-code removal, proven unreachable in G1C.2. Backend endpoints stay.

STEP 3. Decide the password-reset incoherence. Either remove /forgot-password and /reset-password and let Clerk own recovery, or keep them and add the missing local login. Removing is the smaller and more coherent option, but it is a PRODUCT decision, not a code one - flag for the user.

STEP 4. Replace the localStorage key with an in-memory holder plus Clerk's getToken. localStorage persistence buys nothing once Clerk is the authority and is the actual XSS exposure.

STEP 5 (backend, and only after 1-4 and after G1D). Remove the decode_access_token fallback from get_current_user, making Clerk the single verification path. Requires certainty that no non-browser caller uses a local token - scheduler and smoke scripts must be checked.

NOT IN THIS SLICE and explicitly fenced by the user: do not remove local JWT yet, do not change Clerk behaviour, do not touch the backend origin.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialUI commit e15eb01. Design implemented, phases 1-4 all landed. Transport untouched.

PHASE 1 - lib/authToken.ts is the single boundary, and it holds the PROVIDER rather than the token. app/components/AuthTokenBridge.tsx registers Clerk's getToken and is mounted inside ClerkProvider in the root layout, so it covers every route including the landing page and the OAuth callback pages - not only the AuthGuard-wrapped ones. The fourteen Redux thunks and the ApiManager helpers now call getAuthToken() per request, so Clerk's own refresh runs and a rotated token is picked up. Asserted by a test that returns a different token on each provider call.

PHASE 2 - deleted the four unreachable thunks with their twelve reducer cases, and ApiManager.login/signup/getGoogleLoginUrl/handleGoogleCallback. Backend endpoints untouched, per the fence.

PHASE 3 - FOUR client state-construction sites, not the one the closure review recorded: oauthActions.ts plus fetchLoginUrl, fetchLinkedInLoginUrl and fetchXLoginUrl in agentSlice. All removed, and the `state` PARAMETER is gone from the four authorization-URL methods so it cannot be reintroduced for compatibility. The stale OAUTH_SERVER_STATE_ENABLED docstring is gone. Removing the state also removed a getCurrentUser round-trip per connect, since the user id was fetched only to build that string.

PHASE 4 - COMPLETED, not blocked. No production module names app_auth_token. appAuthToken is gone from the Redux store. The landing page reads Clerk isSignedIn instead of inferring a session from a stored token, which also fixes a latent bug: a stale token made the page claim a session that had already ended. app_auth_user survives as a profile cache - it is not a credential - and logout clears it with everything else.

TESTS: __tests__/auth_boundary.test.ts, 24 tests, split behavioural and mechanical. The mechanical half matters more than it looks: a reintroduced localStorage read would keep working as long as something still wrote that key, so it would fail no behavioural test. Guards: only lib/authToken.ts may name app_auth_token; no production module reads a bearer token from storage; exactly ONE module calls getToken. auth_session_regression.test.ts was rewritten rather than deleted - its old assertion (the stored token survives a 401) would now pass vacuously, so it asserts the property it was protecting: a 401 does not tear down the Clerk session, and the next request gets a fresh token.

KNOCK-ON: AgentDebugDrawer had a local variable named getToken that was NOT Clerk's - it resolved through useFreshAuthToken. Renamed resolveToken so the identifier means exactly one thing and the boundary guard can be mechanical.

VERIFICATION: npm ci from the lockfile (manifest and lockfile provably unmodified); lint exit 0; build exit 0, 11 routes; tests 4 suites, 50 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Baseline before this slice was 25 tests.

RAISED, NOT FIXED HERE: socialhub-ijn.3.3.6 - app/page.tsx still routes OAuth callbacks by parsing state PREFIXES that G1B.2 stopped issuing, so every provider now falls through to the Facebook branch. Certain: the prefix matching is dead against an opaque state. Not certain: which redirect URI each provider console has registered, which decides whether this is a live break. Fenced out of this slice by "do not change provider OAuth callbacks", and it must be verified before it is coded.
close_reason: Canonical Clerk token boundary landed; dead local-auth plumbing deleted; client OAuth state construction removed; localStorage token persistence eliminated. lint/build/tests green, 50 tests.

title: G1C.2: Clerk vs app_auth_token forensic trace
description:
DONE 2026-08-27, read-only.

HEADLINE, and it contradicts the G0 framing: there are NOT two live browser auth mechanisms. There is ONE live authority (Clerk) plus unreachable local-JWT plumbing.

- /login and /signup render Clerk <SignIn>/<SignUp>. There is no local login form anywhere.
- loginWithEmail, signupWithEmail, fetchGoogleLoginUrl and handleGoogleAuthCallback are defined in lib/features/agentSlice.ts and dispatched from NOWHERE. Verified by grepping every .ts/.tsx outside agentSlice: zero references.
- So the three localStorage.setItem('app_auth_token', payload.access_token) writers at agentSlice 727/744/864 are unreachable from the UI.
- localStorage['app_auth_token'] therefore holds a CLERK session token, written by AuthGuard (app/components/AuthGuard/index.tsx:36) and lib/useFreshAuthToken.ts:17 from getToken({skipCache:true}). The key is a legacy NAME, not a second credential.

Backend: get_current_user (auth_routes.py:66) tries verify_clerk_token -> sync_clerk_user FIRST, then falls back to decode_access_token. One header, two verification paths. sync_clerk_user reconciles by clerk_user_id then by email, so both paths converge on one users row PROVIDED the emails match.

STILL REACHABLE local-credential surface, which is the real incoherence:
- /forgot-password and /reset-password call ApiManager.forgotPassword/resetPassword, which set users.hashed_password.
- POST /auth/login verifies that password. Nothing in the UI calls it.
- A user can therefore reset a password they can never use. That is the coherent thing to fix, and it is smaller than 'remove local JWT'.

29 app_auth_token sites in 7 source files + 1 test. Grouped in the closure report on the epic.

NOT CHANGED: no auth behaviour touched, per the slice fence.
close_reason: Trace complete and read-only. Clerk is the only live browser authority; the local-JWT thunks are unreachable; app_auth_token holds a Clerk token.

title: Remove import-time Base.metadata.create_all and ad hoc ALTER TABLE from app/main.py
description:
Problem: app/main.py runs schema DDL at IMPORT TIME, which contradicts the schema-authority rule that Alembic is the single schema authority.

Two separate things, both at module scope in app/main.py:
- line 23, Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine), wrapped in try/except that prints and continues
- lines 29-46, hand-written "ALTER TABLE scheduled_posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ..." for x_account_id, instagram_account_id and image_url

Why this was not merely untidy, measured during the G1B closure review:
create_all only issues CREATE TABLE for tables that do NOT exist. It never adds a
column to an existing table. So it does NOT rescue a deploy that ships new mapped
columns without their migration - it silently does nothing, and every ORM query
against that table then fails with "no such column". Reproduced locally against a
database at f4a2c7e9b1d5 with G1B.4 code: SELECT on users raises OperationalError.

That makes the import-time DDL actively misleading. It looks like a safety net,
it is not one, and its presence is why "the schema will sort itself out on boot"
is a tempting and wrong assumption during a rollout.

It also means startup DDL races between multiple workers/containers, and that a
failure prints and continues rather than stopping the process.

Scope:
- delete Base.metadata.create_all from app/main.py
- delete the hand-written ALTER TABLE block; the three columns are already in the
  Alembic chain (verify before deleting)
- tests construct their own schema via Base.metadata.create_all in fixtures, which
  is correct and stays

Prerequisites, which is why this is not done yet:
- the deployed production Alembic revision must be KNOWN (still UNKNOWN from G0)
- production must be confirmed at head, because after this change a database that
  is behind will simply fail rather than half-fix itself

Acceptance: no DDL executes at import; a database behind head fails loudly at the
first query rather than being silently patched; the full suite stays green.
Tests: assert app.main executes no DDL (import with an engine that records
statements); assert the three scheduled_posts columns exist in the chain.
Rollback: single-file revert.

Blocks: socialhub-ijn.3.2.5 step 2 is safer once this is done, but does not
require it.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend ac0bb20 (code), 8dd80e2 (tests).
Removed both import-time DDL blocks from app/main.py. Verified BEFORE deleting the ALTER TABLE block that x_account_id, instagram_account_id and image_url are all in the chain at 1a7e5c0d3b92.
NOT replaced with migrate-on-start, and a test asserts it was not: a process that migrates itself decides schema changes at container start, in parallel across replicas, with no operator gate.
GUARD tests/test_startup_schema_authority.py, 9 tests. The load-bearing one imports app.main in a SUBPROCESS against an empty SQLite file and asserts the file still has no tables - in-process would be a no-op against an already-imported module and would pass vacuously. A second installs a before_cursor_execute listener and asserts zero DDL statements, catching DDL that happens to be idempotent.
The static guards parse each module and STRIP docstrings/comments before scanning, because main.py deliberately explains at length why create_all and ALTER TABLE do not belong there - a guard that flagged its own explanation would push the next person to delete the documentation rather than the defect. One test asserts the stripping has not made the guards blind.
DISCRIMINATION: 5 of 9 fail against pre-fix main.py, including both behavioural tests.
DEPLOYMENT INVARIANT documented in main.py under the heading MIGRATION BEFORE CODE.
VERIFICATION: migration suites 25 passed; SQLite 959; PostgreSQL 977.
close_reason: Startup DDL removed; Alembic is sole schema authority; no migrate-on-start; 9-test guard, 5 discriminating; both migration suites green.

title: G1B.4 rollout: production key, migration, backfill and mode advance
description:
The code half of G1B.4 is committed (socialbackend 766eb52, 066357f) and the repository default is phase 1 + MODE=dual. This bead is the operational half. EVERY step needs explicit approval. Nothing below has been done.

STEP 0 - PREREQUISITES. These gate step 2 and are not optional notes.
0a. Determine the PRODUCTION POSTGRESQL SERVER VERSION. Still UNKNOWN from G0. The chain is validated on 16.2 only.
    sudo docker exec socialhub-api python -c "from sqlalchemy import create_engine,text; import os; print(create_engine(os.environ['DATABASE_URL']).connect().execute(text('select version()')).scalar())"
0b. Determine the DEPLOYED ALEMBIC REVISION. Still UNKNOWN from G0.
    sudo docker exec socialhub-api alembic current
    Expected to be at or before f4a2c7e9b1d5. If it is behind, the repair revisions 1a7e5c0d3b92, 2c9f4d81e6a3, 3e8b06fa2c14 and 5d1c93b7ae60 will also run; they are guarded no-ops on the deployed lineage but they DO execute.
    If alembic_version is empty or unrecognised, STOP: stamping the wrong revision can skip a migration permanently.
0c. Confirm a database backup exists and is restorable, taken after 0b.

STEP 1 - KEY PROVISIONING.
    python -m scripts.encrypt_provider_credentials generate-key
Store in /home/ubuntu/fb_agent/.env:
    PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS={"v1": "<key>"}
    PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_ACTIVE_KEY_VERSION=v1
1b. SEPARATE KEY BACKUP - a distinct requirement from step 1, not a footnote.
    The key must be stored somewhere the database backup is NOT. A key backed up alongside the ciphertext restores the attacker's position exactly and the encryption achieves nothing.
    Losing the key makes every encrypted credential unrecoverable: every user must reconnect every account. There is no recovery path.
    Record WHERE it is backed up, and who can retrieve it, before continuing.

STEP 2 - MIGRATION FIRST. THIS ORDERING IS MANDATORY, NOT ADVISORY.
    sudo docker exec socialhub-api alembic upgrade head   # -> 7b3d5e0c81af
Measured during the G1B closure review: deploying the new code BEFORE this migration breaks every ORM query against users, page_tokens, linkedin_accounts and x_accounts with "no such column ..._ciphertext". Import-time create_all does NOT save this - it only issues CREATE TABLE for tables that do not exist and never adds a column to an existing table (see socialhub-ijn.3.10). The failure mode is a total outage of login and publishing, not a degraded feature.

STEP 3 - DEPLOY AT MODE=dual.
    PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_MODE=dual
Both columns are written, so a code rollback still finds a usable credential.
3b. PROVIDER SMOKE TESTS - one internal account per provider, connect AND publish, for facebook, instagram, linkedin and x. Four providers, both operations. A connect that succeeds while publish fails is the signature of a read path that was missed.

STEP 4 - BACKFILL, WHILE STILL IN dual.
    python -m scripts.encrypt_provider_credentials backfill
Running it in dual rather than encrypted_only keeps a data-level rollback possible: the plaintext column is still populated.
4b. ZERO PLAINTEXT VERIFICATION.
    python -m scripts.encrypt_provider_credentials status
Exits 1 while any row still holds a readable credential, so it is usable as a gate. Do not advance until it exits 0.

STEP 5 - MODE=encrypted_only. Re-run the step 3b smoke tests. New and refreshed credentials stop populating the plaintext column; existing rows are already encrypted by step 4.

STEP 6 - MODE=strict, later. A remaining plaintext row now raises instead of being read. Only enter this after 4b has held at zero across a full refresh cycle.

STEP 7 - LEGACY COLUMN REMOVAL, later still, and separately. A new migration must relax the three NOT NULL constraints (page_tokens.page_access_token, linkedin_accounts.access_token, x_accounts.access_token) and then drop all five plaintext columns. THIS IS THE ONLY IRREVERSIBLE STEP; rollback is restore-from-backup. Not written yet, deliberately.

Per-step rollback: socialbackend/docs/PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION.md.

DISTINCTION THIS BEAD EXISTS TO HOLD: the application SUPPORTS encrypted credential storage today. PRODUCTION CREDENTIALS ARE NOT ENCRYPTED and will not be until step 4b reports zero. Do not describe G1B.4 as done before then.

title: Validate the repaired migration chain against PostgreSQL
description:
Problem: the chain repair (socialhub-ijn.3.5) was validated on SQLite only, because the local verification environment has no PostgreSQL. Two things are therefore unproven on the engine production actually runs:
 1. c3d4e5f6a7b8 creates the LangGraph checkpoint tables ONLY on postgresql, so that branch has never been executed by any test.
 2. SQLite batch_alter_table emulates ALTER via table rebuild; PostgreSQL does not. Behaviour of the historical batch operations can differ.
Scope: run upgrade head from empty, and the representative stamped-lineage upgrade, against a real PostgreSQL instance; extend tests/test_migration_chain.py to run there when TEST_POSTGRES_URL is set.
Out of scope: applying anything to production.
Acceptance: both scenarios pass on PostgreSQL; checkpoint tables are created; schema parity holds including the checkpoint tables.
Dependencies: socialhub-ijn.3.5.
NOTE: this is the last gate before Alembic can be called trustworthy for a production migration.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): commits socialbackend f15d0cc, f5051f7. PostgreSQL 16.2, ephemeral instance via pgserver on a unix socket. Docker was attempted first and rejected: the local daemon returns 500 for every API version 1.44-1.55 then hangs.
1 EMPTY POSTGRES: 17 revisions apply cleanly from base.
2 POSTGRES-ONLY BRANCH: c3d4e5f6a7b8 executed for the first time ever. All four checkpoint tables created, and the dialect-specific types are real - checkpoints.checkpoint/metadata are JSONB, checkpoint_blobs.blob and checkpoint_writes.blob are BYTEA. Asserted on types, not merely on table presence.
3 SCHEMA PARITY: 0 missing tables, 0 unexplained extras, 0 column differences, 0 nullability mismatches, 0 missing indexes, 0 missing foreign keys. FK parity matters specifically here because SQLite does not enforce FKs by default.
4 REPRESENTATIVE LINEAGE: create_all-built PG database seeded with user, page, linkedin account and scheduled post, stamped at e5a7c1d2f9b3, upgraded to head. All rows intact, content verified, oauth_transactions created, repairs ran as no-ops.
5 OAUTH REVISION: applies; state_hash unique index present.
6 SINGLE HEAD: f4a2c7e9b1d5.
7 DOWNGRADE: repaired range down and back; full downgrade to base leaves zero tables on PostgreSQL.
8 REPEATABLE: tests/test_migration_chain_postgres.py, 13 tests, opt-in via TEST_POSTGRES_URL, each provisioning and dropping its own database. Skips cleanly when unset so CI is unaffected.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (this is why the bead existed): users.fb_user_id and users.access_token were NOT NULL in the chain but nullable in the model. No user-creation path supplies access_token, so an Alembic-built schema could not register a user at all - every signup, Clerk sync and Google login would have raised a NOT NULL violation. Production was unaffected only because its table came from create_all. Repaired by 5d1c93b7ae60, with a regression test that performs a real Clerk-style insert against an Alembic-built schema.

SECOND DEFECT, PRE-EXISTING: tests/test_postgres_checkpoint_integration.py had never executed because TEST_POSTGRES_URL was never set. It stamped an EMPTY database mid-chain then upgraded, which cannot work (e5a7c1d2f9b3 creates agent_trace_runs with an FK to users), and created product_sentinel without dropping it so it could pass at most once per database. Verified the failing revision is e5a7c1d2f9b3, which this work did not modify. Fixture repaired; it now passes repeatably. Fixed rather than filed because leaving it broken would have handed over a PostgreSQL path that fails on first use.

SUITE: SQLite only 618 passed / 14 skipped. PostgreSQL enabled 632 passed / 0 failed, run twice with identical results.
REMAINING: PostgreSQL 16.2 tested; the production server version is UNKNOWN. import-time create_all still present, as scoped.
close_reason: Chain validated on real PostgreSQL 16.2: empty upgrade, checkpoint branch executed with real JSONB/BYTEA, total schema parity including FKs, representative lineage with data intact, downgrade to base, single head, and a repeatable opt-in suite. One blocking defect found and fixed.

title: G1B.4: Provider token encryption at rest
description:
Scope: authenticated encryption for access_token, refresh_token and page_access_token columns behind a storage abstraction, with key versioning and a migration path for existing plaintext values.
Out of scope: OAuth state (G1B.1-3); token transport in URLs (ijn.3.1.12).
Dependencies: G1B.3.
Acceptance: no plaintext provider token at rest; key sourced from the environment, never the database; rotation strategy documented; no token in logs, state or memory.
REQUIRES APPROVAL: key management and a data migration over existing rows.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): commits socialbackend 766eb52 (code), 066357f (tests). Docs: socialbackend/docs/PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION.md.

INVENTORY - 5 credential columns across 4 tables: users.access_token, page_tokens.page_access_token (NOT NULL), linkedin_accounts.access_token (NOT NULL), x_accounts.access_token (NOT NULL), x_accounts.refresh_token. Deliberately excluded: users.hashed_password (already one-way) and users.reset_token (looked up BY VALUE through an index, so encrypting breaks the lookup - a separate decision, filed as ijn.3.9).
52 references across 12 modules; all now go through the store. Verified the graph/checkpoint/memory layer never OWNS these values - agent_graph only redacts the NAMES (memory_store, tools/redaction, failure_recovery) and clears them on disconnect.

ARCHITECTURE: provider services -> app/services/credential_store.py -> app/core/credential_encryption.py. Services never encrypt. API: store_access_token, store_refresh_token, read_access_token, read_refresh_token, has_refresh_token, clear_credentials, plus migrate_record/backfill/plaintext_credential_counts for operations.

CRYPTO / DEPENDENCY: AES-256-GCM from `cryptography` 50.0.1, ALREADY present as a transitive dependency of python-jose[cryptography]. NO NEW DEPENDENCY. Nothing hand-rolled: concatenate a nonce, one library call, base64. Envelope ENC1:<key_version>:<b64url(nonce||ct||tag)>, 96-bit fresh nonce, AAD binds ENC1|version|table.column. KNOWN LIMIT, stated not hidden: AAD does not bind the row id (a new row has none until flush), so a ciphertext moved between ROWS of the same column still decrypts; row-level authority stays the G1A ownership checks.

NEW CONFIG KEYS (3, reported as required): PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS (JSON {version: base64 32-byte key}), PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_ACTIVE_KEY_VERSION, PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_MODE.

SCHEMA: migration 7b3d5e0c81af, ten nullable columns (<name>_ciphertext TEXT, <name>_key_version VARCHAR(32)). Purely additive - no column altered, no NOT NULL relaxed, no data moved. Downgrade is a clean drop. Head moved f4a2c7e9b1d5 -> 7b3d5e0c81af.

KEY VERSIONS: every version in the keyring decrypts, only the active encrypts. Unknown version FAILS CLOSED - never assumed to be the active key, which would silently corrupt on a misconfigured rollback. The version is recorded twice (inside the AEAD-protected envelope and mirrored in a column for SQL-targeted rotation); disagreement is a hard failure.

PHASES. Deployed here: phase 1 schema + MODE=dual (write both, read ciphertext first). That is the safest intermediate: a code rollback still finds a usable credential, a schema rollback drops columns without touching data. Phase 2 (encrypted_only) and phase 5 (strict) are implemented and tested but config-gated. Phase 3 backfill and phase 4 proof are the scripts/encrypt_provider_credentials.py command - status exits 1 while plaintext rows remain, so it works as a deploy gate. Phase 6 (drop legacy columns) is NOT written: it is the only irreversible step and belongs in its own migration, which should also relax the three NOT NULL columns.

CODE_VERIFIER: inspected and NOT folded into token storage. consume_transaction now clears code_verifier once its single legitimate reader has it, so its lifetime is one request instead of the remainder of the 10-minute TTL. The atomic claim is untouched - the clear is a second statement, reachable only by the caller that won the claim. Two tests, including a raw-SQL row check.

TESTS tests/test_credential_encryption.py, 58. Keys generated per test so no key constant exists to leak; one plaintext sentinel per credential path. Covers every listed requirement plus a whole-database sweep, session-reload persistence, mode-by-mode rollback properties, backfill idempotency, rotation, retired-key fail-closed, and a guard test that no module outside the boundary touches a credential column (in dual mode a forgotten direct read keeps working and would not fail until production months later).

TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY THESE TESTS, both fixed: clear_credentials wrote NULL into the three NOT NULL legacy columns (the empty value is now read from the mapped column's nullability, so it becomes NULL by itself at phase 6); and the first tamper test flipped a base64 character near the end, which can land in bits padding discards - it passed or failed on the random nonce. Now flips a decoded byte, parametrized across nonce, ciphertext and tag; 5 consecutive clean runs.

KNOCK-ON: test_credential_logging's duck-typed _Acct is now a real XAccount, because credential reads resolve their column context from the mapped class. Head assertions in test_migration_chain.py, test_migration_chain_postgres.py and test_oauth_state_security.py updated.

VERIFICATION: focused provider-auth regression 341 passed; full suite SQLite 848 passed / 18 skipped (twice, for flake); full suite PostgreSQL 16.2 866 passed / 0 failed. Migration exercised on SQLite and real PostgreSQL: fresh chain, populated database at the previous head, downgrade, and a create_all-built database where the columns already exist.

NOT DONE, ALL APPROVAL-GATED: provision and back up the production key (losing it makes every encrypted credential unrecoverable - users would have to reconnect every account); apply 7b3d5e0c81af to production; set the three config keys; run the backfill; advance to encrypted_only then strict. Order matters: the migration must land before code that writes ciphertext, and the backfill must complete before strict.

title: Alembic chain cannot build a database from zero
description:
Problem: 'alembic upgrade head' from base fails at revision 11cb3af4a1e4, the SECOND migration in the chain. It runs batch_op.drop_index('ix_published_posts_id') on a published_posts table whose initial revision (2426bd583d2d) never creates that index. sqlite3.OperationalError: no such index.
Verified during G1B.1 with the new f4a2c7e9b1d5 migration removed entirely, so it is pre-existing and not introduced or worsened by that work.
CONSEQUENCE: no fresh database can be built from migrations. Production schema exists because of the import-time Base.metadata.create_all() in app/main.py, not because of Alembic. That contradicts 'Alembic is the single schema authority' and means a zero-to-head migration test is impossible until fixed. It also means an approved production 'alembic upgrade head' only works because the schema is already present.
Scope: repair or supersede 11cb3af4a1e4 so the chain applies cleanly from base; then a clean-DB migration test becomes possible.
Out of scope: removing import-time create_all (tracked with the schema-authority work).
Acceptance: alembic upgrade head succeeds against an empty database; alembic downgrade base succeeds; a test asserts both.
Tests: zero-to-head and head-to-zero on a temporary database.
Rollback: migration edits are reversible; no production database is touched.
REQUIRES APPROVAL before any production migration action.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): commits socialbackend ea1e428, bf02386.

ROOT CAUSE = C producing B, not A. 2426bd583d2d creates only users and page_tokens. 11cb3af4a1e4 drops published_posts and alters scheduled_posts, neither created by any prior revision, because create_all() supplied them at import time and autogenerate ran against a live database. FORENSIC SCOPE: SIX model tables (scheduled_posts, published_posts, linkedin_accounts, x_accounts, ideas, autopilot_configs) and SEVEN columns (users.username/reset_token/reset_token_expires/created_at/updated_at, page_tokens.created_at/updated_at) existed only via create_all. 11cb3af4a1e4 itself is CORRECT about intent - published_posts really was removed from the models - so the fix supplies missing history rather than weakening the drop. No operation in any historical revision was altered; only two down_revision pointers were re-pointed.

REVISIONS ADDED: 1a7e5c0d3b92 (tables, after initial), 2c9f4d81e6a3 (ideas/autopilot_configs, late), 3e8b06fa2c14 (columns, late). All guarded so they are no-ops on the deployed lineage. published_posts reproduced from the DDL preserved in 11cb3af4a1e4's own downgrade(); scheduled_posts omits project_name because 11cb3af4a1e4 adds it next. The remaining scheduled_posts columns are a RECONSTRUCTION of what create_all produced, stated as such in the revision docstring rather than presented as recovered history.

VALIDATION:
 1 EMPTY DB: 16 revisions apply cleanly from base.
 2 SCHEMA PARITY: 0 missing tables, 0 column differences, 0 missing declared indexes vs SQLAlchemy metadata. ONE intentional difference: the LangGraph checkpoint tables, which c3d4e5f6a7b8 creates only when dialect is postgresql - asserted by reading that guard, not by hardcoding an exemption.
 3 EXISTING-SCHEMA UPGRADE: create_all-built database seeded with a user, a page and a scheduled post, stamped at e5a7c1d2f9b3, upgraded to head. All rows intact, content verified, oauth_transactions created.
 4 OAUTH REVISION: f4a2c7e9b1d5 applies on top; state_hash and code_verifier present.
 5 SINGLE HEAD: f4a2c7e9b1d5; chain linearity and a single base asserted.
 6 DOWNGRADE: repaired range down and back up; full downgrade to base leaves zero tables.
 7 REGRESSION: a test asserts the failure text 'no such index'/'ix_published_posts_id' is absent, so this specific break is named if reintroduced.

KNOWN LIMIT, DELIBERATE: 11cb3af4a1e4 is not idempotent - replaying it over a populated schema fails with 'duplicate column name: project_name'. Left that way on purpose; making a historical revision replayable would misrepresent what it did, and no supported bootstrap path replays it. Idempotency tests are scoped to the three repair revisions and document this.

TESTS: tests/test_migration_chain.py, 16 tests. Full backend suite 618 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed (was 602).

NOT DONE, as scoped: import-time create_all() remains in app/main.py; removing it belongs to the schema-authority work once Alembic has been exercised against PostgreSQL.
close_reason: Chain builds the full schema from zero with exact model parity; deployed lineage upgrades with data intact; downgrade to base clean; single head; regression pinned.

title: Provider access tokens are passed in URL query strings
description:
Problem: Meta and Instagram calls embed the access token in the query string rather than an Authorization header.
  app/services/analytics_service.py:45,123,188
  app/services/facebook_service.py:83,90
  app/services/instagram_service.py:124
Consequence, verified empirically during G1A-9: requests exceptions stringify the request URL, so BOTH ConnectionError and HTTPError carry a live token in str(e). G1A-9 closed the logging exposure by redacting exception text, but the token still travels in the URL and can therefore reach proxy logs, CDN logs, provider-side access logs, APM traces and browser referrers for any surface that echoes it.
Scope: move token transport to the Authorization header for Meta and Instagram calls.
Out of scope: token-at-rest encryption (G1B); provider API version upgrades (G3).
Dependencies: none, but touches provider integration so it fits naturally alongside G3/G7.
Acceptance: no provider request URL contains access_token; calls send Authorization: Bearer. A test asserts the constructed URL for each site carries no credential.
Tests: per-service URL construction tests; existing analytics suite must stay green.
Runtime evidence: captured outbound request URLs in the mocked provider suite.
Rollback: per-service revert.
Docs: PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_MATRIX auth rows.
NOTE: G1A-9 mitigated the log path only. This is the transport defect underneath it.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend 45be105 (code), 25f9ae9 (tests).
SEVEN sites, not the six this bead recorded: facebook_service.delete_post used params={'access_token': ...}, which requests turns into a query string just the same - missed originally because it is not an f-string.
ENDPOINT MATRIX (provider / endpoint / current / official / action):
  Facebook  / GET graph.facebook.com/v22.0/me?fields=id,name          / query / Bearer supported / MOVED
  Facebook  / GET .../me/accounts?fields=...                          / query / Bearer supported / MOVED
  Facebook  / GET .../{page_id}/insights                              / query / Bearer supported / MOVED
  Facebook  / GET .../{post_id}/insights                              / query / Bearer supported / MOVED
  Instagram / GET .../{ig_account_id}/insights (graph.facebook.com)   / query / Bearer supported / MOVED
  Instagram / GET graph.instagram.com/me?fields=...                   / query / Bearer supported / MOVED
  Facebook  / DELETE .../{post_id} (params=)                          / query / Bearer supported / MOVED
  Facebook  / GET .../oauth/access_token (code, fb_exchange_token)    / query / PARAMETERS ONLY  / UNCHANGED
  LinkedIn  / api.linkedin.com/*                                      / Bearer / Bearer          / already correct
  X         / api.twitter.com/2/*                                     / Bearer / Bearer          / already correct
DOCUMENTATION VERIFIED FIRST, not assumed:
- graph.facebook.com: 'include your token in an authorization request header, preceded by Bearer', with a curl example against graph.facebook.com/v25.0 (Meta Access Tokens Guide, developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/access-tokens/).
- graph.instagram.com: every curl example in the Instagram messaging API guide uses -H 'Authorization: Bearer <INSTAGRAM_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN>'. The get-started guide also shows the query form, so both are accepted and the header is the safer.
DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: /oauth/access_token (the credential IS the payload; Meta defines these as parameters, no header form exists - an unsupported API change otherwise); 'fields=id,name,access_token' on /me/accounts (names a field to RETURN, each page's own token, not this request's credential); POST form bodies (not in the URL, different risk class, tracked separately).
TESTS tests/test_provider_token_transport.py, 14. Behavioural tests inspect the ACTUAL outgoing request - url, params and headers as requests received them - so a token spliced back by any route fails, not only the f-string form. The static guard walks function by function so the OAuth exchange is excused BY NAME rather than by excusing its whole module.
DISCRIMINATION: 10 of 14 fail pre-fix.
VERIFICATION: SQLite 959; PostgreSQL 977; security gate 17/17.
close_reason: Seven query-string token sites moved to Authorization: Bearer after verifying official Meta/Instagram docs; OAuth exchange correctly excluded; 14 tests, 10 discriminating.

title: G10.C: Clarification and interaction metrics
description:
Adds interaction-quality measurement to the evaluation framework. Without these, the 'ask only when it materially changes the action' rule is prompt wording, not an invariant.

METRICS:
  clarification precision     of the questions asked, how many were necessary
  clarification recall        of the situations requiring a question, how many produced one
  unnecessary-question rate   the interrogation-form failure mode
  unsafe-assumption rate      proceeded when it should have stopped - the dangerous direction
  successful-resume rate      after an answer, did execution actually continue
  task-continuation accuracy  did it return to the CORRECT suspended task with previously completed work preserved

task-continuation accuracy matters most with LangGraph checkpoints: many systems ask a good question and then forget why they asked it.

Scope: metrics plus dataset labels.
Out of scope: the interaction runtime itself (G4I).
Dependencies: G4I.9.
acceptance_criteria: All six metrics are computed by the evaluation runner and reported per suite. unsafe-assumption rate and task-continuation accuracy are release gates, not advisory numbers. A regression in unnecessary-question rate fails the suite.

title: G4I.9: Clarification evaluation suite
description:
Turn the UX rule into an enforced invariant instead of prompt wording.
MUST ASK: 'Publish this' with three candidate artifacts; 'Schedule tomorrow' with no default time; 'Delete my last post' with account ambiguity.
MUST NOT ASK: 'Write a LinkedIn post about AI'; 'Analyze my last 30 days of LinkedIn engagement'; 'Schedule tomorrow morning' when a preference maps morning safely.
MUST REQUIRE APPROVAL, NOT CLARIFICATION: 'Publish this now' when every detail is known.
Scope: evaluation cases plus metrics.
Dependencies: G4I.2, G4I.3, G4I.6, G10.
acceptance_criteria: Every case above is encoded and passing. The suite fails if the agent asks an unnecessary question, and fails if it substitutes clarification for approval.

title: G4I.7: Free-text answer resolution
description:
Map natural language onto the pending interaction: 'use the second one', 'LinkedIn and X', 'nine in the morning' -> resolved against user timezone and preferences.
Voice and text share this path; input_mode is metadata, not a separate architecture.
Scope: answer resolution.
Dependencies: G4I.3, G4I.6.
acceptance_criteria: 'Use the second one' resolves to the correct option id. 'Nine in the morning' resolves to a timezone-correct datetime. An unresolvable answer re-asks rather than guessing. Low-confidence transcription of a consequential value triggers a re-ask.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend db5587e (code), b5d434a (tests). app/agent_graph/interaction_input.py, 36 tests.
ONE CONTRACT FOR EVERY TRANSPORT. The organising test runs the same intent as chat text, a button, a card and a voice transcript and asserts the four InteractionAnswers are EQUAL. If that holds, the runtime provably cannot behave differently per input mode, because it never sees the difference. RawAnswer.source is telemetry only and a second test asserts no decision reads it.
answered_by IS SERVER-DERIVED: a parameter, never a field on the raw payload - RawAnswer has no identity field at all. A hostile card payload carrying answered_by/user_id/sub is normalized with the caller's id regardless. Same defect class as _state_user_id in G1B.
FREE TEXT resolves in three tiers - exact, unique prefix, unique substring - each exhausted before the next, so a value matching one option exactly is never lost to another that merely contains it. Zero or multiple matches raise AmbiguousAnswer WITH the candidates rather than guessing; picking for the user is how the wrong page gets published.
APPROVAL VOCABULARY IS SMALL AND EXPLICIT. Five forms of qualified or unclear yes are refused, including 'yes, but change the caption' - a qualified yes is not a yes.
CONNECTION LIFECYCLE: offers ids rather than free text so 'I connected it' and 'never mind' are distinguishable without guessing; a completed connection resumes the SAME task with blocked_reason cleared; a cancelled one resolves without connecting; a stale connection answer is refused. Connecting is explicitly NOT approving - a task resumed that way still meets the approval boundary, asserted.
TASK CONTEXT IS CARRIED BY task_id ALONE. A test asserts no goal, plan or capability field exists on InteractionRequest, so nothing copied into an interaction can drift out of sync with the plan.
No frontend change.
close_reason: Free-text answers resolve in three deterministic tiers; ambiguity refuses with candidates rather than guessing.

title: G4I.6: Resume interaction from checkpoint
description:
thread_id -> checkpoint restored -> pending interaction located -> answer applied -> task resumes. Must work after a client reconnect and after a process restart.
This is where LangGraph earns its place rather than decorating the codebase with arrows.
Scope: resume path.
Dependencies: G4I.1, G4.7.
acceptance_criteria: An interaction answered after a process restart resumes the original task with previously completed tasks still completed. Verified against PostgresSaver. An answer to an expired or cancelled interaction is rejected rather than silently applied.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend 147cffe. tests/test_task_checkpoint_resume_postgres.py, 11 tests, opt-in via TEST_POSTGRES_URL.
REAL CHECKPOINTER, NOT A FIXTURE. Uses PooledPostgresCheckpointer/PostgresSaver - what production uses - and the runtime is genuinely destroyed between every phase: pool closed, graph dropped, a NEW checkpointer and NEW graph built against the same thread_id. Anything that survives did so through PostgreSQL. Verified against real data: 57 checkpoint rows, 49 blobs, 90 writes, 16 blobs carrying intent_tasks.
THE TEN-STEP SEQUENCE end to end: plan created; t1-t3 completed; t4 (publish, consequential) blocked on an approval; runtime destroyed; thread resumed; completed tasks still terminal WITH their result_refs; the pending interaction still bound to t4 and t4 still naming it; the answer resuming THAT task; and the three completed tasks asserted untouched afterwards.
STALE-STATE REGRESSION: a stale node copy writing PENDING over a COMPLETED task is refused. DISCRIMINATING - reverting the reducer's terminal guard makes this test fail. For a publish that regression means posting twice. The answered-interaction equivalent is tested too.
INTERACTION SAFETY RE-CHECKED AFTER RESTART, not only in memory: wrong task id, stale answer, duplicate answer, expired approval, rejected approval (skips, does not re-ask) and a clarification answer that cannot grant. All deterministic.
Nothing was wired into main_routing.py; it has zero references to any new module.
close_reason: Pending interaction survives a real checkpoint bound to the same task; the answer resumes that task; six post-restart safety cases deterministic.

title: G4I.4: Approval normalization
description:
Fold the existing approval interrupt into the interaction model WITHOUT weakening it. The current envelope has payload_hash, TTL and tamper detection in main_routing.py and must keep every one of those properties.
Scope: normalization only.
Out of scope: any change to approval semantics.
Dependencies: G4I.1.
acceptance_criteria: Approval remains hash-verified, TTL-bounded and single-use. Existing approval tests pass unchanged. Approval is never substituted by a clarification for a fully specified consequential request.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend ec9e8b3 (code), d1dc70a (tests). app/agent_graph/interaction_runtime.py, 22 tests covering all three lifecycles together.
TRANSPORT-AGNOSTIC: one InteractionAnswer (interaction id, optional option id, optional text, optional decision) serves text, button and voice. answered_by comes from the authenticated caller, never from the payload. No frontend change.
interaction_id resolves EXACTLY ONE pending interaction; an id matching a non-pending one raises StaleAnswer, distinct from UnknownInteraction, because collapsing them would make a duplicate submit indistinguishable from a forged id.
An answer must resume the SAME task_id - binding is verified in both directions before anything mutates. A duplicate answer is DETERMINISTICALLY REJECTED: two clicks on approve must not read as two approvals.
APPROVAL REQUIRES AN EXPLICIT DECISION. approved is tri-state and None is refused rather than guessed, so an empty submit, a timeout or a malformed client cannot read as consent. A clarification answer cannot satisfy an approval, and an approval decision cannot be reinterpreted as clarification data - both directions tested.
Expired and cancelled approvals cannot grant, parametrized. A REFUSED approval SKIPS the task rather than returning it to pending, which would leave it selectable and it would ask again.
CHECKPOINT: a pending interaction round-trips through JSON and the state scanner and still resolves onto the same task afterwards.
close_reason: Approval normalized to an explicit tri-state decision; cannot be satisfied by clarification text; refusal skips rather than re-asks; expired and cancelled cannot grant.

description:
Several valid candidates - drafts, accounts, scheduled posts. Distinct from clarification: the information is not missing, it is plural.
Scope: choice type with stable option ids.
Dependencies: G4I.1.
acceptance_criteria: Options are returned with stable ids resolvable later by id or by natural-language reference. Choice is never emitted when exactly one candidate exists.

title: G4I.2: Clarification interrupt
description:
Suspend on genuinely missing information. Must encode the four uncertainty levels from G2.4 so level 1 proceeds silently and level 2 does useful work before asking.
Worked example: 'Post something about our new AI product tomorrow' - known: post, topic, tomorrow; missing: platform, artifact, exact time. Ask about platform because it materially changes the action; do not ask about tone.
Scope: interrupt type plus the blocking-vs-safe decision.
Dependencies: G4I.1.
acceptance_criteria: A level-1 safe assumption never produces a question. A level-3 blocking ambiguity always does. 'Write a LinkedIn post about agentic AI' produces zero questions; 'Publish this' with three candidate drafts produces exactly one.
