title: G4I.1: InteractionRequest schema
description:
Typed contract: id, type (clarification|choice|approval|connection|authentication), question, reason, required_fields, options, task_id, created_at, status (pending|answered|cancelled).
task_id is mandatory - an interaction that cannot name its suspended task cannot resume it.
Scope: schema only.
Dependencies: G2.4, G4.2.
acceptance_criteria: Schema is typed and validated. An interaction without a resolvable task_id is rejected at construction. Options carry stable ids, not just labels.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend 0cd6af2 (code), 7fd7c75 (tests). app/agent_graph/interactions.py.
Typed and strict: interaction_id, task_id, type, question, reason, required_fields, options, status, created_at, answered_at, answered_by, answer_ref.
task_id IS MANDATORY AT CONSTRUCTION - tested for absence and for whitespace-only. An interaction that cannot name its suspended task cannot resume it.
bind_to_task VERIFIES BOTH DIRECTIONS, each refusal tested independently. One direction is not enough: an interaction naming a task proves nothing if that task has moved on, and a task naming an interaction proves nothing if the interaction belongs elsewhere.
OPTIONS CARRY STABLE IDS, not just labels - labels are user-facing text that changes with wording and translation, so resolving by label would make resolution depend on presentation. Duplicate option_ids rejected; a choice with no options rejected.
APPROVAL IS NOT CLARIFICATION: APPROVAL_TYPES is a frozenset of ONE, disjoint from AMBIGUITY_TYPES, so widening it is a visible edit.  is True only for an APPROVAL that was actually answered - asserted across ALL FIVE types and across pending/expired/cancelled. That is what keeps a timeout from becoming a publish.
merge_interactions refuses to revert an ANSWERED interaction, and answer metadata cannot be forged onto an unanswered one. State passes ensure_safe_graph_state; no field name carries a credential shape; extra fields rejected.
close_reason: InteractionRequest typed and validated; task_id mandatory at construction; options carry stable ids; approval separated from clarification with granted() proven safe across all types and statuses.

title: G4I: Human Interaction Runtime
description:
Makes clarification a first-class capability of the agent rather than an afterthought.

The agent must detect missing information, issue an interrupt, checkpoint, wait for the user - possibly across a reconnect - then resume THE SAME task with previously completed work intact.

FIVE REASONS TO STOP, deliberately distinct:
  clarification    missing information
  choice           several valid candidates
  approval         understood perfectly, needs authorization
  connection       account not connected
  authentication   session/credential problem
Conflating ambiguity with approval is a common agent-design defect. 'Publish this now' with all details known needs approval, never clarification.

CENTRAL UX RULE: ask only when the missing information materially changes the action or makes execution unsafe. A clarifying agent that becomes an interrogation form is a worse product than one that guesses well.

The model may request interaction via an ask_user tool; deterministic policy may also FORCE interaction (for example two eligible accounts). Both paths converge on the same mechanism.

Scope: interaction schema, interrupt types, resume, answer resolution.
Out of scope: the loop itself (G4), frontend cards (G11).
Dependencies: G4 (task runtime must exist to suspend and resume a task).
Rollback: interaction types are additive; approval behaviour must remain byte-compatible until G4I.4 completes.

title: G4.9: Legacy routing compatibility bridge
description:
The flagged seam that lets scenarios move one at a time. Old router remains authoritative until a scenario is migrated.
Scope: bridge plus scenario registry.
Out of scope: deleting anything.
Dependencies: G4.4, G2.5.
acceptance_criteria: A scenario can be moved to the new runtime by configuration alone, with no code change, and moved back the same way. Shadow comparison runs without executing any provider mutation twice.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend 9dd3f16 (code), a17c810 (tests). app/agent_graph/runtime_bridge.py + a 60-line method in thread_service.py. 52 focused tests.

INSERTION POINT: thread_service.command(), immediately AFTER self._graph.invoke and OUTSIDE the lock. The legacy graph has already produced the authoritative result by then, so everything the bridge does is observation. main_routing.py untouched.

ONE FLAG: AGENT_TASK_RUNTIME_MODE = off | shadow | canary | on, default off. A test asserts no second flag exists. canary and on are DECLARED in the contract and REFUSED at resolution (RuntimeModeNotAuthorized) because no gate has authorized serving users from the new runtime; shadow_enabled() returns False for them rather than propagating. An unrecognised value resolves to OFF rather than raising - a typo in an env var must not take the service down.

OFF: 1.02 microseconds per turn, measured over 20,000 iterations. One settings read and a return, before anything is imported or constructed. 1345 SQLite / 1374 PostgreSQL tests pass unchanged.

SHADOW CANNOT EXECUTE - three independent arguments, each sufficient:
1. STRUCTURAL. ShadowExecutor holds no adapter, client, session or DB handle. A test WALKS THE CONSTRUCTED OBJECT GRAPH and asserts vars(executor) == {"observations": []}, so a future adapter added by mistake fails even if nothing calls it. This is not `if shadow: skip` - a conditional is one edit from wrong, a missing object is not.
2. POLICY. shadow_policy_visible hides every consequential prefix, so a mutation never reaches an approval boundary AT ALL - stronger than refusing the approval. A publish plan yields zero observations and no_eligible_capability.
3. IDEMPOTENCY. The shadow COMPUTES the canonical fingerprint (sha256 of capability|platform|account_ref|sorted refs, order-independent, credential-free) and has NO claim path; claim_idempotency exists only to raise. A claimed key could make the legacy operation look already-executed and be SKIPPED.

STATE ISOLATION: shadow::<thread_id>, a PREFIX so a truncated id cannot collide. A test asserts the shadow run does not mutate the plan it was given.

FAILURE ISOLATION: run_shadow cannot raise; _run_shadow_turn wraps everything again. Only the exception CLASS is recorded - a shadow exception message could quote a provider payload and the record is persisted; a test seeds SENTINEL-PAYLOAD in the message and asserts it is absent from the record. Latency is measured around the shadow only and asserted not to overwrite the legacy figure.

COMPARISON RECORD: semantic decisions only - capabilities, task ids, dependencies, platforms, account refs, mutation intent, interaction types, approval requirement, outcome, iterations, attempts, fingerprints, error category, both latencies. No prose comparison. A test asserts no credential marker appears in the serialized record.

IDENTITY: ShadowRequest carries no client-nominatable identity field; a hostile understanding payload with user_id/sub is ignored.

DISCRIMINATION, and one real weakness found by it: the first off-mode test passed even with the mode gate removed, because the service had no planner wired and returned early for the WRONG REASON. It now configures a tripwire planner and sink first, and removing the gate fails three tests. Breaking the fail-closed guard or the policy hiding fails twelve.

ONE EXPECTATION CORRECTED, code was right: connection.status.v1 is a READ - checking connection status is not consequential, only connection.disconnect is.

HARD GATES ALL MET: shadow real provider calls 0; authoritative mutations 0; idempotency claims 0; legacy checkpoint changes 0; duplicate authoritative executions 0; hidden capability executions 0; security gate 18/18.

NOT ENABLED: mode remains off. No canary, no on, no G4.10.
close_reason: Shadow bridge inserted after the legacy invoke; one flag with canary/on failing closed; adapter unreachability proven by object-graph inspection; failure, state and idempotency isolation all tested and discriminating; off-mode overhead 1.02us and every suite unchanged.

title: G4.8: Multi-intent execution evaluation suite
description:
Parametrized over every 2-intent pair and the important 3/4-intent sets, including the four commands from the stabilization brief.
Scope: evaluation suite.
Out of scope: the wider framework (G10).
Dependencies: G4.4.
acceptance_criteria: Every combination terminates. Each required task executes exactly once logically. Node path, tool-call count and duplicate-execution are asserted, not just the final text. The three brief commands that currently loop must pass.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend 49e6dac (loop level), f049af6 (graph level). tests/test_multi_intent_loop_evaluation.py.

PART ONE, loop level: 29 scenarios through run_agent_loop. All nine named scenarios, every 1-4 capability subset as a sequential chain, every 2-3 fan-out shape. Termination 100%.

PART TWO, graph level, added after G4.4 landed: 16 further scenarios through build_task_runtime_graph - the path a real turn takes, with plan-once, durable state, typed outcomes and a checkpointer. Running BOTH matters: the loop rows prove the algorithm terminates, the graph rows prove it still terminates once state must survive a node boundary and a reducer.

EVERY GRAPH SCENARIO IS ENTERED TWICE with the same command and the same intent set, and asserts ZERO re-executions on the second entry. That is precisely the property the old router could not hold, and the reason this suite exists. Matrix: 16/16 rows, planner_calls=1 and re-exec=0 for every one.

HARD INVARIANTS, all holding across both matrices: termination 100%; no task executed more than once successfully; completed tasks never re-executed; hidden capabilities never reach the executor (1 attempt, 0 executions); a rejected approval never executes the consequential capability; dependencies execute in valid order.

Fake model and fake executor throughout. No LLM, no provider, no real mutation reachable.
close_reason: 45 scenarios across loop and graph levels; every graph scenario re-entered with an unchanged intent set records zero re-executions; all hard invariants hold.

title: G4.7: Checkpoint task progress
description:
Task status must survive process death and checkpoint restore. A tool failure must not reset already-completed tasks.
Scope: checkpoint interaction with intent_tasks.
Out of scope: the crash-recovery matrix (G8).
Dependencies: G4.2.
acceptance_criteria: After restart, completed tasks stay completed and the runtime resumes at the correct pending task. Verified against PostgresSaver, not only in-memory - the audit showed the only Postgres checkpoint test is skipped by default.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend 147cffe. tests/test_task_checkpoint_resume_postgres.py, 11 tests, opt-in via TEST_POSTGRES_URL.
REAL CHECKPOINTER, NOT A FIXTURE. Uses PooledPostgresCheckpointer/PostgresSaver - what production uses - and the runtime is genuinely destroyed between every phase: pool closed, graph dropped, a NEW checkpointer and NEW graph built against the same thread_id. Anything that survives did so through PostgreSQL. Verified against real data: 57 checkpoint rows, 49 blobs, 90 writes, 16 blobs carrying intent_tasks.
THE TEN-STEP SEQUENCE end to end: plan created; t1-t3 completed; t4 (publish, consequential) blocked on an approval; runtime destroyed; thread resumed; completed tasks still terminal WITH their result_refs; the pending interaction still bound to t4 and t4 still naming it; the answer resuming THAT task; and the three completed tasks asserted untouched afterwards.
STALE-STATE REGRESSION: a stale node copy writing PENDING over a COMPLETED task is refused. DISCRIMINATING - reverting the reducer's terminal guard makes this test fail. For a publish that regression means posting twice. The answered-interaction equivalent is tested too.
INTERACTION SAFETY RE-CHECKED AFTER RESTART, not only in memory: wrong task id, stale answer, duplicate answer, expired approval, rejected approval (skips, does not re-ask) and a clarification answer that cannot grant. All deterministic.
Nothing was wired into main_routing.py; it has zero references to any new module.
close_reason: Task progress proven across a real PostgreSQL checkpoint with the runtime destroyed between phases; stale-copy regression discriminating; 11 tests.

title: G4.6: Agent reason-tool-observe loop
description:
Implement the G2.2 loop as the central controller. Bounded by the existing GraphBudgets.
Scope: loop node plus budget enforcement.
Out of scope: interaction handling (G4I), command execution (G6).
Dependencies: G4.5, G2.2.
acceptance_criteria: The loop terminates on every evaluation scenario within budget. Tool results re-enter context in a typed form. The loop cannot execute a mutation without passing through policy.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend 30c5129 (code), 5028a1f (tests). app/agent_graph/agent_loop.py, 23 tests.
UNUSED: main_routing.py has ZERO references to agent_loop, capability_exposure, interaction_runtime, task_plan, interactions or task_progress. No provider adapter is reachable - grep for requests/social_action_service/app.platforms/*_service returns 0 in all three new modules. The executor is injected; tests use fakes only.
THE MODEL PROPOSES, CODE TRANSITIONS. ModelDecision can say call/ask/finish. It cannot name a status. Every transition is performed by deterministic code from the EXECUTOR's result. A model claiming FINISH with nothing executed produces SKIPPED, never COMPLETED, with an empty executor call log - asserted directly.
A model naming a capability it was not shown fails at the exposure gate, BEFORE policy and BEFORE the executor.
TWO DISTINCT SAFEGUARDS, asserted not to be subclasses of one another: NoProgress (an iteration changed nothing and did not suspend - a livelock in the loop) and IterationBudgetExhausted (the budget ran out while work was genuinely happening - a defect in the budget). Collapsing them would hide the first inside the second.
Tests cover: single-task completion, multi-task dependencies in order, retry then success, retry exhaustion stopping exactly at max_attempts, non-retryable failures not retrying, clarification and approval suspend/resume onto the same task, rejected approval never reaching the executor, no-progress model response, budget exhaustion, model-cannot-complete-without-evidence, completed tasks never selected twice, and deterministic termination over ten runs.
DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: RUNNING -> SKIPPED was missing from the transition table. Work that started and was then determined unnecessary is a real outcome; it is toward a terminal state so it cannot create a cycle, and the exhaustive 36-pair test covers it automatically.
close_reason: Agent loop implemented as unused tested code with fakes; the model cannot author transitions; NoProgress and IterationBudgetExhausted are distinct; 23 tests.

title: G4.5: Dynamic capability and tool exposure
description:
Do not hand the model every capability every turn. Selection pipeline:
  capability registry -> current context -> connected accounts -> provider support -> permissions/scopes -> relevant subset -> LLM
Registry metadata per capability: id, risk, requires_confirmation, providers, requires_connection, required_scopes, supports_dry_run.
This directly closes an audit finding: post.quote.v1, post.repost.v1 and post.undo_repost.v1 are advertised in the registry with no adapter implementation, and Facebook comment.reply.v1 is advertised without the pages_manage_engagement scope ever being requested.
Scope: registry metadata plus the selection layer.
Out of scope: implementing missing adapter methods (G7).
Dependencies: G4.2, G3.
acceptance_criteria: Disconnected-platform tools are excluded. Provider-unsupported capabilities are excluded. Missing-scope capabilities are excluded. Tool descriptions stay typed and versioned. The model cannot invoke a hidden capability by naming it - proven by a test that attempts exactly that.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend 92ce206 (code), 396f355 (tests). app/agent_graph/capability_exposure.py, 22 tests.
ONE ORDERED PIPELINE: registry -> task relevance -> connection -> platform support -> scope -> policy -> exposed. EVERY STAGE MAY ONLY NARROW, and _narrow() asserts it at RUNTIME rather than only in tests, because the whole security argument rests on it.
EXHAUSTIVE: all 2^3 connected/scoped/policy combinations assert the exposed set is a subset of the catalogue and that exposed and hidden partition it exactly.
Required cases all covered: disconnected provider, missing scope, unsupported adapter platform, policy-hidden, task-irrelevant, and - the sharpest - a policy that says yes to everything still cannot restore what connection removed. Policy is the last stage and the most tempting place to widen.
NAMING IS NOT AUTHORIZATION: require_exposed rejects both a hidden capability and an invented one, before policy is consulted.
EMPTY ELIGIBLE SET IS A DEFINED PATH: NoEligibleCapability carries per-capability reasons and a dominant_reason, so the loop raises a connection interaction instead of crashing. The loop test asserts a tenant with nothing connected BLOCKS rather than throwing.
STAGE ORDER IS FOR DIAGNOSIS, documented and tested: a facebook-only capability with only LinkedIn connected is both disconnected and unsupported; connection owns the reason because it is the one the user can act on.
Registry and policy are INJECTED, so this module imports neither and is testable without a database. Provider adapters unchanged.
close_reason: Deterministic eligibility boundary composing the existing primitives; narrowing enforced at runtime; all required cases plus exhaustive combinations tested.

title: G4.4: Route the graph from the task plan
description:
Drive graph transitions from intent_tasks instead of the intent set, behind the G2.5 feature flag. Old edges remain intact and default-on.
Scope: main_routing.py transitions, flagged.
Out of scope: deleting old routing (G4.10).
Dependencies: G4.3, G2.5.
acceptance_criteria: With the flag off, behaviour is byte-identical and all 443 baseline tests pass. With the flag on, the multi-intent termination suite passes. Both states are covered by CI.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend ebf04dc (code), 5e47706 (tests). app/agent_graph/task_runtime_graph.py, 28 tests.

DIVERGENCE FROM THIS BEAD'S ORIGINAL SCOPE, recorded rather than glossed. It said "main_routing.py transitions, flagged". The session instruction was not to touch that file, and the separate entry point is the better shape anyway: it is what G2.5's strangler design describes - the new runtime BESIDE the old rather than threaded through it - and it makes the old router byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION instead of by a flag nobody can prove is off. The acceptance criterion "with the flag off, behaviour is byte-identical" is met more strongly: there is no flag in main_routing.py to be off.

GRAPH ENTRY POINT: build_task_runtime_graph(deps, checkpointer) -> two nodes, plan then execute. NOT PRODUCTION-SELECTED: an AST test asserts no module in app/ IMPORTS it (checking imports, not mentions - state.py carries an explanatory comment naming it, and a substring guard would have pushed the next person to delete the explanation instead of the coupling). No provider adapter is reachable; planner, model and executor are injected.

ROUTING DERIVES FROM intent_tasks - status, dependencies, attempts, interactions - never from understanding.intents, which may still feed the PLANNER once as a prior. The observable proof: the same command is driven three times with an unchanged intent set and the copywriting task executes exactly once.

PLAN AT MOST ONCE: the plan node returns early when durable state already holds both a goal and tasks. A goal with no tasks is NOT treated as present - resuming into nothing is worse than replanning. DISCRIMINATING: removing that guard fails four tests including both resume scenarios.

TASK IDENTITY: replan() refuses to reuse a task_id for a different capability unless supersede=True, because durable state would otherwise say a publish completed when what completed was a draft. Completed work carries forward when id and capability both match. A source test asserts no graph node calls replan, so implicit replanning is impossible rather than merely discouraged.

EIGHT TYPED OUTCOMES, none collapsed into text: plan_created, work_completed, interaction_required, all_tasks_terminal, no_executable_task, no_progress, iteration_budget_exhausted, no_eligible_capability. all_tasks_terminal is distinct from work_completed because reporting a failure as success is how unfinished work goes unnoticed; no_executable_task is a deadlock, not a completion.

CHECKPOINT RESUME, all eleven steps: the graph OBJECT is discarded and rebuilt around the same checkpointer, then asserts the planner is NOT called, task A is NOT re-executed, the interaction resolves onto its own task, and the resumed turn continues with the schedule ONLY - with t1's result_ref intact afterwards.

MULTI-INTENT: all three previously non-terminating combinations terminate (copywriting+image, websearch+copywriting, connection+copywriting), plus every 2-3 subset sweep and the four-intent worked scenario end to end.
close_reason: Graph-level routing from the durable TaskPlan demonstrated: plan-at-most-once, immutable task ids, typed outcomes, checkpointed resume, and all three previously non-terminating combinations terminating. main_routing.py untouched.

title: G4.3: Pending executable task selector
description:
Replace next_stage() semantics: select the first pending task whose depends_on are all completed. Never re-read the original intent set.
Scope: selector function plus unit tests.
Out of scope: removing old edges (G4.4).
Dependencies: G4.2.
acceptance_criteria: Exhaustive sweep over all 2-intent pairs and the 3/4-intent sets that currently loop shows termination for every combination. Completed tasks are never selected twice.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend 1a23bec (code), a8801a0 (tests). app/agent_graph/task_progress.py.
select_next_task returns the first PENDING task whose depends_on are all COMPLETED. It never reads an intent set. Deterministic by construction - plan order is fixed and the predicate is a pure function of state - which is what makes a shadow comparison meaningful and a failure reproducible.
FIVE EXECUTABILITY CONDITIONS with a closed NotExecutable enum: not pending, dependency incomplete, awaiting interaction, attempts exhausted, capability ineligible. Ordered for diagnosis: a task both terminal and dependency-blocked reports NOT_PENDING because that is the fact that actually stops it. Only COMPLETED unblocks a dependant - skipped and failed do NOT, tested per status.
EXHAUSTIVE SWEEP: every subset of four capabilities (15 combinations, sizes 1-4) with sequential dependencies - the worst case for the old router - run to completion. Each asserts termination within the derived bound, progress on every iteration, and that no task is selected twice.
Capability eligibility is INJECTED so this module imports neither the registry nor policy; selection stays testable without a database and the eligibility decision remains G4.7's.
Also: a completed task is never selected again (five consecutive selections), selection returns None on an empty or finished plan, and 20 repeated calls on the same plan return the same task.
close_reason: Deterministic selector over the task plan; exhaustive sweep of all 1-4 capability subsets terminates with no task selected twice.

title: G4.2: IntentTask state model and reducer
description:
Add intent_tasks to SocialHubGraphState with a merge-by-id reducer. Fields: task_id, intent/capability, status, depends_on, platform, artifact_refs, attempts, required_inputs, blocked_reason, result_ref.
Must preserve ensure_safe_graph_state(): no credentials, no runtime handles, strict JSON. That scanner is one of the strongest controls in the codebase.
Scope: state.py, reducers.py.
Out of scope: routing changes (G4.3, G4.4).
Dependencies: G4.1.
acceptance_criteria: intent_tasks merges by task_id without losing completed status on concurrent node writes. State remains strict JSON and the secret scanner still rejects credential-shaped keys.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend 666e5dc, 1a23bec (state wiring), 7079531 (tests).
intent_tasks added to SocialHubGraphState with merge_intent_tasks; interactions added with merge_interactions. Both are written by NOTHING in the active runtime.
FIELDS: task_id, capability, status, depends_on, platform, account_ref, artifact_refs, attempts, max_attempts, result_ref, error_ref, blocked_reason (closed enum), required_interaction_id.
REDUCER MERGES BY task_id, NOT POSITION - positional merging silently pairs unrelated tasks when two nodes emit different-length lists. A TERMINAL TASK IS IMMUTABLE: tested for every combination of terminal status x attempted regression. That is the checkpoint-safety property as code, because on resume EVERY node holds a stale copy. Idempotent under replay; tolerates empty sides.
TRANSITIONS: LEGAL_TRANSITIONS is the complete relation, exhaustively tested over all 36 status pairs. Every self-transition is illegal - an update that does not move a task is not progress and must not be mistakable for it. Terminal statuses have no outgoing edges.
BLOCKED -> PENDING requires the task's OWN interaction resolved: tested against a wrong id and against nothing at all, the latter being how an unanswered approval would quietly become granted.
ensure_safe_graph_state STILL REJECTS credential-shaped keys - asserted, plus a test that no IntentTask field name carries a credential shape and that extra fields are refused so a payload cannot be smuggled in as an unknown key. result_ref/error_ref/account_ref are references.
close_reason: intent_tasks merges by id without losing completed status; state stays strict JSON and the secret scanner still rejects credential-shaped keys.

title: G4.1: Goal and TaskPlan contracts in code
description:
Implement the G2.3 contract as typed schemas. Goal carries the user objective; TaskPlan carries the ordered task graph.
Scope: app/agent_graph typed schemas.
Out of scope: wiring into the graph (G4.4).
Dependencies: G2.3.
acceptance_criteria: Goal and TaskPlan are typed, validated and round-trip through JSON. Schema rejects a plan with a dependency cycle or an unknown capability id.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend 666e5dc (code), 7079531 (tests). app/agent_graph/task_plan.py.
Goal and TaskPlan are typed, strict (extra=forbid) and round-trip through JSON - asserted by test.
DEPENDENCY CYCLES REJECTED AT CONSTRUCTION via Kahn's algorithm: two-task and three-task cycles both tested. A cycle is unrunnable, so it is refused when the plan is built rather than discovered as a hang at execution. A diamond (two parents, one child) is accepted - not every multi-parent graph is a cycle.
Unknown dependency ids, self-dependency and duplicate task_ids are each rejected with their own test.
CAPABILITY VALIDATION: capability is a constrained string, deliberately NOT validated against the live registry here - that would couple the schema to a database and to G4.7's eligibility decision. Eligibility is injected at selection time (task_progress.CapabilityEligibility) and tested there.
UNUSED BY THE ACTIVE RUNTIME: main_routing.py has zero references.
close_reason: Goal/TaskPlan typed, validated, JSON round-tripping; cycles and unknown dependencies rejected at construction; 85 tests.

title: G2.5: Strangler migration and shadow strategy
description:
Problem: SocialHub already paid for running two runtimes side by side. A third (legacy REST + old routing + new agent loop) would be worse than the original defect.
Define: the feature flag; which scenarios move first; how old and new runtimes are compared without duplicating side effects; the characterization-test safety net; the deletion trigger.
  Current Router
      |- old path (default)
      \- new task runtime (flagged)
Scope: strategy document.
Out of scope: writing the bridge (G4.9).
Dependencies: G2.2, G2.3, G2.4.
acceptance_criteria: A named feature flag, an ordered scenario migration list, a shadow-comparison method that provably cannot double-execute a provider mutation, and an explicit condition under which the old routing may be deleted. main_routing.py is not deleted by this or any G4 bead except G4.10.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): implementation-plan/G2_MIGRATION_STRATEGY.md, root commit 22f6474. No runtime changes.
NAMED FLAG: AGENT_TASK_RUNTIME_MODE = off | shadow | canary | on, default off. ONE setting rather than several, because two flags produce four combinations of which only three are meaningful and the fourth is where a half-migrated state hides.
CANNOT RE-ENABLE INSECURE BEHAVIOUR: it selects between two runtimes that both sit BEHIND the G1 boundaries - identity from the verified JWT, Policy, credential store, error boundary. Nothing removed in G1A-G1D is reachable from any value. A test asserts the enum has exactly four members.
SHADOW CANNOT DOUBLE-EXECUTE, argued three independent ways, each sufficient alone: (1) structural - the shadow Execution Engine is constructed with NO provider adapters bound, so there is no code path to a provider, not merely an instruction not to use one; (2) policy-level - the shadow context is treated as never-approved so consequential capabilities stop at the approval boundary; (3) idempotency-level - both runtimes compute the same key from the same operation fingerprint and effectively-once collapses them. Comparison records DECISIONS (capability, arguments, policy verdict, task graph shape, termination reason), not generated text, which would be noise.
CHARACTERIZATION NET: the 1,010 backend tests are the safety net. A scenario moves only when the new runtime passes the same tests UNCHANGED; a test that must change is a deliberate behaviour change needing its own justification - the standard applied when TestBug016ForgotPassword was found asserting a vulnerability.
TEN ORDERED SCENARIOS, least consequential first, publishing ninth and multi-intent tenth (it has no characterization baseline because the current runtime cannot do it).
DELETION TRIGGER: five conditions including G12 validation and an 18/18 security gate in ON mode. main_routing.py is deleted by G4.10 ONLY.
EXACT G4 SEQUENCE: G4.1 schemas, G4.2 reducer, G4.3 interaction schemas, G4.4 policy integration, G4.5 interaction runtime, G4.6 loop, G4.7 capability selection, G4.8 execution engine, G4.9 bridge and shadow, G4.10 deletion. G4.1-G4.5 add code nothing calls; G4.9 is the first bead that can change a user experience.
close_reason: Named flag, ordered scenario list, shadow safety argued three independent ways, characterization net, five-condition deletion trigger, and the exact G4 sequence.

title: G2.4: Interaction contract
description:
Define why the agent stops. These are NOT the same thing and must not be conflated:
  clarification   - missing information
  choice          - several valid candidates
  approval        - understood perfectly, needs authorization
  connection      - account not connected
  authentication  - session/credential problem
FOUR LEVELS OF UNCERTAINTY, encoded separately:
  1 safe assumption      -> proceed, do not ask
  2 recoverable ambiguity -> do useful work first, ask later
  3 blocking ambiguity   -> must ask before acting
  4 consequential approval -> ask for authorization, not for information
CENTRAL UX RULE, to be enforced as an evaluation invariant and not as prompt wording:
  Ask only when the missing information materially changes the action or makes execution unsafe.
Scope: contract only.
Out of scope: implementation (G4I).
Dependencies: G2.1.
acceptance_criteria: ambiguity and approval are separate types with separate resolution paths. Each of the four uncertainty levels has at least two worked examples, one that must ask and one that must not.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): implementation-plan/G2_STATE_CONTRACTS.md, root commit 22f6474.
InteractionRequest: interaction_id, task_id MANDATORY, type, question, required_fields, options, status, created/answered metadata, answer_ref. task_id is mandatory because an interaction exists to unblock a specific task - without it an answer cannot be routed back and the graph resumes into ambiguity.
FIVE TYPES with separate resolution paths: clarification, choice, approval, connection, authentication.
AMBIGUITY AND APPROVAL ARE DIFFERENT CONCEPTS, stated explicitly. Ambiguity means the system does not know what to do; approval means it knows exactly and may not act unasked. Collapsing them produces BOTH failure modes at once: asking an obvious question, and publishing without consent because the request was unambiguous. Consistent with the recorded interaction-rule memory.
FOUR UNCERTAINTY LEVELS, each with two worked examples - one that must NOT ask and one that must: safe assumption (single connected page; configured timezone), recoverable ambiguity (draft now ask at schedule time; generate image ask caption after), blocking ambiguity (three pages no hint; two drafts no discriminator), consequential approval (publish to a named page; delete a scheduled post or disconnect an account). Level 4 is ORTHOGONAL to 1-3: a request can be perfectly unambiguous and still require approval.
CHECKPOINT BEHAVIOUR: all five required properties mapped to a mechanism, including no credential or OAuth secret in graph state, enforced by the existing sanitizer and the secrets_in_graph_state gate invariant.
DYNAMIC CAPABILITY EXPOSURE: registry -> authenticated context -> connected providers -> provider support/scopes -> policy -> subset -> LLM, where each stage can only NARROW. A model naming a hidden capability is rejected at selection, before Policy is consulted - so an invented or hallucinated name fails early. capabilities/visibility.py already implements narrowing and already records _hidden_reason; G4 wires it to the loop rather than the router.
close_reason: Interaction contract defined; ambiguity and approval separated with separate resolution paths; four uncertainty levels each with must-ask and must-not-ask examples; checkpoint and capability-exposure contracts specified.

title: G2.3: Task-plan contract
description:
Define Goal and TaskPlan. A task carries id, capability, status, depends_on, platform, artifact_refs, attempts, required_inputs, blocked_reason, result_ref.
Statuses: pending, running, completed, blocked, failed, skipped.
Routing selects the first pending task whose dependencies are all completed. This replaces re-reading the original intent set, which is the defect that makes 187/210 four-intent combinations non-terminating.
Scope: typed contract only.
Out of scope: the reducer implementation (G4.2).
Dependencies: G2.1.
acceptance_criteria: A worked example exists for 'analyse last month, write something similar, make an image, schedule Friday morning' showing five tasks with dependency edges. The progress invariant is stated formally: every transition completes new work, requests input, terminates, or fails within bounded retry.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): implementation-plan/G2_STATE_CONTRACTS.md, root commit 22f6474.
IntentTask carries task_id, capability (a registry name, never a free-text agent key), status, depends_on, platform, account_ref, artifact_refs, attempts/max_attempts, result_ref, error_ref, blocked_reason, required_interaction_id.
Statuses pending/running/completed/blocked/failed/skipped with the legal transition graph. NO TRANSITION LEAVES A TERMINAL STATUS - that is what makes 'completed tasks do not re-execute' enforceable rather than hoped for. Selection rule: first pending task whose depends_on are all completed.
result_ref/error_ref/account_ref are REFERENCES, so a provider payload or credential can never reach graph state, checkpoints or memory. The G1 secret boundary applies to the task model, not only to logs.
WORKED EXAMPLE for 'analyse last month, write something similar, make an image, schedule Friday morning': five tasks, four dependency edges, t4 the only consequential one and therefore the only approval source. Contrasted with today's four intents, one flat PlanStep list, and no way to record that t1 finished.
PROGRESS INVARIANT stated formally in the loop contract (G2.2) and referenced here.
close_reason: TaskPlan contract defined with statuses, legal transitions, selection rule and the five-task worked example; progress invariant stated formally.

title: G2.2: Agent-loop contract
description:
Define the reason -> select capability -> tool call -> observe -> update plan -> continue/finish loop, and the boundary it may not cross.
Must specify: loop termination conditions; step and token budgets; how the loop consults the capability registry; what the LLM decides versus what policy decides; how tool results re-enter context; failure and retry behaviour inside the loop.
Scope: contract document + typed schemas.
Out of scope: implementation (G4.6).
Dependencies: G2.1.
acceptance_criteria: The contract states explicitly which decisions belong to the LLM and which are deterministic, and no decision appears in both lists. Loop termination is bounded and provable.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): implementation-plan/G2_AGENT_LOOP_CONTRACT.md, root commit 22f6474.
Ten component boundaries with an explicit 'may never' column. Two DISJOINT decision lists: the LLM decides capability, arguments, ordering preference, wording, and when it believes it is finished; deterministic code decides tenant identity, authentication, capability existence, ownership, provider scope truth, approval requirement, approval validity, idempotency key, transaction and lock boundaries, retry policy, and whether the loop may continue. No item appears in both.
PROGRESS INVARIANT, stated formally: every iteration must terminate a task, raise an interaction and suspend, consume an attempt, or terminate the loop. An iteration doing none of these is detectable by comparing the multiset of (task_id, status, attempts) before and after.
TERMINATION BOUNDED BY CONSTRUCTION: iterations <= tasks x max_attempts + 1, independent of what the model says, with the existing budgets.py ceilings (node steps, LLM calls, tool calls, tokens, recursion) as additional bounds.
Also specifies: tool results re-enter context as TYPED observations never raw provider payloads; a capability the model names but which selection did not expose is rejected before Policy is consulted; retry is gated on failure_recovery's retryable classification and never re-executes a mutation without a fresh idempotency decision.
close_reason: Contract states both decision lists disjointly and proves loop termination is bounded.

title: G2.1: Classify every existing agent and subgraph
description:
Problem: SocialHub advertises 'eleven hidden domain agents'. Most are not reasoning specialists - publishing, scheduling and account retrieval are deterministic jobs wearing an agent costume. Until each is classified, G4 and G7 have no defensible target.
Classify every node/subgraph in app/agent_graph/ into exactly one of:
  A. Real reasoning specialist   (keep as sub-agent)
  B. Deterministic capability    (becomes a tool)
  C. Provider adapter            (becomes an adapter)
  D. Policy/execution code       (becomes policy or execution engine)
  E. Obsolete routing wrapper    (delete after migration)
Expected first pass, to be confirmed against code: Research/Copywriting/Strategy/Creative/Analytics-reasoning = A. Publishing/Scheduling/Analytics-fetch/Connection = B (Connection also needs interaction). Facebook/Instagram/LinkedIn/X = C.
Scope: classification document only.
Out of scope: moving or deleting any code.
Dependencies: G1D.
acceptance_criteria: Every graph node and subgraph in app/agent_graph/ carries exactly one classification with a written justification. No node is left unclassified. The A-list is small and each entry names the reasoning that a tool could not do.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): implementation-plan/G2_AGENT_CLASSIFICATION.md, root commit 22f6474. No runtime code modified.
EVERY module in app/agent_graph/ (57 files, ~21,000 lines) carries exactly one classification with a written justification.
THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDES MOST OF IT: exactly FOUR modules call the LLM gateway - content_graphs, creative_research_graphs, artifact_editing, llm_understanding (llm.py is a 13-line adapter). understanding.py is 512 lines of PURE REGEX with zero LLM calls. platform_agents/subgraphs.py - the four 'platform agents' - makes ZERO LLM calls; it validates an envelope, builds a proposal and shapes a result.
A-LIST IS THREE: content_graphs (novel content judged not verified), creative_research_graphs (open-ended generation over unbounded input), llm_understanding (natural-language ambiguity the regex layer cannot resolve - and it becomes PLANNER INPUT, never a router). artifact_editing calls the LLM but is B: it rewrites under explicit constraints and most of its 265 lines are deterministic string surgery. The test applied throughout: could a well-specified function with the same inputs produce an acceptable output? If yes, B not A.
DEFECT EXPOSED: PlanStep is sequence/agent_key/objective/mutation - NO id, NO status, NO dependencies, NO result - and routing re-reads understanding.intents at TWELVE sites (main_routing.py 176, 432, 597, 704, 710, 772, 830, 918, 922, 926, 1688, 1730). The intent set never shrinks as work completes, so progress is unrepresentable. That is the mechanism behind multi-intent non-termination and why G2.3's TaskPlan is load-bearing.
SURVIVE / DEMOTE / DISAPPEAR recorded per module. ~4,600 lines marked for eventual deletion, 3,759 of them main_routing.py - none deleted before G12 validates the replacement.
close_reason: Every node and subgraph classified with justification; A-list is three and each names reasoning a tool could not do; survive/demote/disappear recorded.

title: Beads SessionStart hook used a nonexistent bd flag
description:
Problem: .claude/settings.json SessionStart ran 'bd prime --hook-json'. bd 1.0.4 rejects --hook-json (exit 1, 'unknown flag'), so no workflow context or memories were ever injected at session start. Combined with the nested-repo discovery failure this meant Beads context was absent in practice, which is the likely reason bd memories was empty while markdown memory files accumulated.
Scope: .claude/settings.json hook command only.
Out of scope: hook framework changes.
Dependencies: none.
Acceptance: bd prime exits 0 and emits workflow context plus memories from all three repository locations.
Tests: manual verification recorded in notes; no automated test exists for host hook wiring.
Runtime evidence: exit=0, workflow=1, memories=1 from socialAgent/, socialbackend/, socialUI/.
Rollback: single-line revert.
Docs: CLAUDE.md beads section.
notes: Fixed in root commit ae200f7. Discovered during B13 verification, not from the audit.
close_reason: Hook command corrected to 'bd prime'; verified exit 0 with memories from all three locations.

title: DECISION: Dolt remote and Beads history visibility
description:
Beads history is currently single-machine. Requires a human decision before any bd dolt push.

- Dolt remote configured: NO (bd dolt remote list -> 'No remotes configured')
