title: G1A-5: Secure media upload against anonymous quota abuse
description:
Problem: POST /media/upload is unauthenticated (media_routes.py:28); content_type is client-supplied and unverified; anyone can burn the Cloudinary quota.
Scope: app/api/v1/media_routes.py.
Out of scope: media pipeline redesign; magic-byte validation may be deferred if it expands scope.
Dependencies: G0.5.
Tests: anonymous upload rejected.
Runtime evidence: route audit row.
Rollback: single-file revert.
Docs: audit section B.2.
acceptance_criteria: Anonymous upload returns 401. Uploads are attributable to an authenticated user.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-26): commit socialbackend 043ad89; tests 416e87b.
- ACCEPTANCE 'anonymous upload returns 401': asserted exactly.
- ACCEPTANCE 'uploads attributable to an authenticated user': upload now targets folder socialhub/u{current_user.id}. Tests assert the folder follows the authenticated user for two different users, and that query params (user_fb_id, user_id) and an X-User-Id header cannot redirect attribution.
- Response inspected for credentials: it already returned only url, public_id, resource_type, width, height. A test now pins that, using a mocked Cloudinary result that DOES include api_key and signature so the assertion is meaningful rather than vacuous.
- HONEST NOTE: test_authenticated_media_upload_succeeds and the response-minimization test also pass against pre-fix code. They are positive/guard controls, not evidence of the vulnerability closure. The discriminating media tests are anonymous rejection and the two attribution tests.
- NOT DONE, deliberately out of scope: content_type is still client-supplied and unverified (no magic-byte check); no per-user rate limit or quota ceiling.
close_reason: Anonymous upload rejected with 401; uploads bound to current_user.id via per-user folder; response minimization pinned.

title: G1A-3: Secure analytics routes
description:
Problem: all 7 analytics routes unauthenticated; four take fb_user_id as the tenant selector; POST /sync is an anonymous trigger.
Scope: app/api/v1/analytics_routes.py.
Out of scope: analytics_service internals; sync scheduling.
Dependencies: G0.5.
Tests: cross-tenant read denied for overview/posts/growth/best-times/sync-logs/sync-status.
Runtime evidence: route audit rows.
Rollback: single-file revert.
Docs: audit section B.2.
acceptance_criteria: fb_user_id no longer selects the tenant. Cross-tenant analytics reads return 404. POST /analytics/sync requires authentication.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-26): commit socialbackend 1940389; tests 416e87b.
- ACCEPTANCE 'fb_user_id no longer selects the tenant': asserted as response EQUALITY with and without the victim identifier on all 5 reads. The weaker 'victim data absent' form passed against pre-fix code for 4 of 5 endpoints because the seeded fixture did not surface in those response shapes; strengthening it moved discrimination from 21/28 to 24/28.
- ACCEPTANCE 'cross-tenant analytics reads refused': /sync-status cross-tenant probe returns 404; /sync-logs scoped to caller (previously returned EVERY tenant's logs when fb_user_id was omitted).
- ACCEPTANCE 'POST /analytics/sync requires authentication': exceeded. It performs ALL-TENANT work, so it now sits behind a new internal/admin boundary (app/api/v1/admin_auth.py). Anonymous -> 401; ordinary authenticated tenant -> 403 with a test proving no SyncLog row is created.
- Justification for gating rather than tenant-scoping: apiManager declares triggerAnalyticsSync/getSyncLogs/getSyncStatus but NO component in socialUI/app or lib/features calls them - verified. So there is no user-facing purpose to preserve.
- require_admin_user reuses AGENT_DEBUG_ADMIN_EMAILS (no new config key), fails closed on an empty allowlist, and does NOT honour the '*' wildcard the agent debug gate accepts.
- PRESERVED: the daily APScheduler job still calls global sync_all_metrics; analytics_service sync_all_* remain intentionally cross-tenant. A test asserts app.main.start_scheduler still references sync_all_metrics.
close_reason: All acceptance criteria met with discriminating tests; all-tenant sync moved behind an internal/admin boundary; global background sync preserved and asserted.

title: G9: Scheduler migration
description:
Problem: execute_scheduled_posts (scheduled_post_routes.py:535) selects due rows with no lock, no claim, no fingerprint, using naive datetime.utcnow(); run_autopilot_cycle is identical; AsyncIOScheduler is in-process with no jobstore or leader election. ExactlyOnceSchedulingExecutor exists and is tested but no production entrypoint calls it.
Scope: durable claim-based worker calling canonical commands.
Out of scope: choosing infrastructure before deployment topology is known.
Dependencies: G8.
Acceptance: concurrent workers against Postgres produce no duplicate logical execution.
Tests required: real concurrent-worker test against Postgres.
Runtime evidence: scheduler call graph terminates in a canonical command.
Rollback: feature-flagged cutover.
Documentation impact: production skill.
BLOCKED ON INFORMATION: deployment topology (containers x workers) is UNKNOWN.
notes: INPUT FROM G1A-2 (2026-08-26): the execution loop is now run_due_scheduled_posts(db) in app/api/v1/scheduled_post_routes.py, called by app.main.run_scheduled_posts_job. It is no longer HTTP-reachable, which removes the anonymous-trigger amplifier but does NOT address the underlying defects G9 owns: no row lock, no claim, no request fingerprint, naive datetime.utcnow(), and an in-process AsyncIOScheduler with no jobstore or leader election. G9 should migrate this exact function to a durable claim-based worker.

title: G8: Durable mutation execution
description:
Problem: no durable record of external mutations; no reconciliation for ambiguous outcomes.
Scope: operation_id, request_fingerprint, user_id, provider, account_id, capability, status, attempt_count, provider_resource_id, timestamps, last_error, reconciliation_status. Statuses: pending/executing/succeeded/failed_retryable/failed_terminal/outcome_unknown/cancelled.
Out of scope: claiming exactly-once delivery — no provider offers idempotency keys for post creation; use effectively-once mutation semantics.
Dependencies: G6.
Acceptance: post-transmission timeout moves to outcome_unknown and reconciles by provider read, never blind retry.
Tests required: crash-recovery matrix (Phase 8 scenarios) against Postgres.
Runtime evidence: durable rows for every external mutation.
Rollback: additive table.
Documentation impact: target architecture execution layer.

title: G6: Canonical application commands
description:
Problem: publishing/scheduling/engagement/analytics have per-caller implementations.
Scope: implement the G2 command set; migrate REST, scheduler, autopilot and graph to call only these.
Out of scope: frontend migration (G11).
Dependencies: G2.
Acceptance: no consequential mutation bypasses a canonical command; verified by call-graph trace.
Tests required: integration per command; caller-parity tests.
Runtime evidence: OLD caller -> NEW implementation proven by trace or integration test.
Rollback: legacy paths retained until G13.
Documentation impact: target architecture.

title: G4: Agent Loop and Task Runtime
description:
Replaces brittle intent-set routing with a task-driven agent loop. This is the runtime half of the G2 pivot.

EVIDENCE THIS IS NEEDED (machine-verified in G0): next_stage() receives 'completed' as a per-edge literal, never accumulated state. 20/45 two-intent, 89/120 three-intent and 187/210 four-intent combinations never terminate; they die on GraphBudgetExceeded at max_node_steps=32. Separately the keyword table misses 'performing' while holding 'perform' and 'performed', silently dropping an analytics task - a defect no loop fix addresses, and a demonstration of why manually maintained intent tables must not be the router.

TARGET: LangGraph stays, but becomes the durable harness - lifecycle, state, persistence, boundaries, interrupts, task progress, failure handling. The model does language understanding, planning, tool selection and adaptation. Deterministic code keeps security, policy and execution. The graph gets THINNER, not larger.

Scope: task runtime, agent loop, dynamic tool exposure, checkpointed progress, and a flagged bridge from the current router.
Out of scope: canonical commands (G6), adapters (G7), interaction runtime (G4I).
Dependencies: G2.

HARD CONSTRAINT: do NOT delete main_routing.py and rebuild. 443 passing tests are the characterization net. Only G4.10 removes old routing, and only after shadow validation.

title: G3: Provider and OAuth platform contracts
description:
Problem: Meta on v22.0 (current v26.0); LinkedIn on unversioned /v2/ugcPosts with no Linkedin-Version header (Posts API replaces ugcPosts; 202508 sunset 2026-08-17); X on api.twitter.com (current api.x.com); scope gaps make advertised capabilities impossible.
Scope: version/host modernization, scope review, capability matrix as executable contract.
Out of scope: adapter refactor (G7).
Dependencies: G1D (may run parallel to G2).
Acceptance: no advertised capability the account tier cannot perform; matrix rows all have contract tests.
Tests required: mocked provider contract suite.
Runtime evidence: sandbox call per provider where test accounts permit.
Rollback: version pin revert.
Documentation impact: PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md.

title: G2: Conversational Agent Runtime Architecture
description:
ARCHITECTURAL PIVOT POINT. This is not 'refactor LangGraph'. It formally establishes the target runtime and the migration strategy for reaching it.

GOVERNING PRINCIPLE: intent recognition is NOT the central controller. The agent loop is. The deterministic understanding layer becomes internal planning input, never the router.

TARGET:
  USER (text/voice/UI)
    -> Conversation Agent (one visible agent)
    -> Task Planner  -> IntentTask[]
    -> Agent Loop: reason -> tool -> observe -> update -> repeat
         branches: Need Tool? / Need User? / Complete?
         Need User? -> Interaction Manager -> LangGraph interrupt
    -> Capability Registry -> Policy Engine -> Command Layer
    -> Execution Engine -> Provider Adapters

THREE BRAINS, strictly separated:
  LLM        : what does the user want, what next, which tool, is the task satisfied
  POLICY     : ownership, connection, provider support, scopes, approval, rate limits - the LLM never overrides this
  EXECUTION  : operation_id, idempotency, retry, locking, timeout, reconciliation, audit

ONE VISIBLE AGENT, many hidden capabilities. The 'eleven domain agents' must stop being a user-facing concept. Architecture must not leak through the product surface.

Scope: contracts, classification and migration strategy. Documents and typed schemas only.
Out of scope: ALL implementation - that is G4, G4I, G6, G7.

Dependencies: G1D (security boundary stable first).

Acceptance: every existing agent/subgraph classified; agent-loop, task-plan and interaction contracts written and typed; strangler migration strategy documented with a feature flag and shadow plan.
Tests required: contract/schema validation tests only.
Runtime evidence: n/a - contract gate.
Rollback: documents are additive; no runtime change.
Documentation impact: docs/SOCIALHUB_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md (new).

HARD CONSTRAINT - NO REWRITE: 443 passing backend tests are an asset. main_routing.py must NOT be deleted and rebuilt in one shot. Strangler migration only. The failure mode to avoid is three runtimes: legacy REST + old LangGraph routing + new agent loop.
notes:
CLOSURE (2026-08-27). All five children closed with individual evidence; every acceptance criterion satisfied. Root commit 22f6474.

EVIDENCE - four implementation-plan documents:
  implementation-plan/G2_AGENT_CLASSIFICATION.md   (G2.1) every module classified, A-list of three
  implementation-plan/G2_AGENT_LOOP_CONTRACT.md    (G2.2) disjoint decision lists, bounded termination
  implementation-plan/G2_STATE_CONTRACTS.md        (G2.3, G2.4) TaskPlan, InteractionRequest, uncertainty levels, checkpoint and capability-exposure contracts
  implementation-plan/G2_MIGRATION_STRATEGY.md     (G2.5) AGENT_TASK_RUNTIME_MODE, shadow safety, ordered scenarios, deletion trigger, exact G4 sequence

THE TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT SHAPED IT:
1. Exactly FOUR modules in app/agent_graph/ call the LLM gateway. understanding.py is 512 lines of pure regex; platform_agents/subgraphs.py - the four 'platform agents' - makes zero LLM calls. The product advertises eleven hidden domain agents; three modules reason.
2. PlanStep has NO status field and routing re-reads understanding.intents at twelve sites, so the intent set never shrinks as work completes and progress is unrepresentable. That is the mechanism behind multi-intent non-termination, and why TaskPlan is load-bearing rather than a modelling nicety.

GOVERNING INVARIANT ESTABLISHED: the LLM decides WHAT, policy decides WHETHER, execution decides HOW - with two disjoint decision lists and no item in both.

NO RUNTIME CODE WAS MODIFIED IN G2. main_routing.py untouched.

This epic remains the standing architectural reference for G4 and G4I. Closing it records that the contracts are agreed, not that they are implemented - implementation is G4.
close_reason: All five children closed with evidence; contracts recorded in four implementation-plan documents; architecture accepted by the user.

title: G1C: Client and transport hardening
description:
Problem: next.config.ts proxies to hardcoded http://3.109.208.88:8000 in plaintext; two competing browser auth mechanisms (Clerk + localStorage app_auth_token).
Scope: env-driven backend origin; establish Clerk as sole authoritative session where investigation confirms it is safe.
Out of scope: DNS/deployment/infrastructure changes.
Dependencies: G1A.
Acceptance: no hardcoded production origin in source; single documented session mechanism; actual network path documented before change.
Tests required: frontend auth session regression; build+lint.
Runtime evidence: confirmed TLS termination path.
Rollback: config revert.
Documentation impact: deployment/transport section.
BLOCKED ON INFORMATION: whether HTTPS is terminated upstream is currently UNKNOWN.

title: Gate L cleanup: retire legacy PLATFORM_TOOL_SPECS and per-platform schemas
description: Remove or collapse legacy per-platform tool specs from platform_agents/tools.py after canonical capability tools replace the old 13 platform-specific shell tools. Target legacy surface includes PLATFORM_TOOL_SPECS, platform_tool_specs, old per-platform args schemas, and build_platform_structured_tools/build_platform_tool_node if no longer needed.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical registry-backed tools replace facebook.*, instagram.*, linkedin.*, and x.* legacy tool specs or keep only explicit compatibility aliases. No duplicated independent schema definitions remain. Tests cover canonical publish/schedule/comment/caption/draft behavior, legacy alias mapping where retained, and import audit proves dead classes/functions are removed.

title: Gate L cleanup: migrate routing constants to capability registry
description: Remove the old hardcoded routing/task contract from platform_agents once the capability registry is the source of truth. Target legacy surface includes PLATFORM_TASKS in platform_agents/schemas.py and direct task-to-capability assumptions in main routing.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime route decisions use registry-backed capability names and support checks. PLATFORM_TASKS is deleted or replaced by a generated compatibility view with no independent source of truth. Tests prove Main Agent still sees no platform tool schemas, platform agents receive only selected candidate tools, and unsupported platform-operation pairs fail before platform-agent execution.
close_reason: Migrated PLATFORM_TASKS to a registry-generated compatibility view, added canonical capability metadata on platform route decisions, expanded legacy alias coverage for all current platform shell tasks, and added regression tests proving aliases support their platforms and platform tasks no longer have an independent allow-list.

title: G13 (was Gate L cleanup): retire legacy platform-agent runtime
description: Track removal of legacy platform-agent runtime files and duplicated tool definitions after the capability registry, dynamic visibility selector, central policy layer, and canonical capability implementations replace them. This exists because socialhub-iw5.1 added the new authoritative capability contract while current production code still depends on legacy platform_agents modules.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy platform-agent code is removed or reduced to thin compatibility shims only after registry-backed routing, visibility, confirmation/idempotency policy, and canonical capability tools are live. Cleanup must include import audits, test migration, deletion of dead files where safe, and proof that Main Agent/platform-agent behavior still passes regression tests.

title: Gate L: Central mutation confirmation and idempotency policy
description: Implement a central deterministic mutation policy layer for platform capabilities. Platform agents propose mutations first; schema validation, reference resolution, capability support validation, permission checks, confirmation policy, idempotency preparation, provider execution, and result normalization happen in deterministic runtime nodes/policy services. Confirmation must not depend on free-form agent reasoning inside individual tools.
acceptance_criteria: Policy table covers artifact.delete/restore, post.publish/schedule/reschedule/cancel, comment.reply, post.repost/quote, retry, and read-only operations with always/never/conditional confirmation rules. Tests verify proposal-before-execution flow, always/never/conditional confirmation behavior, capability support validation, permission checks, idempotency keys, stale payload hash detection, timeout retry safety, duplicate publish prevention, and central policy reuse across platforms.
close_reason: Implemented registry-native central mutation policy with confirmation/idempotency table, proposal-before-execution validation, support/permission/connection gates, stale hash checks, duplicate-operation prevention, approval resume verification, and regression tests.

title: Gate L: Capability registry and dynamic tool visibility policy
description: Create a capability registry that separates LLM-callable tools from internal service methods, graph nodes, policy gates, observability events, and evaluators. Define deterministic dynamic visibility rules from Main Agent structured understanding, not from another autonomous tool-selection agent, so each platform agent receives only the small tool group required for the current task.
acceptance_criteria: Registry records capability type, owner, platform scope, risk, schemas, platform support matrix, visibility rules, implementation adapter, and status. Dynamic selection is the intersection of tools required by intent, tools supported by platform, tools allowed for this user, and tools available for the current connection. Tests prove Main Agent still cannot see platform tool schemas; platform agents receive minimal task-specific tool groups; retrieval does not expose list tools unless needed; image/media/analytics tools are granted only when needed; debug/evaluation/observability capabilities are never visible to normal agents.
close_reason: Implemented registry-backed dynamic visibility selector, platform-agent schema snapshots, runtime visibility metadata, and tests proving minimal tool exposure, permission/connection filtering, and internal capability hiding.

title: Gate L capabilities: multi-platform adaptation and routing nodes
description: Classify multi-platform commands such as post this on LinkedIn and X, adapt this caption for all platforms, or no use LinkedIn instead. Routing helpers like task split, batch plan, and route correction should generally be structured Main Agent output, deterministic LangGraph nodes, or state transitions rather than ordinary LLM tools.
acceptance_criteria: Plan and implementation keep orchestration outside the business-tool surface. Main Agent emits structured multi-platform routes or corrections; LangGraph dispatches platform agents through Send/branches or equivalent deterministic flow. Tests cover multi-platform split, correction from one platform to another, unsupported combo, platform-specific constraints, and confirmation boundaries.

title: Gate L capabilities: engagement and comment workflows
description: Classify and implement engagement capabilities such as comment reply, comment list, quote, repost, and undo repost. Comment read/list can be consolidated as comment.list.v1; mutations may be comment.reply.v1, post.quote.v1, post.repost.v1, and post.undo_repost.v1 with platform arguments where safe.
acceptance_criteria: Engagement mutations require central confirmation and connected-account validation. Read tools expose safe comment/post metadata only. Tests cover comment id/latest-comment resolution, reply confirmation, unsupported platform behavior, wrong-account denial, and no token/raw provider leakage.

title: Gate L capabilities: publish-now and schedule lifecycle
description: Classify and implement publish/schedule/reschedule/cancel capabilities across platforms. Prefer consolidated tools such as post.publish.v1, post.schedule.v1, post.reschedule.v1, and post.cancel_schedule.v1 with platform arguments, while keeping provider-specific publish/schedule methods internal. Existing platform-specific v1 tools must be mapped or wrapped without breaking current confirmations.
acceptance_criteria: Publishing, scheduling, rescheduling, and cancellation use central policy confirmation and exactly-once idempotency. Capabilities validate connected account, media requirements, timezone/date conflicts, artifact hash stability, and ownership. Tests cover publish now, schedule later, invalid time, disconnected account, stale draft, cancel/reschedule, provider failure, and replay.
close_reason: Implemented canonical post publish/schedule lifecycle approvals, schedule cancel/reschedule execution, central policy confirmation/idempotency, and regression coverage.

title: Gate L capabilities: draft and caption lifecycle management
description: Classify and implement draft/caption lifecycle capabilities for delete, duplicate, restore, revise-from-history, and variant creation. Prefer consolidated tools such as artifact.delete.v1, artifact.duplicate.v1, and artifact.restore.v1 with constrained platform/artifact_type arguments instead of separate per-platform tools unless the matrix proves separation is safer.
acceptance_criteria: Deletion, restore, and overwrite mutations go through central confirmation policy. Tools update backend-owned artifact state only after ownership checks. Tests cover latest target resolution, invalid platform/artifact combinations, missing state, confirmation requirement, idempotency, and no frontend-owned context trust.
close_reason: Implemented draft/caption artifact lifecycle capabilities with central confirmation, backend-owned state mutation, ownership checks, routing, and regression coverage.

title: Gate L capabilities: content retrieval and latest-reference resolution
description: Classify and implement retrieval/latest-reference capabilities for queries like show my latest caption/post/draft, list recent posts, get comments, and use the latest one. Prefer consolidated tools such as content.get.v1, content.list.v1, comment.list.v1, and schedule.get.v1 where schemas can safely constrain platform/artifact type. Provider-specific get/list methods should remain internal adapters unless the matrix proves they need LLM visibility.
acceptance_criteria: Capabilities are read-only, return safe metadata/content previews, enforce verified ownership/account scope, support latest/reference resolution, and never expose provider tokens/raw responses. Platform agents receive only the retrieval tools needed for the current task. Tests cover latest reference, missing state, wrong platform denial, schema constraints, and safe projections.
close_reason: Implemented canonical read-only retrieval capabilities for content.get/content.list/comment.list/schedule.get with pydantic schemas, safe graph-state projection, latest/reference resolution, platform/account/user scope filtering, connection-gated comments, graph-level read-only retrieval routing, and regression tests.

title: Gate L: Capability matrix, granularity review, and routing map
description: Create the authoritative capability matrix for real user-query coverage. The goal is not to finalize 54 separate LLM tool names; it is to classify capabilities, consolidate duplicates, and determine the minimum LLM-callable tool surface. The matrix must decide whether each operation is an LLM-callable tool, internal service operation, deterministic graph node, policy gate, observability event, API endpoint, or evaluation function.
acceptance_criteria: Deliverables: 1) capability matrix, 2) platform support matrix, 3) canonical input/output schemas, 4) confirmation and idempotency policy matrix, 5) deterministic dynamic visibility rules, 6) provider adapter mapping, 7) duplicate/consolidation decisions, 8) evaluation-case mapping, 9) deprecation plan for overlapping existing tools, and 10) final count of model-facing tools. Matrix must include capability ID, capability type, domain, supported platforms, supported artifact types, mutation type, confirmation policy, idempotency requirement, required permissions, required/resolvable arguments, provider adapters, agent visibility, visibility conditions, output schema, failure modes, evaluation cases, status, and why this must be LLM-callable. Given any supported command category, the system can determine the responsible agent, minimum visible tool set, expected schema, permissions, confirmation behavior, idempotency behavior, provider adapter, success output, normalized failures, and regression test cases.
notes: Architectural correction accepted: Gate L must avoid exposing every operation as an LLM tool. The capability matrix must classify each item as llm_tool, internal_service_method, deterministic_graph_node, policy_gate, observability_event, api_endpoint, or evaluation_function. Unified LLM tools must include deterministic capability-support validation so unsupported platform/operation combinations return structured errors instead of relying on LLM inference.
close_reason: Implemented capability registry contract, deterministic routing map, support matrix, policy metadata, and regression tests.

title: G7 (was Gate L): Platform capability expansion and provider adapters
description: Expand SocialHub platform-agent capability coverage for real user-query categories without exposing every internal operation as an LLM-callable tool. Gate L must classify each operation as one of: LLM-callable tool, internal provider/service method, deterministic LangGraph node, policy gate, observability event, API endpoint, or evaluation function. Main Agent still sees only route schemas; platform agents receive a minimal dynamic tool surface for the current task; provider-specific operations remain internal adapters behind typed service boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads produce a capability matrix and implementation plan that consolidates duplicates, identifies the minimum safe LLM-callable tool surface, keeps provider adapters separate, defines deterministic routing/state operations outside the tool surface, centralizes confirmation/idempotency policy, and maps every capability to evaluation cases.
notes:
SCOPE NOTE (2026-08-26): G7 now also owns the capability metadata that G4.5 consumes for dynamic tool exposure - id, risk, requires_confirmation, providers, requires_connection, required_scopes, supports_dry_run.
Adapters must implement get_capabilities() and validate_connection() so exposure can be computed rather than asserted. Directly closes the audit finding that post.quote.v1, post.repost.v1 and post.undo_repost.v1 are advertised with no adapter implementation, and that Facebook comment.reply.v1 is advertised while pages_manage_engagement is never requested.
PRINCIPLE: deterministic provider work is a tool or an adapter, never a sub-agent.

title: Gate K internal: evaluation run, report, and comparison APIs
description: Add evaluation execution APIs/scripts for starting dataset runs, checking status, retrieving reports, comparing experiments, and surfacing regressions. These are evaluation-runner capabilities, not ordinary Main Agent/platform-agent tools.
acceptance_criteria: Capabilities can start dry-run evaluations without external provider side effects, poll status, retrieve per-case results, compare baseline versus candidate, and produce regression reports. Tests verify deterministic evaluators, forbidden tool checks, confirmation policy checks, failure reporting, idempotent run handling, and non-visibility to normal agents.

title: Gate K internal: evaluation dataset management APIs
description: Add developer/admin-only evaluation dataset management APIs/scripts, not LLM-callable tools. Use cases: create regression cases from planned scenarios or production traces, tag by platform/capability, and version expected behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Capabilities support versioned cases with command, initial safe state, expected route/platform/tool trajectory/state assertions/forbidden tools/confirmation policy/tags. Access is developer/admin only. Tests cover validation, import/export, promotion from redacted trace, duplicate detection, deterministic expected-behavior schema, and non-visibility to normal agents.

title: Gate K internal: LLM call, tool call, and validation inspection APIs
description: Add protected internal APIs/capabilities for inspecting LLM/tool-call events and validation failures. These support debugging model request/response metadata, selected tool, generated arguments, Pydantic validation errors, retries, and repaired arguments, without becoming part of the normal agent tool surface.
acceptance_criteria: Capabilities expose redacted request/response metadata, generated arguments, validation errors, retry count, repair source, tool execution result status, latency, token/cost fields, and source attribution. Tests cover validation failures, repaired arguments, forbidden-key redaction, no auth/provider/session leakage, and non-visibility to normal agents.

title: Gate K internal: schema and visible-tool snapshot APIs
description: Add protected internal APIs/capabilities for observing which schema/version and tool list were supplied to the model and what structured output instance was produced. These support debugging/evaluation and must not be ordinary agent tools.
acceptance_criteria: Capabilities return prompt_version, schema_version, agent_version, model, available tool names, safe JSON schema references, and generated structured output/tool arguments for a trace/span. Tests verify schema/output separation, per-agent tool visibility, redaction, and non-visibility to normal agents.

title: Gate K internal: trace inspection and timeline retrieval APIs
description: Add protected trace-read APIs/capabilities for inspecting agent executions. These are internal debug endpoints/services, not LLM-callable tools. Use cases: see every node executed, execution order, inputs/outputs by span, retries, latency, status, and final checkpoint summary for one command or a filtered list of commands.
acceptance_criteria: Strict schemas exist for trace get/list and span timeline retrieval. Capabilities enforce verified user/thread ownership plus debug/admin policy, return only redacted span data, support filtering by thread/platform/task/status/time range, and include tests for ownership denial, disabled debug denial, pagination, ordering, redaction, and non-visibility to normal agents.

title: Gate K: Internal observability/evaluation capabilities
description: Define and implement protected internal capabilities needed by Gate K use cases. These are not normal user-facing LLM tools and must not be visible to Main Agent or platform agents during ordinary social workflows. They are debug APIs, trace instrumentation, evaluation scripts, admin UI actions, metric jobs, database queries, and LangSmith/evaluator integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads define protected internal API/evaluation/observability capabilities for every Gate K use case. Each capability has a strict request/response schema, authorization policy, redaction behavior, tests, and a clear API/UI/evaluator consumer. Acceptance explicitly proves these capabilities are not supplied to normal Main Agent or platform-agent LLM tool surfaces.

title: Gate K: Deterministic evaluator runner for agent behavior
description: Build a repeatable evaluation runner that executes the versioned command dataset against the current agent graph and scores deterministic behavior: route correctness, platform correctness, allowed tool visibility, selected tool/tool trajectory, argument validation, forbidden tool avoidance, confirmation policy, state changes, and failure handling.
acceptance_criteria: Runner produces per-case and aggregate reports comparing baseline versus candidate behavior. Deterministic evaluators cover route, platform, tool sequence, Pydantic argument validity, forbidden tools, confirmation requirement, and final state assertions. It can run locally/CI without external social provider calls.

title: Gate K: Versioned command evaluation dataset
description: Create a versioned evaluation dataset for SocialHub commands across Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X, and shared/common capabilities. Each case should include command, initial safe state, expected route/platform/tool trajectory/state changes/prohibited tools/confirmation policy, tags, and notes for subjective content quality.
acceptance_criteria: Dataset contains representative cases for create, edit, context reference, retrieve, schedule, delete, reply/comment, multi-platform, ambiguous, missing state, unauthorized, provider failure, safety confirmation, conflict, memory reference, and correction flows. Cases are grouped by platform/capability and use deterministic expected behavior rather than exact final wording.

title: Gate K: Protected agent debug endpoint
description: Add an authenticated internal endpoint for inspecting one thread command/run. It should expose the safe checkpoint fields plus trace timeline data, including Main Agent understanding, selected route, platform_agent_route, platform_agent_result, visible schema/tool versions, structured output/tool arguments, validation errors, and final state summaries.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/v1/agent/threads/{thread_id}/debug is protected by ownership, debug feature flag, and developer/admin authorization policy. Response is redacted, excludes artifact_index secrets/raw provider data, and includes final_state plus ordered events when available. Tests cover owner access, non-owner denial, disabled flag denial, and redaction.

title: Gate K: Persist agent trace and audit events
description: Implement backend persistence for critical business-level observability events independent of any vendor. Store agent runs, ordered steps/spans, LLM call metadata, visible tool schemas/tool names, selected tool calls, generated arguments, validation failures, retry/repair attempts, tool results, latency, and token/cost metadata using the sanitizer contract.
acceptance_criteria: Database models/migrations and service APIs persist redacted agent_run, agent_step, llm_call, tool_invocation, and validation_result records scoped to verified user/thread. Tests verify ordering, ownership filtering, redaction, and no credential/runtime leakage. Existing thread execution remains functional if tracing persistence is disabled or unavailable.

title: Gate K: Observability event contract, versions, and sanitizer
description: Define the canonical trace/span/event schema for agent execution. Capture schema version supplied to the model, structured output instance/tool arguments produced by the model, prompt/model/agent versions, safe state summaries, source attribution, latency, token/cost fields, and validation/retry metadata. Add a sanitizer contract that strips tokens, cookies, secrets, DB sessions, service clients, authorization headers, and raw provider responses before persistence or display.
acceptance_criteria: A documented Pydantic contract exists for agent_run, agent_span, llm_call, tool_invocation, validation_result, and safe state summaries. Unit tests prove sanitizer redacts credential-shaped keys and runtime objects. Contract includes graph_version, agent_version, prompt_version, schema_version, trace_id, span_id, thread_id, user scope, node name, and source classification.

title: G10 (was Gate K): Agent observability and evaluation framework
description: Build a complete observability and evaluation layer for SocialHub agents. This expands beyond checkpoint inspection by recording schema/tool visibility, structured output instances, node execution order, LLM/tool spans, validation failures, retries, latency, token/cost metadata, and repeatable evaluation datasets. Implementation must preserve user isolation and redact secrets/tokens/session objects.
acceptance_criteria: Child beads cover observability contract/redaction, persistent audit traces, protected debug endpoint, LangSmith integration, versioned command datasets, deterministic evaluators, internal debug drawer, and production metrics/review queue. No code implementation starts until this plan is reviewed.
notes:
SCOPE EXPANSION (2026-08-26): G10 now also covers interaction-quality measurement - see child G10.C. The rule 'ask only when the missing information materially changes the action or makes execution unsafe' must be enforced as an evaluation invariant rather than prompt wording.
Also carried forward from the G0 audit: the dataset is 24 cases against a 300 target with no dev/regression/holdout split, and tests/conftest.py force-disables LANGGRAPH_LLM_UNDERSTANDING_ENABLED for every test while production defaults it to True - so the hybrid understanding path is untested end to end.

title: Gate I: Facebook platform agent connect/publish flow end-to-end
description:
## Context
Platform-agent Gates A-H are complete. The next product step is to move beyond platform-agent shell/proposal behavior and make Facebook usable end-to-end from the Main Agent UI.

## Actual Task
Implement and verify the Facebook platform-agent connect/publish flow end-to-end: frontend should render backend connection_actions, the Connect Facebook action should start the OAuth handoff, connected Facebook state should feed Main Agent context, and publishing a selected Facebook draft should go through confirmation and the existing exactly-once publish executor.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Frontend renders connection_actions from agent messages/artifacts as a clear Connect Facebook action.
- Clicking Connect Facebook starts the existing safe Facebook OAuth login-url flow without exposing tokens/secrets.
- After Facebook is connected, Main Agent connection context reflects owned pages/accounts for the user.
- Facebook create/publish command routes through the hidden Facebook platform agent and maps to publish.execute.v1 confirmation.
- Confirmed publish executes through existing ownership/idempotency checks.
- Backend focused tests, frontend lint/build/tests as applicable, production deployment, and smoke checks pass.
close_reason: Completed Gate I: cleaned active Beads backlog to remove experimental orchestrated-agents workflow tasks, updated the platform-agent plan to Gates A-H closed/Gate I active, verified frontend backend-owned connection_actions rendering with Facebook coverage, and completed the Facebook platform-agent publish confirmation/resume path. Backend now returns Facebook post published after confirmed publish, records execution_result, and does not emit reconnect cards after successful publish. Verification: focused backend tests 54 passed; full backend pytest 235 passed, 1 skipped; frontend lint passed; frontend build passed; frontend jest 21 passed; backend commit f807c55 deployed as socialhub-backend:facebook-flow-f807c55; frontend commit d21b988 pushed to origin/main; production /health passed; production smoke returned Connect Facebook action and Facebook publish confirmation/resume with publish.execute.v1.

title: Gate H: Route Facebook connect intent to connection handoff
description:
## Context
After platform-agent Gates A-G, frontend testing showed commands like 'letsconnect with facebook' still produced the generic Main Agent greeting instead of initiating the Facebook connection flow. The user expects Main Agent to route connect requests to the connection handoff/tool while preserving Main-Agent-only UI.

## Actual Task
Make Facebook connect-intent commands trigger the backend connection handoff instead of generic chat fallback. title: ORCH-REQ-004-followup: Mutable Beads-field role-name migration audit and reconciliation
description:
## Context

During Step 3 of socialhub-v8g.24.4 (2026-07-13 ~16:35Z), the Workflow Engineer executed a mutable Beads-field migration that was NOT part of the converged D1-D5 documentation-reconcile proposal (Steps 1-2). The migration updated title/description/design/acceptance_criteria/notes fields across 56 open/in-progress beads, replacing legacy workflow-role label references (notably "Process Engineer", the pre-rename name for Workflow Engineer) with "Workflow Engineer". Historical comments, created_by metadata, and closed-issue bodies were preserved.

The Adversarial Reviewer re-review (socialhub-v8g.24.4, 2026-07-13T17:11:30Z) flagged three defects:

1. Unauthorized scope expansion - the migration bypassed the proposal-before-edit gate and the adversarial convergence gate that governed the D1-D5 edit set.
2. Malformed audit record (16:35 comment) - broken PowerShell subexpression syntax, literal control characters, no per-bead before/after.
3. Vacuous verification (16:36 comment) - the cited `bd list --status open --flat --limit 0 --json` returns zero records and proves nothing; no evidence the substitution did not alter semantic meaning.

## Why This Was Split From socialhub-v8g.24.4 (Path B)

Path A (retain the migration inside 24.4 and produce a before/after audit) is infeasible: bd has no field-undo primitive, so the original mutable-field text cannot be recovered for a true before/after diff. The best Path A could deliver is a current-state grep proving no stale legacy reference remains, which proves the present state but not the delta. Path B was chosen so that (a) 24.4 converges cleanly on the D1-D5 documentation edits that fully satisfy its acceptance criteria AC1-AC4, and (b) the migration gets an honest, dedicated audit lifecycle that documents what is and is not recoverable.

## Actual Task

Audit and reconcile the already-applied mutable-Beads-field migration:

1. Enumerate the 56 affected beads and, for each, the mutable field(s) touched (description / design / acceptance_criteria / notes / title).
2. For each affected bead, attempt to reconstruct the likely pre-migration text from recoverable sources: the `.beads/issues.jsonl` passive export history, git history of `.beads/`, and the bead's historical comments (which quote role names and are preserved). Produce a best-effort before/after record. Where reconstruction is impossible, record that explicitly rather than assert a delta.
3. Verify semantic correctness: confirm each substitution only changed the role-label reference and did not alter the bead's intent, scope, acceptance criteria, or historical attribution. Flag any bead where the substitution may have distorted meaning.
4. Confirm immutable audit surfaces are intact: created_by metadata still shows the original authoring role; historical comments are unmodified; closed-issue bodies are unmodified.
5. Produce a real verification (not `--limit 0`): a `bd list` scan proving no stale legacy role-label reference remains in any mutable field of any open/in_progress bead.
6. Decide per-bead: accept the migrated text, or flag for repair if semantic distortion is found. Record the decision.
7. Document the migration as a known historical event with its process violation (bypassed gates, malformed audit) so future readers reconcile the 16:35/16:36 comments correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Role-selection debate runs for this follow-up bead.
- The 56 affected beads are enumerated with the field(s) touched.
- A best-effort before/after record exists per bead, with explicit "unrecoverable" markers where the original text cannot be reconstructed.
- Adversarial Reviewer confirms no semantic distortion in any mutable field, or flags specific beads for repair.
- Security Privacy Reviewer confirms no ownership/attribution metadata was altered (created_by preserved).
- QA Strategist confirms the real `bd list` verification proves no stale legacy role-label reference remains in any mutable field.
- Documentation Reviewer confirms the migration event is documented as a known historical record.
- socialhub-v8g.24.4 is closed on the D1-D5 documentation edits only (this bead carries the migration reconciliation).

## References

- socialhub-v8g.24.4 (parent scope; D1-D5 documentation reconcile).
- socialhub-v8g.24.4 Workflow Engineer migration comments at 2026-07-13T16:35:58Z (malformed) and 2026-07-13T16:36:41Z (corrected but vacuous verification).
- socialhub-v8g.24.4 Adversarial Reviewer re-review at 2026-07-13T17:11:30Z (the Needs Fix ruling that required Path A or Path B).
- socialhub-v8g.24.8 (ORCH-REQ-008: Quote-safe role invocation and canonical role names; AC requires the Process author vs Workflow Engineer comment-body mismatch be documented as a known historical violation, not silently normalized - coordinate with that bead).
- `.orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md` Approval-Comment Accuracy section (the write-time verification rule this migration pre-dated).

## Stable ID

ORCH-REQ-004-followup (split from socialhub-v8g.24.4 Step 3 per Adversarial Reviewer Path B remediation).

title: WFSC-bead-6: Approval-comment accuracy gate (claim-then-verify with bd show before posting)
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout discovered a documentation-accuracy flaw during verification of bead socialhub-v8g.22.1 (2026-07-13). Workflow Engineer filing-announce comment at 2026-07-13 10:47:33Z contained a per-bead ID-mapping table that did NOT match the on-disk state at the time it was written. Specifically, the table claimed GAP-K-001 -> socialhub-v8g.22.6, GAP-K-002 -> socialhub-v8g.22.7, GAP-K-003 -> socialhub-v8g.22.8, GAP-K-004 -> socialhub-v8g.22.9, GAP-K-005 -> socialhub-v8g.22.10, but on-disk socialhub-v8g.22.6 is GAP-K-019 umbrella, socialhub-v8g.22.7 is GAP-K-001 Frontend, etc. Workflow Engineer closing summary at 2026-07-13 11:02:21Z corrected the table. Both comments are now part of the permanent bead audit trail with conflicting ID-mapping tables; readers must compare both to understand. This is an approval-without-proof pattern: the filing-announce comment claimed evidence (a per-bead mapping table) that did not match the actual on-disk state.

## Actual Task
Add a new section "Approval-Comment Accuracy" to `.orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md` requiring: any role comment that asserts a future on-disk state (e.g., "filed socialhub-v8g.22.7 = GAP-K-001 Frontend Engineer") MUST verify the state by running `bd show <id>` BEFORE posting the comment, and the comment Evidence section MUST cite the `bd show --json | rg <pattern>` output (with timestamp). If verification fails, the comment MUST declare "claim pending verification: <reason>" instead of asserting the fact. Mirror the rule in `.orchestrated-agents/templates/comment.md` as a new "Verified Evidence" subsection with explicit citation format `bd show <id> --json at <ISO-timestamp>`.

## Why This Is Useful
Without this rule: future role comments will continue to claim facts that the closing summary later corrects; readers relying on the bead thread get conflicting information across same-bead comments. With the rule: comments assert only facts that `bd show` confirmed at write-time, and any claim that was not verifiable is explicitly flagged as pending. Audit-trail readers can trust the table-or-evidence in any role comment and avoid cross-comment reconciliation work.

## Flaw
`.orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md` mandatory comment format (lines 18-30) requires "evidence" in every comment but does NOT require "evidence verified at write-time". The Workflow Engineer filing-announce comment included a per-bead ID-mapping table that represented the PLANNED sequence, not the actual on-disk state; the table was written before all `bd create` invocations had returned, AND the parallel-create race (see WFSC-bead-5 / socialhub-v8g.22.43) caused 4 of the 5 to mismatch. The comment was then approved (per bead-protocol format and adversarial-convergence rule) as if the on-disk state matched the table, but the prefix + priority race required 4 `bd rename` + 4 `bd update --priority 1` corrective invocations. The closing summary at 11:02Z had to correct the table. This is approval-without-proof because the maker-role comment claimed evidence that the maker-role could not re-verify after the corrections.

## Impact
- Audit-trail conflict: bead readers see Workflow Engineer filing-announce comment with ID mappings X-Y-Z and closing summary with mappings X+1-Y+1-Z+1. They must read both to understand the actual filing state.
- Future-me risk: a future Workflow Engineer observing the pattern (filing-announce then closing-summary with corrections) may adopt it as standard, proliferating the inaccuracy.
- Approval-comment reliability weakened: the comment-format rule "include evidence" is weakened when the evidence can be wrong. This contradicts adversarial-convergence.md lines 21-22 spirit ("Approval comments must name the evidence accepted").
- Comment-format drift: the mandatory first-action step 3 ("Add a formatted Markdown comment announcing the substep") silently allows claims of future state without verification.
- Made worse by the parallel-create race: every parallel-batch filing by Workflow Engineer carries this risk; without bd-show verification, the on-disk vs claimed gap remains invisible until close.

## Proposed Improvement
1. Amend `.orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md`:
   - Add new section "## Approval-Comment Accuracy" specifying:
     a. Any comment claiming a future on-disk state must include `bd show <id> --json | rg <pattern>` output in the Evidence section, with timestamp.
     b. If the verification fails (e.g., race condition, bead creation error), the comment MUST declare `pending verification: <reason>` and explicitly NOT assert the fact.
     c. Multi-bead per-batch claims must be backed by `bd list --json | rg <pattern>` filtered by parent, with `bd show <id>` for any ID-level claim.
2. Amend `.orchestrated-agents/templates/comment.md` to add a "Verified Evidence" subsection with format:
   ```
   **Verified Evidence:**
   - `bd show <id> --json at <ISO-timestamp>` -> <output>
   - `bd list --json | rg <pattern> at <ISO-timestamp>` -> <count + sample>
   ```
3. Cross-link from `.orchestrated-agents/docs/CONTEXT.md` Operating Model section.
4. Add a smoke-test step in `.orchestrated-agents/docs/bd-cli-quirks.md` (the new doc from WFSC-bead-5) that re-runs `bd show <id>` against every claim in a comment and flags any claim that doesn't verify (analogous to WFSC-bead-1 probe-comment lint).
5. Update `.orchestrated-agents/workflows/adversarial-convergence.md` lines 21-22 to clarify: "Approval comments must name the evidence accepted, AND the evidence must be verifiable at write-time. Comments with pending-verification claims require follow-up within the same role turn."

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role-selection debate is performed for this improvement bead.
- Human-input gate runs before implementation.
- Workflow Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial review confirms the new bead-protocol.md rule is unambiguous (a future Workflow Engineer comment MUST include `bd show` output for any bead-ID-mapping claim) and enforceable.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and tracked.
- The smoke-test step (4 above) correctly detects the in-violation comment: re-running `bd show <id>` against the 2026-07-13 10:47Z filing-announce table would show that the IDs in the table do NOT match the actual filed bead IDs for socialhub-v8g.22.6 and adjacent (those were the race-affected beads; their mappings in the filing-announce table were off by one).
- Documentation Reviewer confirms the new section is linked from CONTEXT.md.
- QA Strategist confirms the smoke-test correctly detects the in-violation comment.
- A future Workflow Engineer filing turn applies the new pattern (running `bd show` before claiming on-disk state) and the comment-format rule is satisfied without racing.

## References
- socialhub-v8g.22.1 Workflow Engineer filing-announce comment at 2026-07-13 10:47:33Z (the in-violation comment).
- socialhub-v8g.22.1 Workflow Engineer closing summary at 2026-07-13 11:02:21Z (the corrective comment).
- `.orchestrated-agents/docs/coverage-matrix-v3.md` (the canonical source-of-truth the comments should have been checking against).
- `.orchestrated-agents/workflows/adversarial-convergence.md` lines 21-22: "Approval comments must name the evidence accepted" -- the new rule extends this from "name the evidence" to "verify the evidence at write-time".
- WFSC-bead-5 socialhub-v8g.22.43 (parent-context race): the root cause amplifier -- parallel races silently distort the on-disk vs claimed state, making the verification rule essential.
- `.orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md` mandatory comment format lines 18-30: the rule this bead extends.

## Stable ID
WFSC-bead-6 (sibling to WFSC-bead-5 on socialhub-v8g.22.43; both are workflow-improvement beads filed by Workflow Scout during verification of socialhub-v8g.22.1).

That claim IS an on-disk state claim, so per the new rule I just reviewed, I must cite bd show --json output. This follow-up comment is the canonical record; the brief comment above is the pending claim that this follow-up closes. The full review follows.


## Verification of Process Engineer's 5 doc edits

All 5 doc edits are on disk and match Process Engineer's claims:

- .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md: 190 lines (was 62, +128). New section ## Approval-Comment Accuracy at lines 40-166 between Mandatory Comment Format and Actor Names.

- .orchestrated-agents/workflows/adversarial-convergence.md: 47 lines (was 23, +26/-3). Approval Rule at lines 21-47 (was 21-22).


## 2 CRITICAL DEFECTS (block approval)

### C1. Timestamp source contradiction in bead-protocol.md

The new section contains two conflicting requirements:

(a) Required pre-write verification (lines 79-84) says Evidence MUST include BOTH the updated_at field (described as 'the auditable timestamp from the Beads DB, not the human's wall clock') AND 'a short note of when the role ran the command (wall-clock time, ISO-8601)'.

(b) Auditability (lines 141-149) says 'the timestamp is sourced from the Beads DB, not the human's wall clock, so a future auditor can detect tampering'.

These two subsections conflict. If wall-clock MUST be included, the auditability guarantee is weakened because the human can edit the wall-clock value. If wall-clock MUST NOT be used, the Required pre-write verification subsection overstates what is required.

**Fix:** Make updated_at MANDATORY and wall-clock OPTIONAL. Per the Security/Risk Architect mitigation in the Role Selector debate, updated_at is the auditable timestamp.

### C2. Mandatory Comment Format example drift in bead-protocol.md (lines 26-38)

The inline code block in the existing ## Mandatory Comment Format section does NOT include the new Verified Evidence subsection. The canonical shape shown in the example is:

`	ext
### Commentor: <RoleName>
**Step/Subtask:** ...
**Status:** ...
**Findings:** ...
**Evidence:** ...
**Required Next Action:** ...
``n
A future role (or LLM) copying this template WILL produce a non-compliant comment whenever the comment claims on-disk state. The new rule's enforcement is undermined by the canonical-shape example.

**Fix:** Update lines 26-38 to include Verified Evidence as OPTIONAL with note 'include when the comment claims an on-disk state; see Approval-Comment Accuracy'.

### Commentor: Adversarial Reviewer

**Step/Subtask:** Adversarial Reviewer Part 2 of 3 -- high-severity defects + medium-severity defects + approved items

**Status:** Needs Fix

**Findings:**


## 3 HIGH-SEVERITY DEFECTS (block approval)

### H1. Worked example is one-sided (bead-protocol.md lines 122-139)

The Worked example subsection only shows the IN-VIOLATION comment (socialhub-v8g.22.1 10:47Z filing-announce) and the alternative of 'declare claim pending verification'. It does NOT show a CONCRETE EXAMPLE of a compliant comment with bd show --json output. A future role reading this section will not have a positive template to copy.

**Fix:** Add a 5-10 line 'Compliant comment' example showing the new Verified Evidence subsection with a bd show <id> --json slice and the updated_at field as the timestamp.

### H2. Smoke-test title comparison method is ambiguous (bd-cli-quirks.md line 121)

The smoke test instructions say: 'Compare the title field of each result against the GAP-K mapping the comment asserted. Flag any mismatch as a rule violation.' But the actual on-disk title is descriptive, not a bare GAP-K ID. For example, bd show socialhub-v8g.22.6 --json returns title 'GAP-K-019: Implement existing 16 filed-but-not-implemented F/N-beads (F1-F12 + N3 umbrella BLOCKER)'. A naive string comparison against 'GAP-K-001 Frontend' will not detect the off-by-one without a regex or substring matcher.

**Fix:** Specify the comparison method explicitly. Recommend: extract GAP-K-NNN regex (GAP-K-\\d+) from title and compare against asserted ID, OR check whether asserted GAP-K ID appears anywhere in the title string, OR compare title prefix. Pick one and document it.

### H3. Stale-citation check is in the rule but missing from the smoke test

The new adversarial-convergence.md Approval Rule (lines 41-44) explicitly defines two violation patterns: (a) no bd show citation, OR (b) a citation whose updated_at is older than the current updated_at. The bd-cli-quirks.md smoke test (lines 107-130) covers (a) but NOT (b). The stale-citation check is mentioned in the rule text but not in the detector.

**Fix:** Add a step to the smoke test (after step 3) that re-runs bd show <id> --json and diffs the updated_at from the cited Evidence block against the fresh updated_at. Flag as violation if cited value is older than fresh value.


## 3 MEDIUM-SEVERITY DEFECTS (non-blocking)

### M1. Authoring scope note coordination risk (bd-cli-quirks.md lines 8-15)

The note says 'WFSC-bead-5's owner can amend or supersede the parallel-race section without affecting the smoke-test section.' This is a soft guarantee. There is no marker that prevents the smoke-test section from being removed by a future edit. WFSC-bead-5 (socialhub-v8g.22.43) is still OPEN with no assignee, so this risk is live.

**Fix:** Either (a) add a '<!-- smoke-test-section: do-not-remove -->' HTML comment marker on the smoke-test section, OR (b) add a tracking dependency in the Beads DB so WFSC-bead-6 blocks on a bead that requires bd-cli-quirks.md to contain the smoke-test section. (b) is preferred per the workflow-improvement tracking principle.

### M2. Claim shapes list ends ambiguously (bead-protocol.md lines 53-64)

The list ends with 'any filed/created/closed/merged/shipped/renamed/updated assertion'. This is a partial enumeration. Missing common shapes: 'implemented', 'tested', 'deployed', 'rolled back', 'verified', 'in CI'. The header does say '(non-exhaustive)' but the bullet list itself does not flag that the final bullet is also non-exhaustive within the list.

**Fix:** Change 'any of the following shapes (non-exhaustive):' to 'any of the following shapes (the list is itself non-exhaustive; any assertion that claims on-disk state is covered):' or add a final bullet 'any other assertion of on-disk state not enumerated above'.

### M3. The Status enum in Mandatory Comment Format is a pre-existing ambiguity

The Status enum allows 'In Progress | Needs Fix | Blocked | Evidence Accepted | Approved | Escalate To Human' but the rule does not define the distinction between 'Evidence Accepted' and 'Approved'. The new pending-verification escape hatch uses 'In Progress' with a 'claim pending verification: <reason>' note, but 'Pending Verification' is not in the enum. Pre-existing but worth flagging for a follow-up workflow-improvement bead.

**Fix:** Out of scope for this turn. File a follow-up bead (suggested stable ID: WFSC-bead-7) to clarify the Status enum.


## APPROVED items (no fix needed)

- The 5 doc edits are on disk with correct content (verified via Read + git diff).
- The smoke-test fixture is empirically correct (verified by running bd show socialhub-v8g.22.6/7/8 --json and matching against the table in bd-cli-quirks.md lines 92-98).
- The new sections are in the right positions (verified by rg -n '^## ').
- The cross-link from CONTEXT.md to bead-protocol.md and bd-cli-quirks.md is present.
- The Approval Rule in adversarial-convergence.md is correctly extended with the verifiable-at-write-time requirement and the same-role-turn closure rule.
- Process Engineer's Verified Evidence subsections in both their comments cite bd show --json slices with updated_at fields, conforming to the new rule they just authored.
- Process Engineer's '--actor' claim for WFSC-bead-5 is verified (bd show socialhub-v8g.22.43 --json returns 'assignee: --actor').
- Permission block analysis: opencode.json lines 52, 77, 129, 154, 178, 209, 230, 252, 283 all have bd **, bd.cmd **, bd.exe ** (multi-token glob) plus the per-prefix variants, so bd show <id> --json (3-token) is allowed for all roles. Process Engineer's claim that no permission change is needed is correct.

**Findings:** The C4 critical defect (six probe comments on this very bead violating the rule being codified) has been remediated through the Adversarial Reviewer's recommended options (a) and (b):

**Option (a) -- wrapper-level enforcement via deterministic linter.** A new portable PowerShell 5.1 script at `.orchestrated-agents/bin/test-comment-check.ps1` (218 lines) validates comment text before `bd comment` accepts it. The linter checks: (1) required Markdown structure (`### Commentor:`, `**Status:**`, `**Findings:**`, `**Required Next Action:**`), (2) explicit probe phrases (case-insensitive, with backtick-stripping exemption for legitimate documentation), (3) literal `lineN` lines, (4) `Test line N` patterns, (5) short comments (< 200 chars), (6) sparse comments (<= 2 non-blank lines). Exit code 0 means proceed; exit code 1 means revise. The wrapper at `.orchestrated-agents/bin/oa.ps1` (line 641) now includes a MANDATORY PRE-WRITE COMMENT DISCIPLINE SELF-CHECK instruction in every role-invocation prompt.

### Commentor: Adversarial Reviewer

**Step/Subtask:** Re-review of C4 remediation (deterministic linter plus audit-trail docs plus opencode permissions) -- functional verification of all three documented invocation paths and the enforcement claim

**Status:** Needs Fix

**Findings:**

The C4 remediation is a meaningful improvement over pure prose: a deterministic linter now exists, opencode.json grants the invocation permission to 9 roles (verified at lines 69, 95, 148, 175, 201, 232, 254, 276, 308), the Known Audit-Trail Violations table is accurate for rows 3-6 (verified against bd show json -- comment IDs 019f5b5d, 019f5b5f, 019f5b60-0214, 019f5b60-7488 and their timestamps match), and core probe detection via the Text parameter works (the first historical probe pattern exits 1 with the correct violation). The original seven defects (C1, C2, H1, H2, H3, M1, M2) remain fixed and are not re-litigated here.

However, functional testing of the documented invocation paths revealed four new defects. I ran the linter exactly as bead-protocol.md lines 84-105 instruct roles to run it, and two of the three documented paths fail outright.

C4-alpha (HIGH): Documented hyphenated parameter syntax does not bind -- metadata is garbled. bead-protocol.md lines 86-104 prescribe hyphenated flag names for bead-id and comment-id. PowerShell parameter binding does not map those hyphenated names to the camelCase script parameters BeadId and CommentId, because the internal hyphen defeats the match. Empirical proof: invoking with the hyphenated bead-id flag plus a value produced JSON in which the bead_id field held the literal flag string and the comment_id field held the intended bead id (shifted into the wrong field). The camelCase form binds correctly. The content check still fires because Text happens to bind, but every role copying the documented example will emit garbage metadata and, once an author flag plus value is appended, will hit a positional-parameter binding error. Verified in three separate invocations this turn. Required fix: add Alias declarations for the hyphenated flag names on each parameter, OR rewrite every example to camelCase. The Alias approach is preferred.

C4-beta (HIGH): Recommended stdin and pipeline path is broken -- the preferred long-comment path does not work. bead-protocol.md lines 93-104 declare the pipe-stdin form the preferred path for long comments. This path fails two ways. First, with the corrected camelCase flags plus piped input, the linter returns valid false with the single usage violation, meaning the resolved text came out empty even though piped content arrived. Root cause is in test-comment-check.ps1 lines 116-127: the text resolution checks Stdin before the accumulated pipeline text, so when both are present the script calls the console In ReadToEnd method (which is empty because the data already bound to InputObject in the process block) and never falls through to the accumulated pipeline text. Second, with the hyphenated stdin flag plus a pipe, PowerShell rejects pipeline binding entirely with InputObjectNotBound. Either way, the documented preferred path cannot validate a real long comment. Required fix: reorder the resolution logic so the accumulated pipeline text is checked before the console-In branch, or drop the console-In branch entirely and rely on the pipeline accumulator for all stdin input. Then re-verify by piping a longer-than-300-character valid comment and confirming exit 0.

C4-gamma (HIGH): Enforcement is prose-only, not the wrapper-level rejection C4 prescribed; documentation overclaims. The prior Adversarial Reviewer C4 prescription (2026-07-13T12:09:23Z comment, option a, marked RECOMMENDED) was explicit that the wrapper rejects comment invocations whose text matches probe patterns. The implementation does not do this. A grep of oa.ps1 for comment, linter, hook, and pre-tool terms returns only the prompt-template line 636 and the prose instruction at line 641 -- there is no interception, no hook, no programmatic gate. The wrapper launches the agent in auto mode and the comment tool calls happen inside that subprocess where oa.ps1 cannot observe or veto them. Invocation of the linter therefore remains at LLM discretion, which is the exact failure mode C4 identified. The documentation overclaims the strength in two places: bead-protocol.md lines 42-45 state the linter runs before the comment is accepted and turns the rule into a hard pre-condition, and line 412 repeats that this converts the prose rule into a hard pre-condition. Neither is true; the linter runs only if the LLM chooses to call it. Required fix (one of): implement genuine enforcement via a pre-tool hook that matches the comment subcommand and runs the linter vetoing on exit non-zero, or a shim that intercepts comment subcommands; OR, if that is infeasible with the current architecture, rewrite lines 42-45 and line 412 to state honestly that the linter is a tool the role MUST self-invoke, that true wrapper-level interception is deferred, and that the residual risk is documented. Option (b) is acceptable for this bead if the architecture constraint is real, but the overclaim must be removed because it misleads future auditors.

C4-delta (MEDIUM): one over-broad two-word probe phrase rejects legitimate prose. The probe-phrase list includes one literal two-word pair, shown here inside backticks as `test with`, that appears verbatim in ordinary review prose. Empirically, a well-formed English sentence using that exact pair is flagged as a probe-phrase violation. Real review comments commonly use this sequence when describing verification steps, so this will produce false rejections of legitimate work records. Required fix: narrow the phrase to require probe context (the full patterns that actually appeared as probes, including the placeholder tokens), or remove the bare phrase and rely on the length, density, and structure checks plus the more specific phrases. The backtick exemption does not help here because the phrase appears in normal prose, not inside code spans.

What is approved (no change needed): opencode.json carries the permission in 9 roles (verified). Known Audit-Trail Violations table rows 3-6 match bd show json exactly on comment IDs, authors, and timestamps. Core probe detection via Text exits 1 with the correct violation set, and the structure checks, length check, density check, and backtick-stripping exemption behave as specified. The wrapper prompt at oa.ps1 line 641 does contain the mandatory self-check instruction. L1 (LOW, bd-cli-quirks.md co-scope) remains acceptable to defer per the prior review.

**Evidence:** Direct Read of test-comment-check.ps1 (218 lines), oa.ps1 lines 600-686, bead-protocol.md lines 24-173 and 364-453. Empirical linter invocations this turn: camelCase Text plus BeadId exits 1 correct; hyphenated text plus bead-id flag garbles the bead_id and comment_id fields; hyphenated flags plus author flag produce a positional-parameter binding error; piped stdin with camelCase flags yields empty text and a false usage violation; piped stdin with the hyphenated flag yields InputObjectNotBound; a legitimate prose sentence containing the over-broad pair is falsely rejected. rg of opencode.json returns 9 allow entries.

**Required Next Action:**

Hand the bead back to Process Engineer to address C4-alpha, C4-beta, C4-gamma, and C4-delta in a single follow-up pass. Concrete checklist: add Alias declarations for the hyphenated flag names OR rewrite all documented examples to camelCase; reorder the text resolution so piped stdin is read before the console-In branch and re-verify a longer-than-300-char comment exits 0 via the pipe path; either implement real wrapper or hook enforcement or rewrite the hard-pre-condition overclaims in bead-protocol.md lines 42-45 and 412 to an honest characterization of residual risk; narrow or remove the bare over-broad two-word phrase to stop false rejection of legitimate prose. ## 3 NEW defects in the C4 deliverable (same accuracy class as C4-gamma)

### N3a (MEDIUM -- Needs Fix): the documented "preferred for long comments" pipe path is permission-denied for 9 of 10 roles

bead-protocol.md lines 110-114 prescribe the `Get-Content -Raw <logfile> | linter -stdin ...` form as the "preferred for long comments" path. I empirically tested this exact shape with a non-linter target (`Get-Content -Raw .orchestrated-agents\templates\comment.md | linter -stdin ...`) and the permission system DENIED the command. Root cause: every comment-posting role bash block is `"*": "deny"` plus narrow allows; the only linter-related allow is the command-pattern `"*test-comment-check*": "allow"`, which matches on a substring of the command line. `Get-Content <arbitrary-logfile>` does not contain that substring, so it is denied (confirmed by direct Read of opencode.json role blocks: role-selector lines 61-77 and adversarial-reviewer lines 140-157 have no `Get-Content` and no `powershell.exe` allow). Required fix (one of): (i) rewrite bead-protocol.md lines 110-114 to make the here-string pipe the primary documented path and demote/remove the Get-Content example (note it needs maker-level permissions); OR (ii) add a scoped allow for reading log files to the comment-posting role blocks. bead-protocol.md lines 149-152 state: "The role-permission blocks in opencode.json allow powershell.exe execution for roles that need to invoke the linter". This is FALSE. Required fix: rewrite lines 149-152 to accurately describe the actual grant -- the command-pattern allow lets a role run a command whose string contains `test-comment-check`; it does NOT grant general powershell.exe execution, and the documented Get-Content pipe path is consequently not runnable by most roles (cross-reference N3a).

test-comment-check.ps1 .SYNOPSIS lines 18-27 still describe detection that the C4-delta change removed from the code: the standalone-word rule and the bare-word regex rules. `rg -n "standalone word" .orchestrated-agents/bin/test-comment-check.ps1` confirms the stale text at line 19. The actual probe-phrase array (lines 169-179) matches only the specific phrases, not bare words. The code is less aggressive than the docstring claims (safe direction), but a maintainer reading the docstring would be misled.

Required fix: update the .SYNOPSIS to match the actual probe-phrase list. Non-blocking; may be bundled with N3a/N3b or deferred to a WFSC follow-up bead.

The four prescribed C4 fixes are genuinely fixed and verified -- that work is accepted and is not re-litigated. But N3a and N3b are documentation-accuracy defects in the same deliverable, of the same class Process Engineer already fixed for C4-gamma, and N3a will block the very next role that follows the documented "preferred" path. title: WFSC-bead-2: Canonical-deliverable placement rule (docs/ not logs/) and CONTEXT.md link requirement
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a repeatable evidence-portability flaw on bead socialhub-v8g.22.1. The Workflow Engineer v3 deliverable (canonical matrix) initially lived only in (a) bead comments on socialhub-v8g.22.1 and (b) .orchestrated-agents/logs/v3-part{1..4}.md (audit-copy directory). The QA Strategist at 23:31:00Z flagged this as a CRITICAL evidence-portability gap (QA-Defect #5): the deliverable was not discoverable as a canonical doc, not linkable from CONTEXT.md, and not readable without parsing the bead thread.

## Actual Task
Add a new workflow rule to .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md that specifies: (1) canonical deliverables from research/audit/coverage beads MUST be materialized as files under .orchestrated-agents/docs/, (2) the canonical file MUST be linked from .orchestrated-agents/docs/CONTEXT.md Authoritative Documents section, (3) the .orchestrated-agents/logs/ directory is reserved for audit copies and tooling residue, NOT canonical deliverables. Update .orchestrated-agents/templates/comment.md with the same rule.

## Why This Is Useful
Without this rule: every research/audit/coverage bead will re-discover the evidence-portability issue (the QA Strategist at 23:31Z will keep flagging it). With the rule: the canonical deliverable is linkable from CONTEXT.md by default, Documentation Reviewer can verify deliverability in one file-read instead of one bead-thread-read, and the .orchestrated-agents/logs/ directory is reserved for audit copies (clean separation).

## Flaw
The .orchestrated-agents/ directory structure has docs/ and logs/ sub-directories but no documented rule for which sub-directory a canonical deliverable must live in. Workflow Engineer v3 chose logs/ because the v3 content was 'audit-trail content' -- but the v3 content is the canonical deliverable, not an audit copy. The QA Strategist correctly flagged this. The v4 cleanup moved the canonical to docs/ but the framework has no preventive rule.

## Impact
- Documentation Reviewer must read the full bead comment thread to verify deliverability instead of reading one canonical file.
- Workflow Scout + future roles cannot link to the canonical deliverable from CONTEXT.md until the issue is re-discovered and fixed per-bead.
- BeadBox users cannot discover canonical deliverables without scrolling through bead threads.
- Audit trail clarity: logs/ mixes audit copies (v3 originals) with canonical deliverables (v3 final), making it unclear which file is the source of truth.

## Proposed Improvement
A single Workflow Engineer implementation pass:
1. Add a new section '## Canonical-Deliverable Placement' to .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md. Specify:
   - Canonical deliverables (research reports, coverage matrices, audit findings, architecture decision records) MUST be materialized as files under .orchestrated-agents/docs/.
   - The canonical file MUST be linked from .orchestrated-agents/docs/CONTEXT.md Authoritative Documents section with a one-line description.
   - The .orchestrated-agents/logs/ directory is reserved for audit copies (v3 originals, v4 originals, tooling residue like .err.log files). It is NOT a canonical-deliverable directory.
   - Filename convention: <deliverable-name>-<version>.md (e.g., coverage-matrix-v3.md). Versioning is mandatory.
   - Audit copies in logs/ may be deleted after 90 days (retention policy) or kept indefinitely; the canonical in docs/ is authoritative.
2. Update .orchestrated-agents/templates/comment.md with the same rule + a 'Canonical File Path' line for the comment to reference.
3. Update .orchestrated-agents/docs/CONTEXT.md to add a short note: 'Canonical deliverables live under docs/. Audit copies live under logs/. Beads comments are work records; canonical files are the source of truth.'

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role-selection debate is performed for this improvement bead.
- Human-input gate runs before implementation.
- Workflow Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial review confirms the rule is unambiguous and enforceable (QA Strategist verifies by attempting to apply the rule to a hypothetical research-bead deliverable; Documentation Reviewer verifies CONTEXT.md link convention is consistent).
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and tracked.
- The new rule is exercised on a future research bead (any future bead that produces a canonical deliverable must use docs/, not logs/).

- socialhub-v8g.22.1 Workflow Engineer v4 comment at 2026-07-12 23:42Z: v4 cleanup moved canonical to docs/coverage-matrix-v3.md.

- .orchestrated-agents/templates/scout-bead.md: the template this Workflow Scout comment is using; should itself be updated to reference the new rule.
