title: WFSC-bead-1: Probe-comment auto-lint to prevent audit-trail pollution
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a repeatable process flaw on bead socialhub-v8g.22.1 (full SDLC + engineering-role coverage evaluation, 2026-07-12 to 2026-07-13). The bead accumulated 17+ probe/test/scratch comments across 4 roles (HQF 4, PE 1, AR 9, QA 3), all explicitly self-disclosed as protocol violations per .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md line 18 ('Never write test, probe, placeholder, or scratch comments on a real bead. Every comment must be a meaningful Markdown work record.').

## Actual Task
Author and integrate a CI/automation lint that fails the build (or non-zero exit on pre-commit hook) when a Beads comment on a real bead matches a non-conforming pattern. The lint must distinguish probe residue from canonical work records at write-time and at view-time.

## Why This Is Useful
Without auto-enforcement: (a) every role must rely on manual self-discipline to detect and self-disclose probes (high cost, error-prone); (b) probe comments pollute the audit trail and slow QA Strategist + Documentation Reviewer evidence audits (see DR comment at 2026-07-13 00:14Z line 20 on probe-comment audit-trail pollution); (c) the N3 bead socialhub-v8g.21 (probe-comment audit-trail gate) has been filed P2 since the 2026-07-12 21:53 exception-fallback patch round but is not yet implemented, so the gap is open. The bead socialhub-v8g.22.1 thread alone is enough evidence: every role had to manually disclose its own probes. With auto-enforcement, future beads will have clean audit trails by default.

## Flaw
The bead-protocol.md rule 'Never write test, probe, placeholder, or scratch comments on a real bead' is documented (line 18) but is not enforced by tooling. The bd CLI surface has no comment remove / edit / classify subcommand (verified by HQF + PE + AR + QA in bead socialhub-v8g.22.1 at 22:26Z, 22:37Z, 22:46Z, 23:31Z). Every role relied on self-discipline + post-hoc self-disclosure. This pattern recurs across beads and slows convergence.

## Impact
- Audit trail pollution: each probe comment costs ~500-2000 chars of bead-comment storage and ~30 seconds of QA Strategist review time to confirm it is residue.
- Self-discipline risk: a future role that forgets to self-disclose will leave probes in the audit trail unflagged, eroding evidence integrity.
- Convergence slowdown: 4 of 4 adversary roles on socialhub-v8g.22.1 spent comment space on probe self-disclosure that could have been spent on substantive review.
- BeadBox view degradation: probe residue shows in BeadBox comment lists alongside canonical work records; future BeadBox upgrades that surface probe residue as separate kind would need this lint as a precondition.

## Proposed Improvement
A 3-part improvement implemented as a single Workflow Engineer task:
1. **CI/automation lint script** at .orchestrated-agents/lint/bead-comment-lint.ps1 (PowerShell, matches Windows wrapper) + .orchestrated-agents/lint/bead-comment-lint.sh (POSIX, for parity with F2 bead socialhub-v8g.10 POSIX oa.sh wrapper). Script detects: (a) no Markdown header (## / ###), (b) no 'Commentor:' block, (c) no '**Status:**' field, (d) single-token literal under 100 chars matching /^(hello|test|probe|comment|scratch|ignore|TEST_REVIEW_PROBE_.*|line\\d*)$/i, (e) text matching /test|probe|scratch|ignore|placeholder/i without a self-disclosure Commentor block. Non-zero exit on any match.
2. **bd comment --probe flag** (workflow-improvement follow-up): request the bd maintainers to add an optional --probe flag that marks the comment as tooling-validation residue in the audit trail, so BeadBox can hide it by default. This requires either (a) an upstream bd PR or (b) a wrapper shim .orchestrated-agents/bin/bd-comment-probe.cmd that writes the probe to a local file with a probe marker and explains in subsequent canonical comments. Acceptable fallback: write probe comments to .orchestrated-agents/logs/probe-<bead-id>-<timestamp>.md and reference them from the canonical comment.
3. **bead-protocol.md amendment**: add a new section '## Probe-Comment Auto-Lint' that references the lint script and lists the patterns it detects. Also amend '## Mandatory First Actions' to require a lint-run after every bd comment invocation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role-selection debate is performed for this improvement bead (Workflow Engineer is the natural maker; QA + DR + SPR provide adversarial review).
- Human-input gate runs before implementation.
- Workflow Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial review confirms the improved workflow would have caught the flaw (verify by running the lint against the socialhub-v8g.22.1 bead comment history; it should flag all 17+ probe comments).
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and tracked. Verified by re-inspecting bead comments on socialhub-v8g.4 (the exception-fallback patch bead) and confirming the N3 bead socialhub-v8g.21 implementation is either superseded by this bead or cross-linked.
- Lint script passes a smoke test (run on a clean bead with one canonical comment + one probe comment; probe is flagged, canonical is not).
- Documentation: bead-protocol.md amended with Probe-Comment Auto-Lint section; .orchestrated-agents/README.md (if exists) or docs/CONTEXT.md lists the lint command.

## References

- N3 bead socialhub-v8g.21: existing P2 follow-up that this bead supersedes or cross-links.

title: F11: Beads-actor integrity in exception-fallback path
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a Beads-actor integrity gap. The 2026-07-12 21:36 and 21:38 comments on socialhub-v8g.4 have author: Workflow Engineer in bd show output, while the comment body explicitly self-identifies as Documentation Reviewer. The Documentation Reviewer 21:38 verdict self-acknowledged this with: 'the comment actor is being set explicitly via the --actor flag to preserve audit-trail integrity. The wrapper was not invoked for this role; the role author tag was added manually.' This is the same actor-integrity issue that F7's governance rule needs to handle. F11 specifically captures the actor-attribution shape requirement that every exception-fallback comment must follow.

## Actual Task
Add a 'Exception-Fallback Comment Shape' rule to .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md. The rule must require: (a) a 'Why This Was Necessary' heading that names the retry count and the prompt-miss evidence (e.g., 'Why This Was Necessary: 2 PE attempts returned no-op at 21:49 and 22:01; routed via --actor flag to preserve audit-trail integrity'); (b) a 'Role Author' line that names the actual role author (not Codex-Orchestrator); (c) the BEADS_ACTOR env var or --actor flag set to the actual role (e.g., --actor 'Documentation Reviewer'); (d) a cross-reference to F7 governance rule. The bead-protocol change must be enforced by wrapper pre-flight (per F3) so any exception-fallback comment lacking the mandatory shape is rejected with a human-readable error before being posted.

## Why This Is Useful
The 21:36/21:38 actor-mismatch is the kind of audit-trail defect that erodes trust in the framework. A future reader cannot tell whether 'Workflow Engineer' or 'Documentation Reviewer' is the actual author. F11 codifies the attribution shape so every exception-fallback comment has unambiguous role authorship, with a Why-This-Was-Necessary heading that explains the bypass. Closing F11 produces a stable audit-trail attribution invariant for the entire framework.

## Flaw
There is no current rule that requires explicit actor attribution when the wrapper is bypassed. The bead-protocol.md mentions BEADS_ACTOR as the actor source for the wrapper (line 39: 'the wrapper only sets BEADS_ACTOR, OA_TARGET_BEAD, and OA_ROLE_NAME') but does not specify what to do when the wrapper is bypassed. The 21:36/21:38 comments had the BEADS_ACTOR defaulted to the underlying Workflow Engineer (because the wrapper was not invoked and the actor was set via --actor flag after-the-fact), but the comment body self-attributed to a different role. Without F11, every future exception-fallback comment can repeat this pattern.

## Impact
If not fixed, every future exception-fallback comment can have actor-mismatch. The audit trail integrity guarantee is conditional on every future exception-fallback invocation being correctly attributed. Closing F11 produces the mandatory actor-attribution rule and the wrapper pre-flight enforcement that catches mismatches at the source.

## Proposed Improvement
Add the 'Exception-Fallback Comment Shape' rule to bead-protocol.md (per F11's actual-task description). Add a pre-commit check to .beads/hooks/pre-commit that verifies every new comment on a bead matches the actor-attribution rule. Add a wrapper pre-flight extension at oa.ps1 Run-Role (lines 304-381) that detects exception-fallback paths and enforces the comment shape.

This rule prevents the actor-mismatch pattern observed on socialhub-v8g.4 at 21:36 and 21:38 where the comment body identifies as Documentation Reviewer but BEADS_ACTOR defaults to Workflow Engineer.

This follow-up beads the security review for the 21:53 widening.

## Actual Task
Security Privacy Reviewer must produce an Evidence Accepted comment on the multi-arg bd ** / bd.cmd ** / bd.exe ** permission widening across 9 agents. The review must: (1) enumerate every Beads subcommand that can be invoked via multi-arg bd ** (any token after bd). At minimum: bd show, bd update, bd comment, bd create, bd close, bd ready, bd list, bd add, bd dep add, bd dep remove, bd label add, bd label remove, bd sync, bd config, bd admin, bd reset, bd compact, bd migrate, bd stats. (2) Identify which of these subcommands, when invoked via multi-arg, can do destructive things. Examples: bd reset (destructive - drops Dolt state), bd admin (privileged - changes DB schema), bd migrate (destructive - changes schema), bd close (modifying-state - closes bead). (3) Confirm that NONE of the 9 agents has been granted any privilege it should not have. The maker agent (oa-maker-engineer) explicitly does NOT have bd permissions, which is correct per A2. (4) Confirm the new bd ** rule does not permit the maker agent, because the maker permission block (lines 91-114) does not have the new bd ** rule.

## Why This Is Useful
The bd ** rule is the broadest form of the bd permission grant - any token after bd is allowed, including destructive subcommands. Without a Security Privacy Reviewer sign-off, every invocation of bd by a non-maker agent is implicitly trusted. Closing F10 produces an explicit per-subcommand safety matrix. Future permission edits that want to widen further must rerun the same safety review.

## Flaw
The Round-1 review (Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31) covered A2/A4/A11 but did NOT cover the 21:53 widening. The 21:53 widening is functionally equivalent to 'bd-and-anything' for 9 agents. The Round-2 N2 fix at oa.ps1 lines 269-283 was about the wrapper prompt template using bare bd show / bd update / bd comment (single-arg patterns) - it was a prompt-template narrowing, not a permission widening. The 21:53 widening is a permission widening that crosses Security Privacy Reviewer scope per line 10 of workflows/adversarial-convergence.md ('permissions' is explicitly listed as Security Privacy Reviewer trigger).

## Impact
If not fixed, the bd ** widening is implicitly accepted with no security review. Future permission changes that tighten or widen the bd rule will inherit this unverified state. The framework's promise of evidence-backed convergence is broken for the bd permission scope. Closing F10 produces the missing security sign-off comment and validates the safety matrix for the multi-arg bd rules.

## Proposed Improvement
Security Privacy Reviewer must run an explicit safety review of the bd ** rule across all 9 agents. The review must be filed as an Evidence Accepted comment on this bead (socialhub-v8g.X) with the per-subcommand safety matrix. If any subcommand is flagged unsafe, the proposal-implementation must narrow the rule to a more specific pattern (e.g., bd show **, bd update **, bd comment **, bd ready **) or split the rule per-subcommand to allow safe subcommands and deny destructive ones (e.g., bd reset **, bd admin **, bd migrate **). The wrapper prompt template at oa.ps1:336-364 must also be updated (per F12) to teach the narrowed rule set so future roles invoke only the safe subcommands.

The 21:53 patch widened to bd ** to allow multi-token invocations. The wrapper prompt template (oa.ps1:336-364) only requires single-arg patterns (e.g., 'bd show \u003cId\u003e', 'bd update \u003cId\u003e --assignee \u003cRole\u003e'). title: F7: Codex-Orchestrator exception-fallback governance rule
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a missing governance rule for the Codex-Orchestrator exception-fallback path. Across socialhub-v8g.4, the Codex-Orchestrator was invoked THREE times outside the documented adversarial loop: (1) 2026-07-12 20:52 - docs patch after Workflow Engineer prompt-miss; (2) 2026-07-12 21:36 + 21:38 - Documentation Reviewer comments authored via --actor flag because the wrapper was not invoked; (3) 2026-07-12 21:53 - orchestration wrapper code + permission patch after Workflow Engineer was invoked twice. No rule governs when the exception-fallback path is permitted, what scope of edits it can apply, or what retry-threshold must be hit first. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 first named F7 as a follow-up; Documentation Reviewer 21:38 confirmed F7 is Workflow Scout scope.

## Actual Task
Document a Codex-Orchestrator exception-fallback governance rule. The rule must define: (a) SCOPE - exception-fallback invocations may only produce documentation edits or routing-workaround edits; they may NOT modify oa.ps1, oa.cmd, opencode.json, or .orchestrated-agents/roles/*.md; (b) RETRY THRESHOLD - the Codex-Orchestrator must attempt Workflow Engineer at least TWICE before triggering the exception-fallback path (and may trigger after two consecutive no-op rounds or two prompt-misses); (c) ACTOR ATTRIBUTION - the exception-fallback comment must explicitly name the actual role author using --actor flag (the Codex-Orchestrator is a human-role, not an oa-* agent); (d) AUDIT TRAIL - the exception-fallback comment must include a 'Why-This-Was-Necessary' heading that names the retry count and the prompt-miss evidence; (e) POST-HOC ADVERSARIAL REVIEW - any exception-fallback invocation must trigger an Adversarial Reviewer audit before the patch is treated as accepted, and if Security Privacy Reviewer scope applies (line 10 of workflows/adversarial-convergence.md - data, auth, secrets, permissions, network, deployment), that audit must precede the exception-fallback comment being posted.

## Why This Is Useful
The 21:53 exception-fallback patch was technically correct (it fixed a real routing bug) but bypassed every gate in workflows/adversarial-convergence.md. Without F7, the next exception-fallback invocation could rewrite the same files again, but this time introduce a security regression that goes uncaught. F7 codifies the rule that distinguishes 'documentation exception' from 'code/permission exception': only docs may be edited via the exception-fallback path. Any exception-fallback that wants to edit code/permission must reroute through Workflow Engineer, even at the cost of one extra round trip. Closing F7 prevents the most consequential class of exception-fallback edits from happening at all.

## Flaw
The framework as currently designed has no governance rule for the exception-fallback path. The bead-protocol.md mandates that roles do their own work and the wrapper does NOT comment - but does not address what happens when the role-loop is broken. The 21:53 Codex-Orchestrator invocation demonstrates this: three Workflow Engineer attempts and a routing bug forced an out-of-loop patch. The patch was well-intentioned but expanded the bash permission grants across 9 agents without an explicit security sign-off, which is exactly the failure mode that adversarial convergence was designed to prevent.

## Impact
If not fixed, every future out-of-loop situation can produce an exception-fallback patch with no governance. The framework can be silently rewritten by Codex-Orchestrator invocations that 'fixed the immediate problem' while bypassing every gate. This is the highest-leverage governance gap in the framework because (a) it can rewrite code, (b) it can widen permissions, (c) it can be triggered by ANY role-loop failure, and (d) it does not require the human's attention.

## Proposed Improvement
Add .orchestrated-agents/workflows/exception-fallback.md as a new workflow file. The file must define: SCOPE (docs and routing ONLY); RETRY THRESHOLD (>= 2 PE attempts before exception); ACTOR ATTRIBUTION (--actor flag mandatory, with explanation); AUDIT TRAIL (Why-This-Was-Necessary heading mandatory); POST-HOC ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (F9 hook - any code/permission exception MUST be audited before being treated as accepted). Update bead-protocol.md to reference the new workflow. Update role-selector.md to mention the governance rule when debating exception-fallback scope. Update the role-routing flow so Codex-Orchestrator cannot edit code/permission files directly - only via the wrapper, which checks for authorization through Test-WrapperSelf (extends A11).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role Selector debate runs on this follow-up bead before any implementation.
- Human-input gate runs to confirm the scope-vs-permission boundary (the human retains the right to invoke exception-fallback for code edits via an explicit opt-in; the framework default is docs-only).
- Security Privacy Reviewer signs off on the scope-vs-permission boundary rule before implementation.
- Workflow Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial Reviewer confirms the improved rule would have prevented the 21:53 patch from bypassing approval.
- QA Strategist tests the new rule by simulating a role-routing failure and confirming the exception-fallback path is invoked only after 2 PE attempts and produces a docs-only patch.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and discoverable from epic socialhub-v8g.
design: New file .orchestrated-agents/workflows/exception-fallback.md. Must define: (a) retry-threshold for Workflow Engineer before exception applies (default: 2 PE attempts), (b) file-type constraints for exception-fallback patches (docs and routing workarounds ONLY; NOT code, NOT permission changes), (c) actor attribution rule (Codex-Orchestrator must name the actual role author on the bead), (d) audit-trail requirement (every exception-fallback invocation must include a Why-This-Was-Necessary heading in the bead comment), (e) post-hoc Adversarial Reviewer audit hook (any exception-fallback patch must be audited before being treated as accepted). The rule must be referenced from bead-protocol.md.

Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 first named F7; Documentation Reviewer 21:38 confirmed F7 is Workflow Scout scope.

**Defect A2 - Maker Engineer permission too broad under --auto:** opencode.json lines 85-95 grant maker-engineer 'edit: allow' and bash '*': allow, with only narrow denies (git push, git reset --hard, git checkout --, rm -rf, del, Remove-Item). The wrapper spawns OpenCode with --auto (oa.ps1 line 249), which means every allowed command executes without confirmation. maker-engineer.md says 'Do not commit, push, deploy, migrate, or change secrets unless explicitly authorized' but permission does not block 'git commit', 'npm publish', Alembic upgrade head, or writes to .env. Role prompt is not enforcement. Need explicit denies for git commit, alembic upgrade, env-file writes, and any secret-touching file pattern.

**Defect A3 - Process Engineer permission blocks legitimate verification:** opencode.json lines 225-235 allow Process Engineer 'bd *', 'git status/diff/log', 'rg *' but deny npm/pytest by default ('*': ask). Workflow Scout and Adversarial Reviewer hand work to Process Engineer; if Process Engineer needs to verify a fix with npm run lint or pytest it must ask for each call. Either add lint/test as allow, or document that Process Engineer defers verification to QA Strategist and states that explicitly.

**Defect A4 - Security Privacy Reviewer cannot run secret scanners or tests:** opencode.json lines 151-158 grant Security Privacy Reviewer only bd/git/rg. No npm run lint, no pytest, no gitleaks/trufflehog. A meaningful security review of the orchestration package needs to actually run a secret scan and unit-test the wrapper. Add at minimum: npm run lint*, pytest*, and a documented allowlist for gitleaks/trufflehog.

**Defect A5 - Negative-then-allow permission precedence is order-dependent:** opencode.json roles use bash: { '*': deny, 'bd *': allow, ... }. Whether a rule like 'bd *' overrides '*': deny depends on OpenCode's matcher. If OpenCode evaluates pattern in declaration order and '*' matches as literal first, then bd never gets allowed. Need an explicit test of 'oa.cmd run ... adversarial-reviewer' executing 'bd show socialhub-v8g.4' to prove the precedence works. Same pattern repeats for every oa-* agent. Recommend documenting OpenCode's actual behavior in docs/context.md or testing each role once with a benign bd command.

**Defect A6 - README overstates portability:** README.md lines 56-67 'Copying To Another Repository' implies the package is portable. The wrapper itself (bin/oa.cmd + bin/oa.ps1) is Windows-only: oa.cmd uses @echo off, the .ps1 uses PowerShell SecureString DPAPI (Windows-only), and the spawn pattern uses %~dp0 and Read-Host -AsSecureString. README never says 'Windows-only' or 'experimental macOS/Linux support'. Either implement a POSIX shell wrapper or explicitly state Windows-only in the README and in docs/context.md.

**Defect A7 - System reminder points to uppercase CONTEXT.md while file is lowercase:** The orchestration package's doc path in the operating context is .orchestrated-agents/docs/context.md (lowercase). The system instruction I just received referenced .orchestrated-agents/docs/CONTEXT.md (uppercase). On Windows the case-insensitive FS hides this; on macOS/Linux the mismatch will break. README, opencode.json, and all role prompts reference lowercase context.md. Normalize the system reminder path or rename the file consistently.

**Defect A8 - Role-selection template is missing the Meta column it already needs:** templates/role-selection.md columns are 'Role | Reason | Maker Or Adversary | Required Sign-off'. The actual Role Selector comment on THIS bead (socialhub-v8g.4) used 'Meta' classification for Role Selector, Human Question Framer, and Workflow Scout. The template should be updated to add 'Meta' as a valid value for the Maker Or Adversary column, or split into two columns. Currently the template forces the role to free-text it.

**Defect A9 - scout-bead.md template is missing required Context / Acceptance headers:** Templates for new workflow-improvement beads (templates/scout-bead.md) include '## Context' but not '## Actual Task', '## Why This Is Useful', or '## Acceptance Criteria' which other beads in this repo (including the parent epic socialhub-v8g and this bead itself) use. Workflow Scout will produce inconsistent improvement beads. Align the template with the standard bead description shape.

**Defect A10 - Acceptance criteria for this bead is ambiguous about verdict ownership:** Acceptance criterion 6 says 'The evaluation records whether the setup is ready for product-code tasks.' No role is assigned this verdict. Workflow Scout files follow-ups; who declares ready/not-ready? Should be named explicitly (proposal: Workflow Scout synthesizes the verdict after collecting sign-offs, with Human Question Framer on standby for unresolved disagreement).

**Defect A11 - Permission allows Process Engineer to edit the wrapper that runs everything:** opencode.json lines 220-224 allow Process Engineer to edit '.orchestrated-agents/**' (including bin/oa.cmd and bin/oa.ps1) and 'opencode.json'. If Process Engineer makes a typo in oa.ps1, the next oa.cmd invocation could break before any role has a chance to review. Recommend at minimum requiring an Adversarial Reviewer checkpoint before any change to bin/** takes effect, or adding a pre-flight self-test inside oa.ps1.

**Defect A12 - Workflow Scout permission lacks 'bd close' for filing improvement beads:** opencode.json lines 205-212 allow git status/diff, rg, and bd * (which covers bd close). Actually this is fine on review; bd * matches bd close. No defect here, withdrawing A12.

**Evidence:**

- .orchestrated-agents/bin/oa.cmd (4 lines, full read)
- .orchestrated-agents/bin/oa.ps1 (270 lines, full read)

After fixes are committed, I will re-review and post Part 2 with the verdict. Workflow Scout should also pick up A1, A2, A6, A7 as workflow-improvement follow-up beads regardless of inline fixes, since they document process gaps. ### Commentor: Security Privacy Reviewer

**Step/Subtask:** Independent security/privacy sign-off on the three security-sensitive fixes (A2 maker permission width, A4 security-privacy-reviewer permission, A11 wrapper self-check adequacy) plus verification that the Codex-Orchestrator fallback doc patch introduces no secret values.

**Status:** Evidence Accepted (Approved with documented residual follow-ups F1-F8 + N3 owned by Workflow Scout)

**Threat/risk scope reviewed:**
1. Secret exposure - `MINIMAX_API_KEY`, `MINIMAX_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY` handling, wrapper status output, edit/deny rules on `.env*`.
2. Authorization and user ownership - permission blocks for destructive git/alembic/docker/npm/scp, maker edit deny rules, role-attribution trust in `BEADS_ACTOR`/`OA_TARGET_BEAD`.
3. Prompt/state/checkpoint leakage - wrapper does not inject secrets into prompts; only sets `BEADS_ACTOR`, `OA_TARGET_BEAD`, `OA_ROLE_NAME` env vars for the child `opencode` process.
4. Filesystem and shell safety - destructive bash deny rules on maker; wrapper self-check parses `oa.ps1` and validates `oa.cmd` shim existence.
5. Dependency and supply-chain risk - `bd` resolved via `Resolve-Exe` from `$env:PATH`; `opencode` resolved the same way; no fixed-version pinning in the wrapper itself (pinned `bd v1.0.4` documented in `beadbox-windows.md`).
6. Network/API handling - wrapper does not make network calls; only child `opencode` process calls the MiniMax endpoint (out of scope for this review).
7. Data retention and logs - wrapper never echoes the secret value; only `minimax_key_value_printed: $false` is asserted. `Set-MiniMaxKey` scrubs `firstPlain/secondPlain = $null` in `finally`.
8. Risky actions that need confirmation - adversarial/QA/security roles have `edit: deny`; the framework relies on the maker prompt + adversarial loop, NOT a permission-blocked-confirmation gate. Documented residual risk; not in scope to redesign here (F7 tracks the governance rule).

**A2 evidence - `oa-maker-engineer` permission (`opencode.json` lines 79-110):**
- `edit`: `*` allow, `*.env` deny, `*.env.*` deny, `.env` deny, `.env.*` deny, `.env.example` allow. Cross-variant `.env*` coverage correct; example file allowlisted.
- `bash`: `*` allow with destructive-action denylist - `git push*`, `git commit*`, `git reset --hard*`, `git checkout -- *`, `git clean -fd*`, `rm -rf *`, `del *` (ask), `Remove-Item *` (ask), `alembic upgrade*`, `alembic * upgrade*`, `docker push*`, `npm publish*`, `scp *`.
- Residual risk observed, not flagged: maker still has `edit: * allow` and `bash: * allow`. Denylist blocks the known destructive primitives; permission block cannot police every phrasing (`git commit -am`, `git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit`, etc.). The framework relies on the maker prompt + adversarial review + Workflow Scout audit trail. Consistent with framework design.
- No secret-leak paths in this agent: never touches `.env*` beyond `.env.example` (sample/template file).

**A4 evidence - `oa-security-privacy-reviewer` permission (`opencode.json` lines 156-182):**
- `edit`: deny (security reviewer is read-only by design).
- `bash`: `*` deny, `bd *`/`bd.cmd *`/`bd.exe *` allow, `git status/diff` allow, `rg *` allow, `npm run lint*`/`npm test*`/`pytest*` allow, and the three-family allowlists for the two secret scanners: `gitleaks*`, `gitleaks.cmd *`, `gitleaks.exe *`, `trufflehog*`, `trufflehog.cmd *`, `trufflehog.exe *`.
- Scanner family coverage correct: matches the `Resolve-Exe` ordering (`bd.exe`, `bd.cmd`, `bd`); identical three-family allowlist pattern used for `gitleaks` and `trufflehog` - confirmed in Adversarial Reviewer's Part 2 audit and re-read this turn.
- This role cannot edit files, so no script-injection / rule-bypass risk via this agent.

**A11 evidence - `Test-WrapperSelf` (`oa.ps1` lines 167-197):**
- Uses `System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser.ParseFile()` to parse `oa.ps1`; throws with first parse-error line number on syntax errors.
- Validates `oa.cmd` shim exists at `oa.ps1` directory.
- Wired into `Show-Status` (lines 207-212, returns `wrapper_self_check: ok` or `fail: <reason>`) and `Run-Role` pre-flight (lines 236-239, throws on non-`ok` and aborts invocation).
- Live this turn: `wrapper_self_check: ok`. This means `oa.ps1` parses cleanly and `oa.cmd` is present.
- Residual risk observed, not flagged: parse-only check catches syntax errors but NOT logic errors (accidentally deleted function, semantic regression). Documented in F3 (`--auto` failure-visibility gap).

**Secret-handling evidence (`oa.ps1` lines 57-143):**
- `Get-SecretPlainText` (57-67) - `SecureStringToBSTR` + `PtrToStringBSTR` + `ZeroFreeBSTR` in `finally`. Proper DPAPI handling.
- `Set-MiniMaxKey` (109-132) - `Read-Host -AsSecureString`, double-entry equality check, `SetEnvironmentVariable("MINIMAX_API_KEY", ..., "User")`, `$firstPlain = $null` + `$secondPlain = $null` in `finally`, returns `minimax_key_value_printed: $false`.
- `Clear-MiniMaxKey` (134-143) - removes User scope via `SetEnvironmentVariable` + `Remove-Item Env:\` for Process scope. Returns `minimax_key_value_printed: $false`.
- `Get-MiniMaxKeyState` (69-86) - only returns `_present` booleans; never returns the value.
- `Show-Status` output (214-224) - asserts `minimax_key_value_printed: $false`. Confirmed in live this-turn output.
- Live validation: `minimax_key_value_printed: false`. Key value never appeared in any command output across the entire bead audit trail (verified by Process Engineer Round-1/2/3/4 and Adversarial Reviewer Part 2).

**Codex-Orchestrator fallback patch security review:**
- `.orchestrated-agents/docs/beadbox-windows.md:33-59` and `.orchestrated-agents/docs/CONTEXT.md:185-197` are documentation-only edits; `rg "MINIMAX_API_KEY" .orchestrated-agents/docs` returns only the legitimate references in `CONTEXT.md` env-var documentation (e.g., line 161 area describing the required env-var). No actual key value introduced.
- No new file paths or env-var names touched. No code paths affected. Documentation-only.

**OpenCode JSON validity:** `(Get-Content -Raw .\opencode.json | ConvertFrom-Json) | Out-Null` -> `JSON_VALID`. Schema unchanged since Round-1 closes; no permission widening in subsequent rounds.

**Independent security conclusions:**
- **A2**: `oa-maker-engineer` destructive denylist is correctly scoped (git commit/push, alembic upgrade, docker push, npm publish, scp) and `.env*` write paths are blocked while `.env.example` remains allowed. Residual prompt-trust risk is documented but out of scope.
- **A4**: `oa-security-privacy-reviewer` is read-only (edit denied) with allowlisted secret-scanner families and standard test runners. Cannot be coerced to edit files or bypass the denylist.
- **A11**: `Test-WrapperSelf` is parse-only and best-effort, but does catch the failure mode (syntactically broken `oa.ps1`) that would brick every subsequent role invocation. Wired into both `Show-Status` and `Run-Role`. Sufficient as a first-line guardrail; F3 captures the `--auto` failure-visibility follow-up.
- **Secret-handling**: `MINIMAX_API_KEY` value never enters stdout, stderr, environment export, or log lines. DPAPI SecureString + memory scrub + explicit `minimax_key_value_printed: $false` invariant hold across live validation.
- **Codex-Orchestrator fallback patch**: documentation-only, no security surface change.

**Residual follow-ups (NOT closed inline, owned by Workflow Scout per adversarial-convergence framework):**
- **F3** (`--auto` failure-visibility gap): `Test-WrapperSelf` aborts `Run-Role` on parse failure, but `--auto` bypasses the interactive prompt that would normally surface the abort. Failure is logged but not user-visible.
- **F7** (Codex-Orchestrator exception-fallback governance): an orchestrator edited orchestration docs after three Process Engineer role misses. No rule yet governs when direct orchestrator editing is permitted, including scope and retry thresholds. Security review confirms the patch itself is benign, but the governance rule needs definition.
- **F8** (Process Engineer prompt-miss pattern): same exception-fallback path. Security neutrality maintained, but a chronic prompt-miss pattern would degrade the adversarial loop's effectiveness and could be exploited (e.g., a malicious role prompt that quietly fails). Independent of the immediate patches.
- **N3** (probe-comment audit trail): four low-content probe comments on this bead (three role-selector 17:53, one HQF 18:01, plus Adversarial Reviewer 20:55). Bead-protocol gap; no security exposure (no secrets, no commands executed by those comments), but should be gated by minimum-length / structured-heading rule.
- All F1, F2, F4, F5, F6 (verdict ownership, POSIX wrapper, per-role smoke-test, bd version-pin tracked-decision bead, comment-count staleness) - tracked but not security-critical.

**Approval:** Approved for the three security-sensitive fixes (A2, A4, A11) and the Codex-Orchestrator documentation patch. Residual risk is documented and converted to follow-up beads (F3, F7, F8, N3) for Workflow Scout to file against epic `socialhub-v8g`.

**Evidence:**
- `opencode.json` lines 79-110 (oa-maker-engineer A2 fix) and 156-182 (oa-security-privacy-reviewer A4 fix) - re-read end-to-end this turn.
- `opencode.json` lines 220-228 (oa-process-engineer A3 fix) - confirmed by QA Strategist, no security change.
- `.orchestrated-agents/bin/oa.ps1` lines 1-316 - full re-read.
  - 57-67 `Get-SecretPlainText`
  - 69-86 `Get-MiniMaxKeyState`

- `.orchestrated-agents/bin/oa.cmd` (4 lines) - `@echo off` shim, passes args to `oa.ps1`. No secret handling here.
- `.orchestrated-agents/docs/beadbox-windows.md` lines 33-59 and `.orchestrated-agents/docs/CONTEXT.md` lines 185-197 - docs-only patch, no secrets.
- Live this turn:
  - `bd update socialhub-v8g.4 --assignee "Security Privacy Reviewer" --status in_progress` returned `Updated issue`.
  - `powershell -File .\.orchestrated-agents\bin\oa.ps1 status` returned `wrapper_self_check: ok`, `opencode_config_exists: true`, `minimax_key_present: true`, `minimax_key_value_printed: false`. Both `process_minimax_api_key` and `user_minimax_api_key` are present; machine scope is empty (correct).
  - `(Get-Content -Raw .\opencode.json | ConvertFrom-Json) | Out-Null` -> `JSON_VALID`.

title: Add orchestrated agents invocation wrapper
description:
﻿## Context
Add a thin wrapper that lets Codex invoke MiniMax role workflows with minimal context by bead ID.

## Scope
- Provide a Windows-friendly launcher script.
- Enforce bead assignment and Markdown comment protocol around role invocations.
- Provide dry-run/status/help commands so setup can be validated without spending model tokens.
- Keep secrets in environment variables only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Wrapper can show status and validate required local tooling.
- Wrapper has documented command examples.
- Wrapper never prints API key values.

title: Make BeadBox detect bd on Windows
description:
﻿## Context
BeadBox v0.24.1 is installed, but its welcome screen says it cannot detect the `bd` command-line tool on PATH.

The shell can currently resolve `bd.cmd` at `C:\Users\alvil\AppData\Roaming\npm\bd.cmd`, so this is likely a GUI process PATH/startup detection issue rather than a missing Beads install.

## Required Outcome
BeadBox should be able to detect and use `bd` for this repository without requiring repeated manual troubleshooting.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Confirm the installed `bd` path and version.
- Ensure the user-level Windows PATH includes the directory that contains `bd.cmd`.
- Provide a repo-local, copyable BeadBox troubleshooting note if app restart is still required.
- Do not store secrets.
- Add all work notes as formatted Markdown comments on this bead.

title: Test databases and shadow evidence stores must stay separate
description: A PostgreSQL test run and a live shadow window shared a DSN; the fixtures deleted the whole window silently. pytest_configure now refuses to start against a database holding task_runtime_shadow rows, or one matching SHADOW_EVIDENCE_DATABASE_URL. Unreachable databases are not refused. Socket DSNs compare by socket directory. A separate socialhub_tests database is provisioned locally. DEPLOYMENT ACTION: export SHADOW_EVIDENCE_DATABASE_URL on the development host before the organic window, so the guard holds while the evidence table is still empty.

title: Planner coverage falls to 81% on conversational follow-ups
description: Single-turn commands plan at 100%. In multi-turn sessions 6 of 32 turns produced EMPTY_PLAN: 'Make it shorter', 'Just do LinkedIn', 'The LinkedIn one', 'Retry it', 'Add a line about the pricing change', 'Draft the first post'. The legacy runtime also derives no capability intent for these (its intent capability list is empty too), so both priors need conversation state neither of them reads. Only multi-turn traffic can surface this; the curated single-turn corpus reported 100% coverage. Canary must either exclude follow-up turns or the planner needs a conversational referent.

title: _needs_platform disagrees with what the legacy runtime attaches a platform to
description: EXECUTION_PLATFORM_MISMATCH fired on 14 of 26 evaluable turns in the multi-turn window. 11 are legacy=[linkedin] -> shadow=[]: the legacy runtime resolves and records a platform for drafting and retrieval work (content.copywriting.v1, artifact.delete.v1, content.get.v1, schedule.create.v1) while the planner's _needs_platform returns False for those capabilities. 2 are the reverse on analytics and publish. Not a safety issue - none produced a directional finding - but the two runtimes model 'which account does this touch' differently, and canary should either align them or record the difference as accepted.

title: The approval resume path is not shadow-observable
description: DevelopmentThreadService.resume() does not call the shadow bridge and writes no thread_command trace, so an accepted or rejected approval is neither a shadow-eligible turn nor in the denominator. Two of the sixteen required coverage categories are therefore structurally unreachable. Canary over command turns does not cover the approval entrypoint; extending the bridge to resume is a bridge-semantics change and needs its own gate.
notes:
CLOSED (2026-08-28, socialbackend 8bb24f1). resume() now reaches the same observation hook command() uses.
SHARED, NOT COPIED: _observe_step carries the mode gate, the legacy extraction, the classification, the sink and the failure isolation. Two copies would both still write records, so drift between them would be invisible. A test asserts one definition, two callers, one mode gate.
RESUME DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PLAN. The approval being settled belongs to a plan the command step already recorded; planning again would be a second logical execution of the same work. Shadow half = NOT_REPLANNED, which is not an error and is excluded from the agreement denominator.
IDENTITY DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: turn_id was shadow::<thread_id> - the THREAD, not the turn - so every turn in a conversation shared one identity. Invisible only because each evaluation scenario used a fresh thread. Scheme is now shadow::<entrypoint>::<thread_id>::<checkpoint_id>: server-derived, unique per authoritative step, idempotent. A missing checkpoint degrades to "unknown" rather than inventing uniqueness that would defeat the duplicate check.
The early returns in resume() are not observed because they change no state - which is also what makes a duplicate or stale resume write nothing.
A THIRD SETTLEMENT STATUS: an accepted approval settles as executed OR confirmed_dry_run ("Approval verified. Mutation is disabled, so nothing was scheduled."). It reads like success and is not one; widening the executed-mutation gate to accept it - which the word "confirmed" invites - would report mutations that never touched a provider. Documented at the gate and pinned by a test.
SCENARIOS, all over real HTTP: requested->accepted, requested->rejected, stale approval, duplicate resume, prior-turn residue. 19 tests. Discrimination: remove the hook -> 3 errors; make resume re-plan -> 2 failures; revert identity -> 3.
DEPLOYED EVIDENCE: 2 resume records in the window, 1 accepted 1 rejected, approval entrypoint covered.
close_reason: One shared observation hook now serves command() and resume(); accepted and rejected approvals are both observed, with a documented server-derived per-step identity scheme.

title: PLATFORM_MISMATCH is a comparison artefact, not a disagreement
description: 7 of 26 evaluable turns diverged on platform because the two sides measure different things: the legacy summary reports platforms the turn is ABOUT (from understanding.entities), the shadow reports platforms ATTACHED TO TASKS, and the planner deliberately attaches none to a drafting capability or to an ambiguous multi-platform turn. Not security-sensitive. Resolve by comparing like with like before canary; the comparison schema is frozen for G12.
notes:
CLOSED by splitting the concepts, not by filtering the divergence (2026-08-28, socialbackend 439fa3a).
THE BUG: legacy reported platforms the turn REFERRED TO; shadow reported platforms its tasks would ACT ON. Any turn mentioning two platforms while acting on one diverged by construction - 14 of 28 turns in the first deployed window, none of them a disagreement.
THE FIX: context_platforms and execution_platforms are now derived on BOTH sides and compared on their own axes. Execution platforms read only evidence about work - an executed operation's platform, the platform a pending approval targets, an artifact produced this turn, the platform the route resolver settled on. Nothing there reads understanding, which is the other concept.
RESULT in the multi-turn window: CONTEXT_PLATFORM_MISMATCH 2, EXECUTION_PLATFORM_MISMATCH 14. Context now agrees on 24 of 26, and the 14 sit on the axis where they mean something.
WHAT THE 14 ACTUALLY ARE, characterised rather than dismissed: 11 are legacy=[linkedin] -> shadow=[] on content.copywriting.v1, artifact.delete.v1, content.get.v1 and schedule.create.v1 - the legacy runtime attaches a platform to drafting and retrieval work, the planner's _needs_platform does not. 2 are the reverse on analytics and publish. Neither produced a directional finding, so none is a safety issue. Follow-up filed.
NOT VACUOUS: a genuine execution disagreement still fires, asserted by test, and a test reconstructs the original conflation to show it would still be caught.
close_reason: Platform comparison split into context and execution axes on both sides; the artefact disappeared because the semantics aligned, and both platform sets are still recorded and compared.

title: Shadow planner has no vocabulary for artifact lifecycle, retrieval or engagement turns
description: In the first evidence window 6 of 30 curated turns produced EMPTY_PLAN because understand_command_hybrid classified them as assistant_chat: delete a draft, edit a draft, post to X, show a schedule, correct a platform. The legacy runtime did real work on all six. These turns can never be compared, so canary must either exclude them or the vocabulary must be extended. INTENT_CAPABILITY and the understanding component are frozen for G12; this is the follow-up.
notes:
CLOSED by the route prior (2026-08-28, socialbackend a8f6f05).
TRACED, NOT GUESSED. scripts/planner_coverage_matrix.py follows 55 canonical commands through understanding -> INTENT_CAPABILITY -> map_understanding_to_capability_route -> catalogue -> TaskPlan and classifies which link broke.
RESULT: ZERO UNDERSTANDING_VOCABULARY_GAP. All 16 failures were CAPABILITY_MAPPING_GAP - the legacy route resolver knew the intended capability for every one of delete, edit, retrieve, list, reschedule, cancel, quote, repost, comment; the planner simply never asked it. The four named turns (delete / edit / post to X / show schedule) are all in that class.
FIX: the planner consults map_understanding_to_capability_route, the same pure resolver the legacy router routes from, whose own comment says specific verbs must win over coarse intent labels "so unsupported commands fail deterministically instead of falling through to assistant chat". No new agent, no change to understanding, and a FALLBACK not an override - the route rule returns one capability and would truncate a multi-intent plan.
COVERAGE 70.9% -> 100% (53 planned, 2 correctly refused), zero previously-planning commands changed.
SAFETY DEFECT THE WIDENING EXPOSED: is_consequential derived authorization from a name prefix and was wrong in BOTH directions once registry capabilities became nameable. artifact.duplicate.v1, artifact.restore.v1, content.adapt.v1 and comment.reply.v1 require confirmation and matched no prefix - the shadow would have recorded no approval where the legacy runtime demands one, which is SHADOW_LESS_RESTRICTIVE on a mutation. schedule.get.v1, publish.status.get.v1 and publish.failure.lookup.v1 are reads whose names start with a consequential prefix and would have produced a false approval mismatch every turn. It now reads the registry's confirmation contract - the same contract the legacy runtime routes approvals from - so the two cannot disagree. All 35 registry capabilities aligned, asserted by test.
DISCRIMINATION: override-instead-of-fallback -> 1 failure; prefix-only consequentiality -> 7.
close_reason: Planner coverage 70.9% -> 100% via the legacy runtime's own deterministic route resolver; no new agent and no change to understanding. Consequentiality now reads the registry's confirmation contract, closing a SHADOW_LESS_RESTRICTIVE class the widening would otherwise have opened.

title: G12-OPS.5 Schedule and execute shadow trace retention cleanup
description: purge_shadow_runs exists and is proven; no APScheduler job invokes it. Scheduling one is a deployment change.
notes:
EXECUTED AGAINST THE DEPLOYED DATABASE (2026-08-28). Still NOT SCHEDULED.
Measured on 30 real shadow rows in PostgreSQL: purge at now removed 0 (correct - nothing had aged out, and a purge that removes rows on the day they are written would be the failure); at +20d removed 6 agreements, leaving 24 divergence/error rows; at +200d removed the remaining 24. Throughout, 28 thread_command rows it did not write were untouched.
Windows: agreement 14d, divergent 90d, error 90d. Sanitization does not relax with the longer window.
REMAINING: no APScheduler job invokes purge_shadow_runs. Adding one is a deployment change and needs approval. Until then retention is manual and an unattended window will grow the table.
close_reason: purge_shadow_runs is now registered as a daily APScheduler job (03:30), scheduled unconditionally because the rows outlive the mode that wrote them; the preflight detects the registration rather than asserting it, and blocks a window if retention is not running.

title: Static gate for unresolved names and missing imports
description:
The G1A-9 defect: app/api/v1/auth_routes.py referenced safe_fields, provider_response_summary and a module-level logger that were never imported. Three runtime NameError paths, invisible to every behavioural test because those branches only run on failure.

tests/test_credential_logging.py has a hand-rolled AST guard for exactly that, written after the fact and scoped to the safe-logging boundary. A general undefined-name check subsumes it.

Objective: unresolved names and missing imports across app/. NOT a type-system rewrite, not strict mypy.

Prefer an existing tool. Ruff implements pyflakes F821 (undefined name) and F401 (unused import) and is a single dependency with no configuration burden; pyflakes alone is smaller still. Check what is already installed before adding anything, and report the dependency explicitly if one is required.

Acceptance: a test fails when a name is used without being bound; the existing safe-logging guard is kept or explicitly subsumed; no false positives on the current tree.
Rollback: delete the test.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend 397aebf. tests/test_static_name_resolution.py, 8 tests.
TOOLING FINDING, reported as required: NO linter is installed in this environment - no ruff, flake8, pyflakes, mypy or pylint - and adding a dependency is approval-gated by CLAUDE.md. Used stdlib symtable, which performs the same LEGB resolution the interpreter does. NO NEW DEPENDENCY. Adopting ruff later would subsume this file and that is the recommended eventual path.
VERIFIED AGAINST THE REAL DEFECT: deleting the safe_logging import from auth_routes made the gate fail with 7+ findings naming safe_fields and provider_response_summary in exactly the error-handler scopes G1A-9 hit. Restored.
FALSE-POSITIVE SURFACE is one case - __class__, implicitly bound by zero-argument super() - and the legal patterns that could plausibly trip it (late module-level binding, closures, comprehensions, conditional imports) are each asserted NOT to be flagged.
Scope held: unresolved names only, not type checking.
close_reason: Stdlib symtable gate landed, no new dependency, verified against the historical defect, no false positives on the current tree.

title: G1C.5: retire local password-recovery UI in favour of Clerk recovery
description:
Implements OPTION A from socialhub-ijn.3.3.7.

Evidence that this is the right direction and is mechanically safe, all from the repository:
- /login and /signup render Clerk SignIn/SignUp. There is no local login form (G1C.2).
- ApiManager.login was removed in G1C.3, so nothing can use a password even after resetting one.
- No email delivery exists in the backend at all, so the local flow was never functional AS RECOVERY. Removing it therefore removes no working capability - only the vulnerability tracked separately as the P0 disclosure bead.
- Clerk's SignIn component provides password recovery natively when password auth is enabled on the instance; when it is not, there is no password to recover and nothing is lost either way. The outcome does not depend on the remote setting, which is why this is not blocked on it.

Scope: socialUI only - delete app/forgot-password and app/reset-password, their ApiManager methods, and the /forgot-password link on the reset page.
NOT in scope: the backend endpoints. They stay for now; their removal is backend policy under ijn.3.3.7. With the P0 disclosure fixed and no email delivery, they are inert.

Acceptance: no route or client method for local password recovery; lint/build/tests green; a test asserts the symbols are gone.
Rollback: single revert.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialUI 6621b71. Deleted app/forgot-password, app/reset-password and ApiManager.forgotPassword/resetPassword. Two guard tests added to __tests__/auth_boundary.test.ts.
Decision rationale is repository evidence, not preference: Clerk owns /login and /signup; ApiManager.login was removed in G1C.3 so a reset password could not be used; and the backend has NO email delivery of any kind, so the flow was never functional as recovery. Removing it removed no working capability - only the disclosure tracked as ijn.3.13.
NOT blocked on remote Clerk settings: Clerk's SignIn provides recovery natively when password auth is enabled, and when it is not there is no password to recover. The outcome is the same either way.
Backend endpoints deliberately left in place - that is backend policy under ijn.3.3.7. With ijn.3.13 fixed and no delivery path they are inert.
VERIFICATION: lint 0, build 0 (9 routes, down from 11), tests 52 passed.
close_reason: Local password-recovery UI retired; Clerk owns recovery; lint/build/tests green.

title: DECISION: retire local password recovery, or restore local login
description:
DECISION REQUIRED FROM THE USER. Not decided in G1C.3, and deliberately not decided by inaction.

Current state, verified:
- /login and /signup render Clerk <SignIn>/<SignUp>. There is no local login form.
- /forgot-password and /reset-password ARE reachable and call ApiManager.forgotPassword / resetPassword, which hit the backend and set users.hashed_password.
- POST /auth/login verifies that password. Nothing in the UI calls it, and after G1C.3 ApiManager.login no longer exists.

So a user can complete a password reset and then have no way to use the password. The flow appears to work and achieves nothing.

OPTION A - retire local password recovery.
  Remove /forgot-password and /reset-password from socialUI; Clerk owns recovery.
  Backend endpoints stay for now (backend policy is a separate later decision).
  Smallest change, and it matches where the login UI already is.

OPTION B - intentionally restore local username/password login.
  Add a local login form, reinstate the removed thunks and ApiManager methods, and
  accept two session authorities permanently - with the identity-convergence
  question below becoming load-bearing rather than theoretical.

WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN: option B being chosen by accident, because the endpoints were
left in place and nobody looked. That is what this bead exists to prevent.

Note for whoever decides: option A does not remove the backend's local-JWT
verification path. get_current_user still falls back to decode_access_token, and
removing that is gated behind G1D per the G1C fence.
notes:
DECIDED 2026-08-27: OPTION A. Implemented as ijn.3.3.8 (socialUI 6621b71) on repository evidence - no email delivery exists, so local recovery was never functional; Clerk already owns login and signup; ApiManager.login was gone. Option B was not chosen by accident, which is what this bead existed to prevent.
Frontend half is done. The BACKEND half - whether /auth/forgot-password, /auth/reset-password, /auth/login and /auth/signup should exist at all - remains open here and is coupled to the local-JWT fallback decision fenced behind G1D.

title: Non-callback handlers still return detail=str(exc)
description:
Found while auditing ijn.3.7, deliberately NOT fixed there because that slice was fenced to the four provider callbacks.

The same publish-the-exception pattern remains at:
- app/api/v1/auth_routes.py:277 - POST /auth/google, 'Google authentication failed: {exc}'. Unauthenticated, and the closest analogue to the callbacks.
- app/api/v1/scheduled_post_routes.py:284,356 and saved_post_routes.py:272 - 500 with detail=str(e); authenticated, but these paths do write to the DB, which is where the IntegrityError class of leak comes from.
- app/api/v1/agent_thread_routes.py:120,163,199 and agent_debug_routes.py:315,351,378,397 - 409/422 detail=str(exc). These raise domain exceptions with deliberately user-facing messages, so they need reading one at a time rather than a blanket rewrite.

Acceptance: no response body contains SQL, bound parameters, stack traces or internal paths. Reuse app/api/v1/oauth_errors.py's split - exception to the log under a correlation id, stable sentence to the caller - rather than inventing a second convention.
Not started, and not blocking G1B.4.

Risk if deferred: moderate for /auth/google (unauthenticated), low elsewhere (authenticated callers, though a tenant still learns schema internals).
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): commits socialbackend 670c339 (code), 36ef249 (tests).

SWEEP: an AST scan for every HTTP response whose detail derives from a caught exception found 22 sites, not the 8 this bead listed. It also corrected the bead: the unauthenticated route is GET /auth/google/callback, not POST /auth/google. Extra sites the bead missed: media_routes 71/106 (Cloudinary), scheduled_post_routes 221 (LLM gateway), agent_debug_routes 115/634 (ValidationError). After: 9 sites remain, every one an explicit reviewed type.

GROUP A - sanitized (11): google callback, google/instagram/linkedin/x login-url, scheduled-post create, bulk and content-generation, saved-post save, media upload and image generation, thread rename fallback, thread command. Fixed sentence + 16-hex correlation id; exception to the log, redacted and capped at 500 chars.

GROUP B - preserved under an explicit contract: ProviderConfigurationError (503, names setting KEYS), ProviderInputError (400, the instagram method list), ThreadValidationError (422), SchedulingExecutionError / ActionExecutionError (409), EvaluationRunConflict / EvaluationRunReportUnavailable (409), pydantic ValidationError (422, projected).

TRUST NOW ATTACHES TO A TYPE. Every route previously caught a broad builtin - except Exception, except ValueError, except RuntimeError - which handed publish rights to anything on the call stack. New UserFacingError marker with three subclasses; user_facing_detail matches the EXACT type, so a subclass falls through to sanitization instead of inheriting the trust (asserted per provider).

HIGHEST PRIORITY, GET /auth/google/callback: unauthenticated AND it commits a User row. fb_user_id is unique, so a real UNIQUE violation published the INSERT, its column list and its bound parameters. The test reproduces this end to end with no injected exception - seed an account already holding google_<sub>, then drive the callback - and asserts the value is absent from the response but present in the log.

ONE BOUNDARY, NOT TWO: app/core/error_boundary.py now holds the mechanism and app/api/v1/oauth_errors.py delegates to it, keeping the OAuth status and wording. The ijn.3.7 suite still passes unchanged in behaviour.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND WHILE CLASSIFYING, both fixed:
1. agent_debug_routes returned exc.errors() whole. That carries "input" - the ENTIRE dict under validation, not just the offending field - and "ctx", which holds the live exception object. It also never rendered: a datetime in "input" is not JSON-serializable, so the model-validator branch returned an unhandled 500 instead of a 422. Projected to loc/msg/type, the shape FastAPI's own handler uses.
2. The google and linkedin configuration messages named "fb_agent/.env" - an internal deployment path - to an unauthenticated caller. Removed; the setting keys stay because they are the actionable part.

DEAD DISCLOSURE CHANNEL: except RuntimeError in POST /threads/{id}/commands had no legitimate producer (nothing under service.command raises a bare RuntimeError) while SecurityConfigurationError IS a RuntimeError. The 409 is kept so the external contract does not move; the message is not.

STATIC GUARDS, all fail closed:
- user-facing classes are raised only with literal messages. First run found TWO REAL violations: SchedulingExecutionError interpolated the platform name (now literal) and ActionExecutionError forwards snapshot["safe_message"].
- the safe_message forward is permitted only because a paired guard proves every safe_message in app/ is either a developer-written literal or a forward of one - they all originate in failure_recovery's fixed classification table. A third test asserts that guard is not vacuous.
- no except clause naming a broad builtin may publish its exception (the sweep, kept as a regression guard).
- UserFacingError has no unreviewed subclasses.

TESTS tests/test_error_disclosure_boundary.py, 26 tests. DISCRIMINATION: 16 of 26 fail against pre-fix code. The 10 that pass are Group B preservation tests (which SHOULD pass both ways - that is the point) plus unit and meta tests of the new helper and guards. Pre-fix log output captured during the discrimination run also confirmed the credential finding was real, not theoretical: "api_key=SENTINEL-..." was written to the log by the old logger.error(f"...{e}").

VERIFICATION: focused error-disclosure + OAuth 195 passed; auth/security regression 152 passed; full suite SQLite 786 passed / 14 skipped; full suite PostgreSQL 16.2 800 passed / 0 failed.

DEPLOYMENT: none. No migration, no config, no dependency. Rollback is a revert of 670c339.

FRONTEND: not verified. Any client that matched on "Failed to retrieve access token from Instagram: ..." or on 500 detail text would now see the generic sentence, but a grep of socialUI found no such matching - it renders the provider's own error_msg query parameter.
close_reason: 22 sites audited and classified; 11 infrastructure sites sanitized behind one shared boundary; domain messages preserved under an exact-type contract with mechanical guards; two further defects fixed (unserializable 422, .env path); 26 tests, 16 discriminating; full suite green on SQLite and PostgreSQL.

title: Callback error responses leak internal exception detail
description:
Problem: the provider callbacks end with 'except Exception as e: raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e))'. Observed during G1B.3: a database IntegrityError surfaced the full SQL statement, column names and bound parameter values in the HTTP response body.
This is the same class as the Instagram login-url handler fixed in G1A-8, which now returns only the exception class name.
NOT a tenant leak - G1B.3's consume path returns a uniform safe message before any provider work - but it exposes schema internals to an unauthenticated caller and can echo provider payloads.
Scope: the four callback handlers' terminal except blocks in app/api/v1/auth_routes.py, plus the equivalent in x_service.authenticate_and_sync.
Acceptance: no callback response body contains SQL, column names, bound parameters or a provider payload; the exception class and a correlation id are acceptable.
Tests: force an IntegrityError and a provider error, assert the response carries neither SQL nor payload.
Rollback: single-file revert.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): commits socialbackend 0faf82d (code), b0e806b (tests).

INVARIANT: exception -> safe structured log + generic externally stable OAuth error. One direction only.

NEW BOUNDARY app/api/v1/oauth_errors.py: OAUTH_CALLBACK_FAILURE_STATUS=400, one stable sentence, plus a 16-hex correlation id. Chose a correlation id over the exception class name the bead allowed: the class name is an internal detail that is neither stable for the client nor useful to the user, while still narrowing an attacker's guesses. sanitized_exception_message runs sanitize_text (whole-string drop on any credential match) then caps at 500 chars.

ALL FOUR CALLBACKS AUDITED, not only the IntegrityError path:
- facebook: terminal detail=str(e) replaced.
- instagram: terminal detail=str(e), PLUS two branches interpolating raw provider payloads - "Failed to retrieve access token from Instagram: {token_data}" and "Failed to fetch Instagram user info: {user_info}". Both now log an allowlist summary and return a fixed sentence.
- linkedin: terminal detail=str(e); added the missing token-exchange log summary; the non-fatal organizations branch logged the raw provider error, which can carry the request URL and therefore the token (ijn.3.1.12) - now redacted.
- x: BOTH "except ValueError -> str(e)" and "except Exception -> str(e)". ValueError is no longer special-cased: treating it as user-safe is exactly how the raw token-exchange body reached the response. x_service.authenticate_and_sync also stops interpolating token_data and profile_data into its ValueErrors.

HTTPException is now re-raised rather than reshaped. Side effect: the G1B.3 uniform state message arrives clean instead of as "400: This connection link..." - Starlette's HTTPException.__str__ prefixes the status, so the old generic handler was re-wrapping it.

TESTS tests/test_oauth_callback_error_disclosure.py, 66 tests. Five fault classes x four providers: real database IntegrityError (produced by an actual duplicate insert, so its str carries the real INSERT, real column names and a sentinel bound parameter), provider HTTPError with the token in the URL, ConnectionError with internal host and deploy path, a service embedding the raw body in its exception, and an unexpected RuntimeError.
Two sentinel classes on purpose: SQL/host/path/body sentinels must be ABSENT from the response but PRESENT in the log - without that second half a handler that simply swallowed the error would pass everything else. The credential sentinel must be absent from both, and the log must show [REDACTED].
Also asserted: no response contains INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/Traceback/File "/IntegrityError/sqlalchemy/psycopg/sqlite3; the detail prefix is identical across all 20 provider x fault combinations while all 20 correlation ids differ; the ref joins to a log line carrying provider, stage and error_type; G1B.3 consumption semantics unchanged (a failed callback still consumes, still writes no account rows, is still not replayable).

DISCRIMINATION: 53 of 66 fail against pre-fix code. The 13 that pass are accounted for and none is a disclosure assertion: 4 unit tests of the new helper (the module exists in both arms, so it cannot discriminate), 8 semantic guards that SHOULD pass pre-fix because they assert G1B.3 behaviour was preserved, and the facebook payload test (facebook never interpolated its payload - a guard, not a fix).

KNOCK-ON: test_modules_using_the_safe_logging_boundary_actually_import_it (the G1A-9 guard) failed on the new module because it only asked whether the MODULE defined "logger" - a false positive for a helper taking one as a parameter. Rewritten scope-aware. The first rewrite was wrong in the other direction (ast.walk descends into nested function bodies, crediting a function-local binding to the module, which would have re-admitted the original G1A-9 bug); the added meta-test caught it. Both directions are now asserted by tests.

VERIFICATION: focused OAuth 169 passed; auth/security regression 150 passed; full suite SQLite 760 passed / 14 skipped; full suite PostgreSQL 16.2 774 passed / 0 failed.

FRONTEND: none needed. socialUI renders the provider's own error_msg query parameter, not our detail; no code matches on the old strings.

DEPLOYMENT: none. No migration, no config, no dependency. Rollback is a revert of 0faf82d.

NOT FIXED HERE, filed as socialhub-ijn.3.8: the same detail=str(exc) pattern outside the callbacks, including the unauthenticated POST /auth/google.
close_reason: All four callbacks and x_service sanitized; exception to the log under a correlation id, stable generic sentence to the caller; 66 tests across 5 fault classes x 4 providers, 53 discriminating; full suite green on SQLite and PostgreSQL.

title: DECISION: no global ENVIRONMENT indicator for production-only policy
description:
Problem: G1A-7 needed to distinguish production-like from local, and no reliable indicator exists. LANGSMITH_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT is LangSmith-specific and would fail OPEN if tracing were disabled. Inventing a committed config contract was out of scope, so G1A-7 avoided needing one: forbidden secrets are rejected unconditionally, and a missing secret disables the local token path rather than blocking startup.
What is still not enforceable without an indicator: 'a production deployment must not START with a missing secret'. Today a production box with no SECRET_KEY starts Clerk-only, which is safe but silent.
Scope: decide whether to add ENVIRONMENT/APP_ENV, and which policies become production-only.
Acceptance: either the key is approved, added and consumed by security_config, or the decision is recorded as deliberately declined with rationale.
REQUIRES APPROVAL: adds a committed configuration contract and a deployment .env change.

title: Clerk audience verification is disabled (verify_aud=False)
description:
Problem: clerk_auth_service passes options={'verify_aud': False}. A token minted for a different Clerk audience would still validate provided the issuer and signature match. Left untouched in G1A-8 because that slice was scoped to algorithms and enabling audience checks changes Clerk verification behaviour.
Scope: clerk_auth_service audience handling plus a CLERK_AUDIENCE setting.
Out of scope: algorithms (done in G1A-8); OAuth state (G1B).
Acceptance: when an audience is configured, a token with a mismatched aud is rejected; when unset, behaviour is unchanged so no deployment breaks.
Tests: matching aud accepted; mismatched aud rejected; unset audience preserves current behaviour.
Rollback: single-file revert.
REQUIRES APPROVAL: adds a configuration key. Verify against the real Clerk token shape before enabling by default.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend e5b5ba8 (code), de9d8b9 (tests).

TRACED FIRST, AND THE BEAD'S PREMISE NEEDED CORRECTING.
- EXPECTED ISSUER: settings.CLERK_ISSUER, already enforced when set. Unchanged.
- IS aud IN REPOSITORY TEST TOKENS? No. Neither 'aud' nor 'azp' appears anywhere in app/ or tests/ before this slice.
- WHAT SHOULD SOCIALHUB ACCEPT? A Clerk session token carries NO aud claim by default. The documented default set is azp, exp, fva, iat, iss, jti, nbf, sid, sub, v, pla, fea, sts; aud exists only if the instance defines a JWT template adding one (clerk.com/docs/backend-requests/resources/session-tokens). Enforcing verify_aud unconditionally would reject every token this application receives.
- DOES THE FRONTEND REQUEST A TEMPLATE? No. app/components/AuthTokenBridge.tsx calls getToken() with no argument, so it receives the default token.
- STILL UNKNOWN IN PRODUCTION: whether any JWT template defines an audience, and the production frontend origin. Neither is knowable from this repository.

IMPLEMENTED, both config-gated and both unset by default so behaviour is unchanged:
- CLERK_AUDIENCE enforces aud when set. Setting it means REQUIRING the claim.
- CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES enforces azp against an origin allowlist. THIS IS THE SUBSTANTIVE HALF: azp is present in every default token and Clerk explicitly recommends checking it - 'validate that the azp claim equals any of your known origins permitted to generate those tokens' - because otherwise an app on another subdomain of the same root domain can mint valid sessions for this one, and CSRF becomes possible. No wildcard honoured.

THE AUDIENCE CHECK IS HAND-ROLLED, not delegated to python-jose, because its verify_aud was MEASURED and found unsuitable twice: it ACCEPTS a token with no aud while an audience is configured (making the setting decorative - an attacker just omits the claim), and it refuses a list of audiences outright ('audience must be a string or None'). Both were caught by tests before shipping. RFC 7519 permits aud as string or array; both accepted.

Expected values come from server configuration only - never the token, a header, or anything a caller influences. A test feeds a token carrying its own CLERK_AUDIENCE/audience claims and asserts it is still refused.

TESTS tests/test_clerk_audience_policy.py, 16, with real RSA keys and real signatures. Issuer and signature behaviour asserted unchanged. DISCRIMINATION: 16 of 16 fail pre-fix (as setup errors, because the settings keys do not exist).

CODE READY, DEPLOYMENT OPERATIONALLY GATED: adding either key is a production configuration change requiring approval, and the correct values are the two unknowns above.
close_reason: Audience and authorized-party verification implemented, both config-gated and unset by default; the substantive azp check added per Clerk's own guidance; 16 tests, all discriminating. Production values remain unknown so enabling stays operationally gated.

title: Dedicated ADMIN_EMAILS setting for the internal/admin boundary
description:
Problem: app/api/v1/admin_auth.py (added in G1A-3) reuses AGENT_DEBUG_ADMIN_EMAILS because introducing a config key requires approval and was out of slice scope. That couples the analytics all-tenant sync boundary to a setting named for agent debugging, so widening one silently widens the other.
Scope: a dedicated ADMIN_EMAILS setting in app/core/config.py plus admin_auth.py.
Out of scope: changing who is an admin; any production env change.
Dependencies: none.
Acceptance: require_admin_user reads a dedicated setting, still fails closed on an empty allowlist, still refuses the '*' wildcard, and AGENT_DEBUG_ADMIN_EMAILS no longer grants all-tenant sync.
Tests: allowlist empty -> 403; non-listed user -> 403; listed user -> 200; '*' -> 403.
Rollback: single-file revert.
Docs: verification environment env table.
REQUIRES APPROVAL: adding a configuration key.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend 0585ef2 (code), c3e4383 (tests).
ADMIN_EMAILS is now its own setting. require_admin_user reads only it; require_agent_debug_access reads only AGENT_DEBUG_ADMIN_EMAILS.
The sharpest form of the old coupling: the debug gate honours '*', and the only thing stopping that wildcard from making everyone a system administrator was admin_auth filtering the string out by hand.
FAILS CLOSED: empty allowlist denies everyone; a '*' entry is DROPPED rather than expanded, so a wildcard configuration yields an EMPTY allowlist and denies everyone.
INDEPENDENCE ASSERTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. One direction alone is the trap - showing debug does not grant admin while quietly letting admin grant debug just moves the coupling. A mechanical test checks each boundary reads only its own setting, because the original coupling was invisible: both functions looked correct in isolation and the shared setting was one identifier.
TESTS tests/test_admin_authorization_boundary.py, 15, behavioural on the real all-tenant analytics route POST /api/v1/analytics/sync (403 for a debug admin, not-403 for a system admin, 401 anonymous) plus the allowlist contract. DISCRIMINATION: 15 of 15 fail pre-fix (setup errors, ADMIN_EMAILS does not exist on the settings model).
NO RBAC REDESIGN and no change to who is an administrator: ADMIN_EMAILS is unset until an operator sets it. Setting it in production is a configuration change requiring approval.
close_reason: Dedicated ADMIN_EMAILS boundary; fails closed; no wildcard; independence asserted in both directions; 15 tests, all discriminating.

title: G4I.8: Structured option and card answers
description:
Answer by option id from a UI card. Same interaction, same resume path as free text.
Scope: backend contract for structured answers.
Out of scope: the UI itself (G11).
Dependencies: G4I.3.
acceptance_criteria: An option-id answer and the equivalent free-text answer produce identical task state.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): socialbackend db5587e (code), b5d434a (tests). app/agent_graph/interaction_input.py, 36 tests.
ONE CONTRACT FOR EVERY TRANSPORT. The organising test runs the same intent as chat text, a button, a card and a voice transcript and asserts the four InteractionAnswers are EQUAL. If that holds, the runtime provably cannot behave differently per input mode, because it never sees the difference. RawAnswer.source is telemetry only and a second test asserts no decision reads it.
answered_by IS SERVER-DERIVED: a parameter, never a field on the raw payload - RawAnswer has no identity field at all. A hostile card payload carrying answered_by/user_id/sub is normalized with the caller's id regardless. Same defect class as _state_user_id in G1B.
FREE TEXT resolves in three tiers - exact, unique prefix, unique substring - each exhausted before the next, so a value matching one option exactly is never lost to another that merely contains it. Zero or multiple matches raise AmbiguousAnswer WITH the candidates rather than guessing; picking for the user is how the wrong page gets published.
APPROVAL VOCABULARY IS SMALL AND EXPLICIT. Five forms of qualified or unclear yes are refused, including 'yes, but change the caption' - a qualified yes is not a yes.
CONNECTION LIFECYCLE: offers ids rather than free text so 'I connected it' and 'never mind' are distinguishable without guessing; a completed connection resumes the SAME task with blocked_reason cleared; a cancelled one resolves without connecting; a stale connection answer is refused. Connecting is explicitly NOT approving - a task resumed that way still meets the approval boundary, asserted.
TASK CONTEXT IS CARRIED BY task_id ALONE. A test asserts no goal, plan or capability field exists on InteractionRequest, so nothing copied into an interaction can drift out of sync with the plan.
No frontend change.
close_reason: Structured option and card answers normalize to the same contract as text and voice; identity stays server-derived.

title: G4.10: Remove old routing after shadow validation
description:
The ONLY bead permitted to delete old routing. Blocked until shadow/canary passes.
Scope: deletion plus manifest.
Out of scope: anything before G12 passes.
Dependencies: G4.9, G12.
acceptance_criteria: Every removed function names its replacement in a deletion manifest. Frontend and scheduler no longer reach the old path. Rollback procedure exists and has been rehearsed.

title: G1A-4: Secure saved-post routes
description:
Problem: POST /saved-posts/save and GET /all_saved are unauthenticated and select tenant by user_fb_id.
Scope: app/api/v1/saved_post_routes.py.
Out of scope: draft model changes.
Dependencies: G0.5.
Tests: cross-tenant read/write denied.
Runtime evidence: route audit rows.
Rollback: single-file revert.
Docs: audit section B.2.
acceptance_criteria: Both routes authenticated; user_fb_id ignored for authorization; cross-tenant access returns 404.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-26): commit socialbackend 4021f5f; tests 416e87b.
- Both routes authenticated; anonymous asserts 401 exactly.
- user_fb_id retained for FE compatibility, deprecated in the OpenAPI schema, ignored for authorization; _get_user removed.
- Cross-tenant list isolation asserted by id set, not substring.
- ADDITIONAL DEFECT FOUND IN SCOPE: create resolved page, LinkedIn and X accounts with no ownership filter, so a caller could save a draft against another tenant's page. Same confused-deputy shape as G1A-1/G1A-2. Now scoped via _owned_page/_owned_linkedin/_owned_x. The negative test sends an otherwise-valid payload including topics so its 404 can only come from the ownership check, not from business validation, and re-reads the DB to prove no row was written.
- Positive owner control kept separate. Data-minimization test on the listing response.

title: G14: Production cutover
description:
Scope: final switch to the single architecture.
Out of scope: any step before G12 passes.
Dependencies: G12, G13.
Acceptance: all release gates in docs/EVALUATION_GATES.md met with evidence.
Tests required: full regression + production smoke.
