title: G12: Shadow and canary
description:
Scope: compare legacy vs canonical decision, account, capability, policy, generated content and mutation proposal without duplicating side effects; then canary internal accounts.
Out of scope: executing duplicate external mutations — strictly forbidden in shadow mode.
Dependencies: G9, G11.
Acceptance: divergence report clean over the agreed window.
Tests required: shadow harness tests.
Runtime evidence: comparison log.
Rollback: shadow is read-only.
Documentation impact: evaluation gates.

title: G11: Conversational frontend
description:
Problem: frontend calls legacy unauthenticated endpoints and two nonexistent ones (/autopilot/pending-approvals, /autopilot/approve/{id}).
Scope: move to canonical command endpoints; account ids become resource references only.
Out of scope: cosmetic refactor of oversized files before characterization tests exist.
Dependencies: G6.
Acceptance: no frontend call reaches a legacy mutation route; no 404 endpoints.
Tests required: frontend regression + integration.
Runtime evidence: network trace.
Rollback: per-endpoint.
Documentation impact: frontend section.
notes:

title: WFSC-bead-5: bd CLI parallel-create race condition (parent-context prefix/priority loss)
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout discovered a repeatable tooling-friction flaw during verification of bead socialhub-v8g.22.1 (2026-07-13). Workflow Engineer filed 37 GAP-K/GAP-L follow-up beads per Codex-Orchestrator Option C. The first batch was 5 parallel `bd create` invocations. 4 of those 5 beads got auto-generated short-prefix IDs (socialhub-cai, socialhub-khd, socialhub-771, socialhub-2bo) instead of the expected socialhub-v8g.22.{7,8,9,10} sequence, AND the same 4 beads got priority 2 (P2 default) instead of priority 1 (P1 requested). The remaining 32 beads were then filed SEQUENTIALLY to avoid the race. Total corrective work: 4 `bd rename` invocations plus 4 `bd update --priority 1` invocations. The flaw is a parent-context race in bd CLI parallel-create mode.

## Actual Task
Author `.orchestrated-agents/docs/bd-cli-quirks.md` (modeled on the existing `.orchestrated-agents/docs/beadbox-windows.md`) that documents the bd CLI parallel-create race condition. The doc must: (1) describe the failure mode (parent-context lookup loses the parent prefix in parallel invocations, falling back to a default-prefix random ID; priority similarly defaults to P2), (2) recommend the workaround: file beads SEQUENTIALLY when parent-child context matters, OR if `bd create --batch-file <jsonl>` is supported use a single batched invocation, (3) provide a sanity-check command the filing role runs after a parallel batch (rg the resulting beads and compare prefixes). Add a CROSS-LINK from `.orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md` Workflow-Engineer-Filing subsection to the new quirks doc.

## Why This Is Useful
Without this documentation: every future multi-bead filing turn will re-discover the parallel-race, lose prefix + priority context, require 2 corrective invocations per affected bead (proportional to 4N for an N-bead parallel batch), and risk shipping malformed bead IDs to the audit trail. The audit trail will then contain id-mismatch corrections that future readers must reconstruct. With the documentation: future Workflow Engineer turns either file sequentially OR use a documented batch primitive, avoiding the race and the corrective invocations entirely.

## Flaw
The bd CLI `bd create --parent <parent-id>` honors parent-child context for prefix inference + label inheritance when run sequentially. In PARALLEL invocations the parent-lookup step loses context (race condition between parallel bd-engine processes resolving the parent prefix), falling back to the database default prefix (random short hash) + default priority (P2). The race is SILENT -- bd does not warn; the issue only surfaces when `bd list --json` shows wrong prefixes. Workflow Engineer 2026-07-13 11:02Z closing summary correctly identified this in the socialhub-v8g.22.1 turn and mitigated by switching to sequential filing, but the framework now has no documented guard against future parallel filings encountering the same race.

## Impact
- Audit-trail pollution: 4 beads in the socialhub-v8g.22.1 filing required `bd rename` corrective calls; the filing-announce comment claimed `socialhub-v8g.22.{6..10}` IDs but on-disk state showed `socialhub-{cai,khd,771,2bo}` until rename.
- Priority drift: 4 beads got P2 instead of the requested P1; correctable via `bd update --priority 1` but only if caught before close.
- Hidden multi-arg loss: parallel invocations may ALSO drop --labels, --assignee, --deps, --silent flags under race; only prefix + priority were caught in the socialhub-v8g.22.1 incident.
- Future parallel batching blocked: until the race is fixed upstream OR a batch primitive is documented, Workflow Engineers are incentivized to file sequentially, increasing filing time linearly with bead count.
- Cross-bead ID drift: the match between the matrix's stable IDs (GAP-K-NNN) and the bd engine's sequence IDs (socialhub-v8g.22.{7..42}) depends on correct sequencing; parallel races break the match.

## Proposed Improvement
1. Create `.orchestrated-agents/docs/bd-cli-quirks.md`:
   - Section "Parallel-create race condition": describes prefix + priority race; cite the socialhub-v8g.22.1 2026-07-13 evidence.
   - Section "Recommended patterns": (a) SEQUENTIAL filing when parent-context matters; (b) BATCH-FILE via `bd create --batch-file <jsonl>` if bd CLI supports it (verify with `bd create --help`).
   - Section "Sanity-check after parallel batch": provide exact rg commands and expected patterns.
2. Amend `.orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md` Mandatory First Actions subsection to add a new step for multi-bead filing turns: "If creating >1 bead in a single turn, file SEQUENTIALLY OR run sanity-check verification after parallel batch (see bd-cli-quirks.md)."
3. Amend `.orchestrated-agents/templates/scout-bead.md` Acceptance Criteria to include: "If Workflow Engineer filed >1 bead in a single turn, verify all bead IDs begin with the parent-prefix and all priorities match the matrix; flag any anomaly."
4. Optionally propose `bd create --batch-file <jsonl>` and `bd create --parallel-safe` to the bd CLI maintainers (out of scope for socialhub; reference only).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role-selection debate is performed for this improvement bead.
- Human-input gate runs before implementation.
- Workflow Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial review confirms the bd-cli-quirks.md documentation is complete and the sanity-check command correctly detects the race condition.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and tracked.
- The amended scout-bead template correctly catches the race when re-applied to the socialhub-v8g.22.1 2026-07-13 evidence.
- A future Workflow Engineer filing turn applies the sequential-or-batch pattern and produces zero corrective `bd rename` or `bd update --priority` invocations.
- Documentation Reviewer confirms the new quirks doc is linked from bead-protocol.md and CONTEXT.md.

## References
- socialhub-v8g.22.1 Workflow Engineer closing summary at 2026-07-13 11:02:21Z, section "Notable filing-pass friction encountered and mitigated".
- socialhub-v8g.22.5 (WFSC-bead-4: Long-comment multi-part workaround) -- adjacent tooling-friction issue (similar `--file` pattern used as PE mitigation), but separate scope.
- `.orchestrated-agents/docs/beadbox-windows.md` -- existing ops doc the new bd-cli-quirks.md can be modeled after.
- `.orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md` -- amendment target.
- `.orchestrated-agents/templates/scout-bead.md` -- amendment target for sanity-check rule.
- `bd create --help` output (this turn): confirms `--body-file`, `--silent`, `--parent` flags; `--batch-file` is NOT currently in the help output so the batch-primitive recommendation is conditional.

## Stable ID
WFSC-bead-5 (parent to the existing WFSC-bead-1..4 numbering on socialhub-v8g.22.2 through socialhub-v8g.22.5).

Amend .orchestrated-agents/roles/workflow-scout.md to explicitly state that Workflow Scout files workflow-improvement beads using the scout-bead.md template, NOT implementation beads. Implementation beads (one per GAP-K-NNN, GAP-K-IMP-NNN, GAP-K-DEF-NNN, GAP-L-NNN) are filed by the appropriate maker role per the matrix Section K target artifacts (Workflow Engineer for workflow files, Maker Engineer for product code, etc.). The .orchestrated-agents/roles/workflow-scout.md charter says 'You do not edit files. You find process flaws and create workflow-improvement beads.' title: N3: Probe-comment audit-trail gate in bead-protocol.md
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a bead-protocol gap. Across socialhub-v8g.4, five probe-class comments have been observed: (1) 17:53 Role Selector probe x3 (short, no structured headings), (2) 18:01 HQF probe, (3) 20:55 Adversarial Reviewer probe, (4) 22:01 Workflow Scout tool-mechanic probe (this turn, self-acknowledged in the 22:02 substantive comment). The bead-protocol.md No Test Comments rule (per .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md) forbids probe / placeholder / scratch comments on real beads, but the rule is not enforced by any wrapper pre-flight or bd-side check. Comments can be posted without the required six headings (Commentor / Step+Subtask / Status / Findings / Evidence / Required Next Action) or the minimum-length that a meaningful Markdown work record implies. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 first named N3 as a follow-up; the 22:01 Workflow Scout probe is direct evidence that the gap is open.

## Actual Task
Add a Probe-Comment Gate rule to .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md. The rule must: (a) require every bd comment invocation to include the six required headings per .orchestrated-agents/templates/comment.md (Commentor, Step+Subtask, Status, Findings, Evidence, Required Next Action), (b) require a minimum-length (e.g., the comment body must be \u003e= 200 characters or \u003e= 8 lines after the role author line), (c) reject comments that match probe-token patterns (e.g., 'TEST', 'Line 1', 'placeholder', 'scratch', 'scratch text', 'experiment', single-status-only comments). Enforce the rule at wrapper pre-flight (per F3) by extending oa.ps1 Run-Role to validate the comment body before passing it to bd. Reference N3 from bead-protocol.md as the source of the rule.

## Why This Is Useful
Probe comments on real beads pollute the audit trail. Future readers cannot distinguish a probe from a real work record without parsing prose for probe-token patterns or checking for the mandatory headings. The 5 observed probes on socialhub-v8g.4 demonstrate the gap. Closing N3 produces a hard-enforced rule that future probe comments are rejected at the wrapper pre-flight before being posted.

## Flaw
The current rule is documented (bead-protocol.md mentions no test/probe/placeholder/scratch comments) but not enforced. The wrapper pre-flight at oa.ps1 Run-Role does not check comment body shape. bd does not check comment body shape. The rule is purely aspirational. The 5 observed probes on socialhub-v8g.4 are direct evidence that the rule does not work as written.

## Impact
If not fixed, every future evaluation bead will accumulate probe-class comments in the audit trail. The audit-trail integrity guarantee erodes. Closing N3 produces a hard-enforced rule that future probes are rejected. The audit trail stays clean.

## Proposed Improvement
Extend bead-protocol.md with a Probe-Comment Gate rule (per the actual-task description). Extend oa.ps1 Test-WrapperSelf at lines 212-271 to include a comment-shape validation step that asserts any new comment on a bead matches the bead-protocol.md shape. Add a sibling pre-commit hook at .beads/hooks/pre-commit that re-checks the same condition (in case the wrapper is bypassed or the comment is posted via a direct bd invocation). Update Documentation Reviewer docs to reflect the new mandatory shape (the shape is already documented in .orchestrated-agents/templates/comment.md lines 1-11; F11+N3 just add the enforcement). The probe-class exceptions (exception-fallback comments per F11) are explicitly whitelisted because they include the Why-This-Was-Necessary heading.

title: F8: Workflow Engineer prompt-miss and role-routing anomaly pattern
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a recurring prompt-miss / routing-anomaly pattern. Across socialhub-v8g.4, Workflow Engineer was invoked 5 rounds (Round-1 at 18:05 closure, Round-2 at 20:43, Round-3 at 20:50, Round-4 Docs patch at 20:52, Round-5 no-op at 21:49). The Codex-Orchestrator 21:53 comment claims 'I tried to route the fix through Workflow Engineer twice; the role ignored the explicit infrastructure-fix instruction'. The 2026-07-12 21:36 + 21:38 comments were authored with PE as the underlying actor but content authored as Documentation Reviewer - the routing-vs-content split is the same anomaly. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 first named F8 as a residual follow-up; Workflow Engineer 21:49 self-flagged the pattern as F8 candidate.

## Actual Task
Add detection and handling rules for the Workflow Engineer prompt-miss / role-routing anomaly pattern. The rules must: (a) detect a prompt-miss (a PE round with no editor commands or with a no-op comment that does not assign the bead to a new role), (b) detect a routing-anomaly (a PE round whose comment content was authored by a different role), (c) escalate to the Codex-Orchestrator exception-fallback path per F7 after two consecutive prompt-misses, (d) close the loop properly when PE has no remaining scoped work (return a 'no-op handoff' comment, reassign to the next role in the convergence loop).

## Why This Is Useful
Prompt-misses can degrade the adversarial loop's effectiveness. Routing-anomalies break the audit-trail invariant (the BEADS_ACTOR must match the role that did the work). The 21:36/21:38/21:49/21:53 events demonstrate that without an explicit detection rule, the framework will silently accumulate the same anomalies on every evaluation bead. F8 closes the loop by making the detection explicit in the role-prompt and the workflow documentation.

## Flaw
There is no detection rule for prompt-miss or routing-anomaly. The 21:36 + 21:38 comments are syntactically valid Markdown work records but the actor tag does not match the comment content. The 21:49 comment is a no-op handoff that did not produce any editor commands because no Workflow Engineer work remained. The 21:53 Codex-Orchestrator invocation was triggered after 2 PE prompt-misses, but the rule that 2 is the threshold and that the exception-fallback can ONLY do docs was implicit. F7 captures the docs-only rule; F8 captures the prompt-miss detection rule.

## Impact
If not fixed, every future evaluation bead will accumulate prompt-miss / routing-anomaly comments in the audit trail. The audit-trail integrity guarantee erodes. The exception-fallback path becomes more likely to be invoked because the framework cannot self-diagnose the prompt-miss. Eventually, the framework will produce false evidence (workflow-engineer comments authored as a different role) that downstream readers cannot trust.

## Proposed Improvement
Add .orchestrated-agents/workflows/workflow-engineer-miss-detection.md as a new workflow file. The file must define: PROMPT-MISS SIGNATURE (round with no editor commands or no-op comment without bead reassignment); ROUTING-ANOMALY SIGNATURE (round whose comment content does not match the assigned role); ESCALATION RULE (two consecutive prompt-misses trigger Codex-Orchestrator exception-fallback per F7); LOOP-CLOSURE RULE (after adversarial convergence, if PE has no remaining scoped work, return a no-op handoff and reassign to the next adversarial role); ROLE-PROMPT CLARIFICATION (workflow-engineer.md role-prompt explicitly recognizes the no-op handoff pattern and the role-routing anomaly pattern). Update workflow-engineer.md role-prompt with these explicit instructions so future PE rounds recognize the pattern and self-correct.

Update workflow-engineer.md role-prompt with these signatures as explicit instructions.

title: F4: Per-role permission smoke-test scaffolding for every oa-* agent
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a missing automated verification step for OpenCode permission blocks. The Adversarial Reviewer Part 2 (2026-07-12 20:29) on socialhub-v8g.4 ran an empirical bounded-glob proof ( d show socialhub-v8g.4 vs  d show socialhub-v8g.4 --json) to demonstrate the declaration-order precedence rule. This proof is a manual, one-time test. Every future permission change to opencode.json must re-run a comparable proof, but no scaffolding exists. A2/A4 round-1 fixes (Workflow Engineer Round-1) added permission grants without re-running the empirical proof against the new rules. The Codex-Orchestrator 21:53 exception-fallback patch widened  d ** permissions across 9 agents (lines 52-54, 77-79, 129-131, 154-156, 179-181, 209-211, 231-233, 253-255, 283-285) without any smoke-test to confirm no destructive subcommand regression.

## Actual Task
Add a permissions-smoke-test.ps1 script (and POSIX equivalent in the future oa.sh per F2) under .orchestrated-agents/tests/permissions/ that loads opencode.json, iterates over every oa-* agent, and asserts: (1) every llow rule actually allows the matched command; (2) every deny rule actually denies the matched command; (3) declaration order matters (a more-specific rule before a less-specific rule overrides; a less-specific rule before a more-specific rule is shadowed). The smoke-test must be exercisable by oa.cmd status --smoke-test and exit non-zero on any failure. The exit-code propagation requirement from F3 applies.

## Why This Is Useful
The Round-1/-2 audit cycle took 4.5 hours and 19 comments to converge partly because permission behavior could not be re-verified automatically. Every future permission change must be re-proven. The Codex-Orchestrator 21:53 patch demonstrated that a permission widening can happen without an adversarial review because no smoke-test existed to even surface the change. With F4 in place, every permission edit produces a re-runnable assertion matrix that the QA Strategist must approve. The framework's confidence in its own permission blocks becomes evidence-backed, not assumption-backed.

## Flaw
There is no automated way to re-prove the bounded-glob empirical test on socialhub-v8g.4. The test was carried out by Adversarial Reviewer Part 2 manually. Future permission edits rely on operator code review alone, which cannot replicate the empirical proof at scale. Workflow Engineer's Round-1 permission edits were accepted by Adversarial Reviewer Part 1 via code inspection, which is weaker than behavioral proof.

## Impact
If not fixed, every future permission change is review-only. Workflow Engineer can ship a permission edit that LOOKS correct but BEHAVES incorrectly (e.g., a denylist pattern that does not match a destructive phrasing like git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit). Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 noted this as residual prompt-trust risk. The Codex-Orchestrator 21:53 patch added 9 multi-arg allow rules without a smoke-test, demonstrating the same gap. Closing F4 produces the only durable defense: a re-runnable behavioral assertion matrix.

## Proposed Improvement
Add .orchestrated-agents/tests/permissions/permissions-smoke-test.ps1 (and F2-port POSIX equivalent). The script uses Get-Content -Raw opencode.json | ConvertFrom-Json to load the config, iterates over gent.PSObject.Properties, and for each oa-* agent emits assertions like: 'agent oa-adversarial-reviewer: bash.allow.bd * - prove  d show socialhub-v8g.4 exits 0', 'agent oa-maker-engineer: bash.deny.git commit* - prove git commit -m test is blocked', 'agent oa-maker-engineer: bash.deny.rm -rf * - prove m -rf /tmp/foo is blocked (with a tmpdir cleanup)'. The script must handle three-family  d.exe / bd.cmd / bd resolution matching Resolve-Exe at oa.ps1 lines 25-34. The script must emit a structured JSON summary so the QA Strategist can review the matrix in a comment. Reference the smoke-test invocation from .orchestrated-agents/workflows/pre-flight-check.md (which F3 creates) so every CI run invokes it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role Selector debate runs on this follow-up bead before any implementation.
- Security Privacy Reviewer reviews the smoke-test for safe destructive-command proof patterns (the script must NOT actually execute destructive commands during the proof; it must use --dry-run or scripted verification).
- Workflow Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial Reviewer confirms the smoke-test catches the empirical bounded-glob case from socialhub-v8g.4 and at least one additional round-trip case per agent.
- QA Strategist runs the smoke-test against the current opencode.json (with the 21:53 multi-arg widening) and confirms every assertion passes; the matrix is appended to the smoke-test output and shared in the bead comment trail.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and discoverable from epic socialhub-v8g.

The script must be runnable via oa.cmd status extended mode and exit non-zero on any failure. Output is structured so QA Strategist can review the assert matrix from the comment trail.

title: F3: Wrapper pre-flight --auto failure visibility (exit code propagation)
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a wrapper pre-flight visibility gap. Test-WrapperSelf (oa.ps1 lines 212-271) catches parse errors and missing shim, but the Run-Role abort at lines 313-316 throws silently. With --auto, OpenCode's interactive confirmation bypass leaves the abort invisible to the operator. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 named F3 as a documented residual follow-up on socialhub-v8g.4.

## Actual Task
Make the wrapper pre-flight failure mode user-visible when --auto is in effect. The current 	hrow at oa.ps1:315 inside Run-Role should produce a non-zero exit code AND a human-readable error message that surfaces before OpenCode spawns. Show-Status must also exit non-zero when Test-WrapperSelf fails so that oa.cmd status can be used as a CI-style guardrail. The same visibility requirement must apply to the future POSIX oa.sh wrapper (F2).

## Why This Is Useful
A silently aborted role invocation under --auto would surface as 'OpenCode ran but produced no actionable output, the bead was never assigned, and the next role in the loop gets routed to a previous-assignee bead'. The visible-failure pattern catches (a) syntax errors introduced by Workflow Engineer edits, (b) config changes that break Test-WrapperSelf, (c) permission changes that silently fail. Without exit-code propagation, every CI integration must grep stderr for an unrecognized error string - a fragile contract. Closing F3 produces a stable contract for wrapper pre-flight verification.

## Flaw
Run-Role at oa.ps1 lines 313-316 throws 'Wrapper self-check did not return ok. Aborting role invocation.' but does not exit the OpenCode child process, and the throw is captured by OpenCode's --auto handler as a soft error. The operator sees 'opencode ran', the bead is never assigned, and the next role invocation starts against a stale-assignee state. The pattern is not human-detectable without parsing stderr. Show-Status at lines 273-302 returns a JSON object that includes wrapper_self_check: ok or wrapper_self_check: fail: <reason> but does NOT propagate the failure as an exit code - so oa.cmd status always exits 0 even when the wrapper is broken.

## Impact
If not fixed, every wrapper pre-flight failure is silent. Future framework changes that break Test-WrapperSelf will produce 'bead appears stuck' situations that take operator eyes-on to diagnose. The CI integration story for the framework is fragile (must grep stderr) and the wrapper cannot be used as a smoke-test gate at the top of automation scripts. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 confirmed F3 is a real residual risk that the Round-1 A11 mitigation did NOT close.

## Proposed Improvement
Modify oa.ps1 Run-Role (lines 304-381) so that when Test-WrapperSelf returns != ok: (1) Write-Warning prints the wrapper_self_check fail reason, (2) exit 1 is returned BEFORE spawning OpenCode, (3) the bead is NOT assigned by the wrapper (matches the bead-protocol.md invariant 'the wrapper does NOT assign the bead'). Modify Show-Status (lines 273-302) so that if Test-WrapperSelf throws, the script exits 1 after emitting the JSON error object (so the JSON contract is preserved for tooling AND the exit code signals failure). For the future oa.sh POSIX wrapper (F2), apply the equivalent exit-1 propagation. Add a .orchestrated-agents/workflows/pre-flight-check.md rule that says 'every CI integration MUST assert oa.cmd status exits 0 before invoking any role' so the contract is codified.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role Selector debate runs on this follow-up bead before any implementation.
- Security Privacy Reviewer signs off on the exit-code contract (specifically that an exit-1 from a wrapper self-check is NOT a secret leak).
- Workflow Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial Reviewer confirms the improved behavior would have surfaced the A11 mitigation gap on socialhub-v8g.4.
- QA Strategist writes a smoke-test that intentionally breaks Test-WrapperSelf and asserts the correct exit code and human-readable message.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and discoverable from epic socialhub-v8g.
design: In Run-Role (oa.ps1 lines 304-381), replace the silent throw at line 315 with an explicit Write-Warning + Write-Error + exit 1 sequence. Add a parallel exit-1 path to Show-Status (lines 273-302) so that oa.cmd status always exits 1 if wrapper_self_check fails. Mirror these exit behaviors in the future oa.sh POSIX wrapper (per F2). The visibility gap exists because --auto bypasses OpenCode's interactive confirmation, so a silent abort is invisible to the operator.
acceptance_criteria: Test-WrapperSelf failure exits non-zero from oa.cmd run and oa.cmd status; --auto invocation propagates the exit code to the parent shell; oa.cmd emits a human-visible warning before aborting even with --auto

Wired into both Show-Status and Run-Role. Sufficient as a first-line guardrail; F3 captures the --auto failure-visibility follow-up.'

title: F1: Verdict-ownership rule for evaluation-bead acceptance criterion 6 (A10)
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a missing governance rule while auditing socialhub-v8g.4. Every evaluation bead carries an acceptance criterion 6 ('ready / not-ready for product-code tasks'), but no rule names which role owns that verdict. The verdict becomes orphaned at convergence time, blocking bead closure. Only the orphaning itself is observable, not the criterion check that would have prevented it.

## Actual Task
Add a 'Verdict Owner' rule to .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md (and optionally .orchestrated-agents/templates/role-selection.md) that names the role responsible for the acceptance criterion 6 verdict on every evaluation bead. The rule must default to Workflow Scout unless Role Selector explicitly assigns an alternate at intake time.

## Why This Is Useful
Four roles (Adversarial Reviewer, QA Strategist, Security Privacy Reviewer, Documentation Reviewer) agreed at 21:23/21:28/21:31/21:38 on socialhub-v8g.4 that the 'ready / not-ready for product-code tasks' verdict had no owner, and consistently attributed F1 to Workflow Scout. Workflow Engineer at 21:49 also handed off without naming a verdict owner. Without the rule, every future evaluation bead will hit the same gap and stall at the same convergence point. Adding the rule unblocks evaluation-bead closure across the entire framework.

## Flaw
The evaluation-bead template (inherited from .orchestrated-agents/templates/scout-bead.md Acceptance Criteria section) lists five role-level acceptance criteria but does NOT name a Verdict Owner for criterion 6. The role-selection template and bead-protocol.md are silent on the question. When the adversarial loop converges, no role is on the hook for the criterion 6 verdict, and Workflow Scout is implicitly assuming ownership by default - an unacceptable implicit design choice for a framework that requires explicit evidence-backed approvals.

## Impact
If not fixed, every evaluation bead will (a) require an implicit Workflow Scout verdict at closure, (b) fail named-evidence convergence because no role claims ownership, and (c) accumulate conflicting comments about who should have produced the verdict. The framework's appetite for evaluation beads will degrade as each one stalls. socialhub-v8g.4 is the first evaluation bead to hit this gap; future evaluations like socialhub-v8g.5+ will inherit it.

## Proposed Improvement
Extend .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md with a 'Verdict Owner' section under 'Acceptance Criteria'. The section must state: (1) every evaluation bead declares a Verdict Owner in its acceptance criteria; (2) default Verdict Owner = Workflow Scout; (3) Role Selector may assign an alternate at intake; (4) convergence requires the Verdict Owner to post an explicit Approved or Not-Approved comment on the criterion 6 verdict before the bead can close. Update the role-selection template to remind Role Selector to set the Verdict Owner explicitly. Update scout-bead.md Acceptance Criteria template to include a 'Verdict Owner (criterion 6)' line. Backward compatibility: existing evaluation beads that lack the line default to Workflow Scout ownership at next convergence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role Selector debate runs on this follow-up bead before any implementation.
- Human-input gate runs and resolves any ambiguity about ownership (e.g., should the default be Workflow Scout, or another role).
- Workflow Engineer implements the rule only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial Reviewer confirms the improved rule would have unblocked the A10 verdict on socialhub-v8g.4.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and discoverable from epic socialhub-v8g.
design: Add an explicit 'Verdict Owner' line to the evaluation-bead template (or to bead-protocol.md under 'Acceptance Criteria') that names the role responsible for closing criterion 6 ('ready / not-ready for product-code tasks'). Default verdict owner = Workflow Scout unless an explicit alternate is named by Role Selector. Convergence rule: without a Verdict Owner line, the bead cannot close.

title: bd list tree mode does not terminate when a child depends on its epic's sibling
description:
`bd list` (tree mode, the default) never terminates on this database. It follows parent edges AND dependency edges, so a child of an epic that depends on a sibling of that epic makes the walk revisit the epic forever.
NOT CAUSED BY THE G12 WORK and not a data cycle: bd itself rejects true cycles, and bd ready / bd show / bd stats / bd blocked are all consistent. Reproduced from socialhub-00s.9.2, created 2026-08-26, which is a child of epic 00s.9 and depends on 00s.1 and 00s.2 - both children of 00s, the parent of 00s.9. The ids repeated 28 times each in the first 400 lines of output are all in that subtree.
WORKAROUND: `bd list --flat` completes normally and prints parent and blocked-by inline. Use it, or bd ready / bd show.
The dependency graph is correct and should not be flattened to satisfy a renderer.

title: Architecture prose states a loop bound that would abort legitimate plans
description:
Found while implementing G4.4's bound in app/agent_graph/task_progress.py.

implementation-plan/G2_AGENT_LOOP_CONTRACT.md states the termination bound as:
    iterations <= task_count * max_attempts + 1

That figure ignores the block/resume pair. A task that blocks on an interaction and is later resumed consumes THREE iterations per attempt (start, block, resume), not one. A loop configured with the prose bound would abort a legitimate plan that used any interaction - which is every plan containing a consequential capability.

The implementation derives and guarantees instead:
    sum(3 * task.max_attempts + 1 for task in plan.tasks) + 1

max_iterations() carries the derivation in its docstring, and a test asserts the derived bound exceeds the prose figure so the two cannot silently converge again.

ACTION: correct the prose in G2_AGENT_LOOP_CONTRACT.md to match, or record why the two differ. Filed separately rather than editing the accepted architecture document mid-implementation.

Not urgent: the code is correct and no loop is wired yet. It matters before G4.6 configures a real budget.
notes:
EVIDENCE (2026-08-27): root commit 6ad9ff5 (docs), socialbackend 30c5129 (runtime consumes the canonical bound).
WHY T x R + 1 WAS INVALID: it reasoned that every iteration terminates a task, consumes an attempt, or suspends. Blocking and resuming are TWO FURTHER ITERATIONS that terminate nothing and consume no attempt - the suspend is legitimate progress and so is the resume, and neither appears in T x R. The bound was not merely tight; it was SMALLER THAN THE SHORTEST LEGAL EXECUTION of any plan containing a consequential capability, so a loop configured with it would abort every publish.
NOT A NUMBER SWAP: the document now shows the CALL - max_iterations(plan) - and states the runtime must use it, because a duplicated bound drifts from the state machine it describes, which is exactly what happened here. agent_loop.run_agent_loop imports max_iterations and defaults to it; a test asserts run.budget == max_iterations(plan).
The budget is overridable, for two stated reasons: shadow mode may want a tighter ceiling, and IterationBudgetExhausted is otherwise UNREACHABLE in correct operation because the loop charges an attempt per execution - a backstop nobody can trigger is a backstop nobody has tested.
close_reason: Prose corrected with the reason recorded; the runtime consumes max_iterations(plan) rather than restating a formula.

title: Move provider tokens out of POST form bodies to Authorization headers
description:

  facebook_service publish_post, edit_post, reply_comment, publish_photo_post

title: Retire the Clerk email-convergence fallback once every signable account has a clerk_user_id
description:
Follow-up to socialhub-ijn.3.11, which hardened the email fallback rather than removing it.

The fallback is the ONLY path by which a pre-Clerk local account can ever be linked to a Clerk session. It cannot be deleted while such accounts exist. Once none do, deleting it removes the account-takeover class permanently rather than gating it.

MEASURABLE CRITERION:
    SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE clerk_user_id IS NULL;
Rows that can still sign in must all carry a clerk_user_id. Rows that cannot - abandoned Facebook-only rows with no email, say - do not block this; the query needs narrowing to signable accounts before it is used as a gate.

Sequence:
1. Measure the count in production (needs approved DB access, currently unavailable).
2. If non-zero, decide whether those accounts are dormant or need an outreach/link flow.
3. When zero: delete the  branch and the surrounding evidence check, so a Clerk session can ONLY resolve by clerk_user_id.
4. The convergence tests become tests that convergence does NOT happen.

Blocked on production data access, not on code.

Also outstanding from ijn.3.11: confirm CLERK_SECRET_KEY is set in production, or that the token template carries email_verified. Without one of the two, existing users cannot link at all after 0c1a4aa - they are locked out rather than taken over. That is the correct direction but it must be verified before deploying.

title: Stale G1B artifacts in socialUI: removed flag name and legacy OAuth state format
description:
Found during the G1C.2 trace. Both are dead or ignored; neither changes behaviour; neither was fixed, to keep the G1C slice read-only.

1. lib/apiManager.ts:523-528 - the oauthStartHeaders docstring still explains itself in terms of OAUTH_SERVER_STATE_ENABLED, a backend flag DELETED in G1B.3. It now describes a world that does not exist, and it says 'sending the token unconditionally is safe while the flag is off' - which reads as optional when it is now mandatory.

2. app/agent/components/oauthActions.ts:21-28 - still builds oauthState = '<prefix>_user_<userId>', the exact client-supplied format that G1B.3 made non-authoritative. The backend accepts it as client_state and explicitly discards it (auth_routes _issue_oauth_state does '_ = client_state'), so it is harmless, but it is the shape of the vulnerability that was fixed and will mislead the next reader.
   The surrounding code also fetches getCurrentUser purely to build that string, so removing the string removes a network round-trip on every connect.

Acceptance: no socialUI source references OAUTH_SERVER_STATE_ENABLED or constructs a user-id-bearing OAuth state.
Tests: existing frontend suite; add one asserting the connect flow sends no user id in state.
Do together with G1C.3 step 1, since both touch the same files.
notes: DONE in socialUI e15eb01 as part of G1C.3. The OAUTH_SERVER_STATE_ENABLED docstring is gone. Client OAuth state construction removed at FOUR sites, not the one this bead recorded: oauthActions.ts plus fetchLoginUrl, fetchLinkedInLoginUrl and fetchXLoginUrl in agentSlice. The state parameter was also removed from the four authorization-URL methods so it cannot come back for compatibility, and a test asserts both. The getCurrentUser round-trip that existed only to build the state string went with it.
close_reason: Both stale artifacts removed and guarded by tests.

title: users.reset_token is stored in plaintext and looked up by value
description:
Found during the G1B.4 inventory and deliberately excluded from it.

users.reset_token is a password-reset credential stored in plaintext. It cannot simply join the G1B.4 credential store: it is indexed and looked up BY VALUE, so encrypting it with a random nonce breaks the lookup.

Options, in rough order of preference:
1. Store a SHA-256 of the token and look up by digest, exactly as oauth_transactions.state_hash already does. The emailed token stays the only copy.
2. Deterministic encryption - defeats much of the point and needs its own key handling.
3. Leave it, and rely on the short expiry.

Option 1 is the same pattern G1B.1 already established, so it is mostly mechanical.

Not urgent: the token is short-lived and single-purpose. Recorded so the exclusion is a decision rather than an oversight.

title: WFSC-bead-4: Long-comment multi-part workaround (bd comment --file <path>) and bead-protocol.md amendment
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a repeatable setup-friction flaw on bead socialhub-v8g.22.1. Every substantive review on this bead had to be split into 'Part N of M' comments because the bash tool command-size limit truncated long  d comment <id> <text> invocations. PE v3 4 parts (23:19Z), AR v3 3 parts (22:54Z), AR v4 3 parts (23:47-48Z), SPR v4 2 parts (2026-07-13 00:06-07Z), PE v4 2 parts (23:36+23:42Z). The pattern is consistent and predictable but the framework has no documented workaround.

## Actual Task
Document the  d comment --file <path> (or  d comment socialhub-v8g.22.1 --file <path>) pattern as the canonical workaround for bash tool command-size limit when posting substantive reviews to Beads. Amend .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md to recommend this pattern for substantive reviews exceeding ~2000 lines. Add a smoke-test step to .orchestrated-agents/docs/beadbox-windows.md or a new .orchestrated-agents/docs/bd-cli-quirks.md explaining the --file pattern.

## Why This Is Useful
Without this documentation: every future substantive review will re-discover the truncation issue and re-invent the multi-part workaround (with risk of inconsistent split points, lost continuation context, and self-critique addenda required when the split is uneven). With the documentation: future roles will know to write the canonical comment to a file (e.g., .orchestrated-agents/logs/<bead-id>-<role>-<step>.md) and use  d comment --file <path> to post it as a single atomic comment. The multi-part pattern becomes a fallback for the rare cases where --file does not work (e.g., offline environments without write access to the .orchestrated-agents/ tree).

## Flaw
The bead-protocol.md mandatory comment format is documented (lines 18-20, mandatory Markdown format). The bd CLI's  d comment <id> <text> invocation form is implied but not explicitly recommended. The  d comment --file <path> form is supported by the bd CLI (verified by PE on socialhub-v8g.22.1 v4 turn at 23:36Z:  d comment socialhub-v8g.22.1 --file .orchestrated-agents/logs/v4-part1-subtask.md returned Comment added to socialhub-v8g.22.1) but is not documented in bead-protocol.md. Roles default to inline  d comment <id> <long-text> which hits the bash tool command-size limit.

## Impact
- Comment-split inconsistency: PE v3 split at Section boundaries, AR v3 split at evidence section, AR v4 split at Part 1/2/3 boundaries, SPR v4 split at Section K vs evidence section. Each role made up its own split logic.
- Self-critique addenda required: every multi-part comment requires a 'Continued in Part N' footer + a 'Required Next Action' on the last part. Adds ~5% comment overhead.
- Reviewer confusion: when reading the bead thread, the reader must mentally merge Parts 1+2+3 to understand the review. DR + SPR already noted this; future roles will repeat the confusion.
- Lost context: some parts were truncated (the bash tool truncated lines >2000 chars, e.g., PE v3 Part 4 line 1279 was truncated mid-sentence). The truncation was repaired by later comment-addenda but the truncation itself is a tool-friction issue.

## Proposed Improvement
A single Workflow Engineer documentation pass:
1. Amend .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md:
   - Add a new section '## Long-Comment Multi-Part Workaround' that recommends the  d comment <bead-id> --file <path> pattern for substantive reviews exceeding ~2000 lines.
   - Specify the canonical file path convention: .orchestrated-agents/logs/<bead-id>-<role>-<step>-<ISO-timestamp>.md (e.g., socialhub-v8g.22.1-workflow-engineer-v3-part1-2026-07-12T23-19Z.md).
   - Specify that the file is the canonical Markdown source; the bd comment is just a copy that links to it. The file lives in logs/ (audit-trail location per WFSC-bead-2).
   - Document the multi-part fallback: when --file does not work (e.g., sandboxed read-only environment), split the canonical content into 'Part N of M' comments and reference each part from the previous one ('Continued in Part N+1'). Each part must end with the required 'Continued in Part N+1' footer.
2. Add a new file .orchestrated-agents/docs/bd-cli-quirks.md (or amend beadbox-windows.md) that lists known bd CLI quirks:
   -  d comment <id> <text> is bounded by shell command-size limit (~2000 lines / ~100KB).
   -  d comment <id> --file <path> is unbounded and is the recommended form for substantive comments.
   -  d exposes no comment remove / edit / classify subcommand; comments are append-only.
   -  d exposes no comment probe flag; tooling-validation residue must be disclosed manually in the canonical comment.
3. Update .orchestrated-agents/README.md (if exists) or .orchestrated-agents/docs/CONTEXT.md Current Local Setup section to reference the new docs file.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role-selection debate is performed for this improvement bead.
- Human-input gate runs before implementation.
- Workflow Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial review confirms the workaround is unambiguous and the documentation is complete (Documentation Reviewer verifies).
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and tracked.
- A future substantive review uses the --file pattern and produces a single canonical comment instead of N multi-part comments. (Test: a future Workflow Engineer or Adversarial Reviewer substantive review applies the new pattern.)
- Documentation Reviewer confirms the new docs file or amendment is consistent with the existing CONTEXT.md Current Local Setup section.

## References
- socialhub-v8g.22.1 PE v4 Part 1 comment at 2026-07-12 23:36Z:  d comment --file invocation form verified working.
- socialhub-v8g.22.1 multi-part comments: PE v3 4 parts, AR v3 3 parts, AR v4 3 parts, SPR v4 2 parts, PE v4 2 parts -- total ~14 multi-part comments where ~4 --file invocations would have sufficed.
- .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md line 18: the comment format rule that the new workaround complements.
- .orchestrated-agents/docs/beadbox-windows.md: the existing ops doc that the new bd-cli-quirks.md can be modeled after.

title: F12: Wrapper prompt template parity with new Test-WrapperSelf role-map
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a documentation/permission parity gap. The 2026-07-12 21:53 Codex-Orchestrator patch widened bash permission grants to allow multi-arg bd ** / bd.cmd ** / bd.exe ** across 9 agents in opencode.json (lines 52-54, 77-79, 129-131, 154-156, 179-181, 209-211, 231-233, 253-255, 283-285). The Run-Role prompt template at oa.ps1 lines 336-364 still teaches new roles to use bare bd show \u003cId\u003e, bd update \u003cId\u003e --assignee \u003cRole\u003e, bd comment \u003cId\u003e --stdin (single-arg patterns that were the norm before the 21:53 widening). The prompt template has not been revised to use multi-arg patterns that the new permission grants now permit, and does not teach the new role-agent verification capability added by Get-AgentName at lines 48-76 and the role-map validation at lines 237-263. Future roles will not learn that they can use bd show \u003cId\u003e --json for structured output, or that they can verify a role display name maps to a configured agent via Test-WrapperSelf.

## Actual Task
Revise oa.ps1 Run-Role prompt template at lines 336-364 to teach new roles: (a) use bd show \u003cId\u003e --json (multi-arg) instead of bare bd show \u003cId\u003e for structured output, (b) verify role display names against the role-agent map (Get-AgentName at lines 48-76) before claiming a role is available, (c) discover parent beads and dependencies via bd list --parent \u003cbead-id\u003e + bd dep list \u003cbead-id\u003e (replacing the current inability to programmatically traverse the bead hierarchy). The prompt must remain a complete, runnable example for new roles (so a new role can copy-paste it as the first command of the round).

## Why This Is Useful
The 21:53 patch updated the framework's permission grants to allow multi-arg bd invocations, but did not update the prompt template that teaches new roles how to use the grants. Without the prompt template update, future roles will not know they can use --json for structured output, role-agent verification, or dep traversal. The prompt template is the documentation that new roles actually read. F12 closes that gap so the documentation matches the capability.

## Flaw
The prompt template at oa.ps1 lines 336-364 is now under-spec'd relative to the new permission state. It still teaches single-arg examples even though the new permission grants allow multi-arg. Future roles reading the template will not learn the full capability. This is the same documentation-rot pattern as F6 (hardcoded count) but applied to a different file (oa.ps1 prompt template instead of CONTEXT.md).

## Impact
If not fixed, every new role invocation will be under-instructed. Roles will use the bare single-arg examples even when they could use multi-arg for richer output. The framework capability grows but the documentation stays frozen. Closing F12 keeps the prompt template in sync with the actual capability of the framework.

## Proposed Improvement
Revise the prompt template at oa.ps1 lines 336-364 to: (a) use bd show \u003cId\u003e --json as the first example (multi-arg) so new roles learn the structured output pattern, (b) include a role-agent verification example (e.g., 'verify the assigned role maps to a configured agent by checking bd role-agent \u003cRoleName\u003e or running Test-WrapperSelf'), (c) include a parent/dependency discovery example so new roles can navigate the bead hierarchy. Also update the wrapper status output at oa.ps1:265-270 to include a 'wrapper_prompt_template_version' field, so future changes to the prompt template are version-tracked. Documentation Reviewer must re-confirm the new wording matches the intent.

Reference the new functions Get-AgentName (lines 48-76) and the role-map validation in Test-WrapperSelf (lines 237-263).

title: F6: Replace hardcoded comment count at CONTEXT.md:197 with CLI verification
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a documentation-rot risk. The .orchestrated-agents/docs/CONTEXT.md line at approximately 197 (the BeadBox Context section, cross-referencing beadbox-windows.md) contained the literal phrase '21 inline comments' to describe the socialhub-v8g.4 bead. The count will go stale the moment any role posts a new comment - and the Workflow Scout 22:01 probe-comment + the Workflow Scout 22:02 substantive comment have already invalidated the literal. Documentation Reviewer 21:38 explicitly acknowledged F6 as a Workflow Scout follow-up: 'The replacement should be the verification CLI command (bd comments \u003cbead-id\u003e --json) and the success criterion (non-empty array), not a literal count.'

## Actual Task
Rewrite CONTEXT.md line 197 to remove the literal count. Replace with a verification instruction that uses the live CLI: 'verify bd comments socialhub-v8g.4 --json returns a non-empty array'. The text may keep its surrounding prose but the specific integer '21' must be removed. Confirm with rg that no other documented file in .orchestrated-agents/ contains a similar hardcoded inline-count.

## Why This Is Useful
Documentation-rot is one of the most common audit-trail defects: a literal number goes stale, future readers trust the number, and the discrepancy is not caught until a metadata review. Replacing the literal with a verifiable CLI command makes the documentation true-by-construction (any reader can run the command and verify the current count matches the description, which is the array being non-empty). The same pattern can be applied to F5's dates, F7's version numbers, F12's example command - any place a hardcoded value can be replaced by a live verification.

## Flaw
CONTEXT.md line 197 says '21 inline comments' as a current-state assertion. It is a snapshot at the moment of writing; the moment anything changes, the assertion is false. The same anti-pattern is in: beadbox-windows.md line 45 ('local bd v1.0.4 downgrade' - this is a version, also a rot risk if a future contributor bumps bd) and CONTEXT.md line 197 itself. There is no fix policy. The text is descriptive prose that is implicitly authoritative but explicitly mutable.

## Impact
If not fixed, the documentation will become a lie as the audit trail grows. The count '21' is already stale at the time of writing this Workflow Scout comment. Beadbox-windows.md line 45 will go stale the moment bd is re-upgraded. Future readers (and future Workflow Scouts) will misread the current state. Documentation Reviewer 21:38 confirmed the rot risk and recommended the CLI-verification replacement; this follow-up beads the implementation.

## Proposed Improvement
Replace '21 inline comments' with the verification instruction: 'verify with bd comments socialhub-v8g.4 --json that the returned JSON array is non-empty (audit-trail integrity)'. The replacement is a fixed string, not a snapshot, so it never goes stale. Apply the same pattern to any other hardcoded count or version in .orchestrated-agents/docs/ and the corresponding comment trails. Optionally add a style-rule to bead-protocol.md stating: 'Documentation must not contain literal counts or version numbers when those values can be replaced with live CLI verifications.'
design: Replace the literal count with a fixed-string reference to the verification CLI command and the success criterion. The text '21 inline comments' must become 'non-empty array from bd comments socialhub-v8g.4 --json' or equivalent. The relocation of the count to a structured audit-trail command removes the rot risk entirely.
acceptance_criteria: CONTEXT.md:197 rewritten to reference bd comments socialhub-v8g.4 --json non-empty-array as the success criterion; specific integer count removed; Documentation Reviewer re-confirms the new wording matches Documentation Reviewer 21:38 acceptance matrix
notes: Discovered during socialhub-v8g.4 audit. CONTEXT.md:197 contained the literal count '21 inline comments' which will go stale the moment any role posts a comment. Documentation Reviewer 21:38 explicitly ack'd F6 as Workflow Scout scope.

title: F5: bd v1.0.4 version-pin as a tracked decision bead
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a process gap. The bd CLI was downgraded to v1.0.4 to work around an upstream BeadBox comment-body bug (issue 27 at github.com/beadbox/beadbox/issues/27). The downgrade is documented in .orchestrated-agents/docs/beadbox-windows.md lines 45-50 and .orchestrated-agents/docs/CONTEXT.md line 197. But the upgrade/rollback decision trail is not recorded as its own bead. The doc describes WHAT was done, not WHO decided it, WHEN, or WHY. Future agents may upgrade bd back without context and re-introduce the same upstream bug.

## Actual Task
Record the bd v1.0.4 version-pin as a tracked decision bead. The decision body must include: (1) DATE the downgrade was applied; (2) SYMPTOM that triggered it (missing comment bodies in BeadBox UI; CLI confirmed comments existed; BeadBox log confirmed the UI bug); (3) PREVIOUS version (whatever bd was installed before the downgrade); (4) CURRENT version (bd v1.0.4); (5) RATIONALE for staying on v1.0.4 (upstream BeadBox issue 27 is open AND no bd release has fixed the comment-body regression); (6) EXIT CRITERION for re-upgrading (upstream BeadBox issue 27 is closed AND bd upstream releases a comment-body-safe version); (7) OWNER of the decision (Codex-Orchestrator or this role). Cross-link the decision record from beadbox-windows.md and CONTEXT.md sections so future readers find it.

## Why This Is Useful
A future contributor who runs bd upgrade latest will not know there is a pinned version below a known-bad upstream release. They will install the broken version, see the symptom, and lose hours debugging it. Recording the decision as a tracked bead makes the version constraint visible via bd ready and bd show. The exit criterion also makes the upgrade path explicit. Documentation Reviewer 21:38 confirmed the gap.

## Flaw
The downgrade is a one-line note in beadbox-windows.md and CONTEXT.md. There is no decision bead recording the upgrade constraint, the exit criterion, the date, or the owner. Anyone running bd upgrade today would silently roll back the fix. There is no automated check that bd is on v1.0.4 (the wrapper resolves bd via Resolve-Exe at oa.ps1:38 from env PATH, which allows any version to satisfy the lookup).

## Impact
If not fixed, the framework is one bd upgrade away from the comment-body regression. The downstream impact: every role comments would silently fail to surface in BeadBox UI; operators would see what looks like a complete failure of the adversarial loop. Many hours of debugging would follow.

## Proposed Improvement
File a decision bead under epic socialhub-v8g titled bd v1.0.4 version-pin (downgrade from upstream buggy release). Body uses the standard decision-shape: Context (the bug), Decision (pin to v1.0.4), Consequences (positive: works around the bug; negative: future contributors may not know). Cross-link from beadbox-windows.md:50 and CONTEXT.md:197. Add a wrapper-side guard at oa.ps1 Run-Role pre-flight (lines 304-381) that asserts the bd version is exactly v1.0.4 and exits non-zero (per F3 exit-code propagation) if it is not. Optional: pin bd v1.0.4 in opencode.json provider block by hardcoding the version, but that requires upstream patch - flag as F5-exit-criterion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role Selector debate runs on this follow-up bead before any implementation.
- Workflow Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial Reviewer confirms the decision record would have prevented the bd-upgrade regression risk.
- QA Strategist verifies the wrapper-side guardrail (if implemented) exits non-zero on a non-v1.0.4 bd install.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and discoverable from epic socialhub-v8g.
design: Use bd create --type decision (or chore, depending on Beads type registry) to record the upgrade/rollback/downgrade trail. The decision body must include: (1) the beadbox-windows.md symptom (missing comment bodies, link to upstream issue 27), (2) the current pinned version (bd v1.0.4 per beadbox-windows.md:45-50 and CONTEXT.md:197), (3) the exit-criterion for re-upgrading (upstream BeadBox issue 27 closed AND a release of bd that fixes the comment-body regression), (4) the owner of the decision (Codex-Orchestrator or the Workflow Scout role).
acceptance_criteria: Decision record at .orchestrated-agents/decisions/bd-version-pin.md with date, symptom, version-changed-from, version-changed-to, rationale, exit-criterion, owner; beadbox-windows.md and CONTEXT.md sections cross-link to the decision bead

title: F2: POSIX oa.sh wrapper for orchestrated-agents framework
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a platform-support gap. README.md Platform Support section (lines 70-81, 70=heading, 72='Status: Windows-only.', 79='macOS and Linux are NOT supported by this version', 81='POSIX support is tracked as a follow-up bead') explicitly excludes macOS and Linux and references this follow-up. Without POSIX support, the framework is single-platform and any contributor on macOS or Linux must port oa.ps1 themselves.

## Actual Task
Implement oa.sh under .orchestrated-agents/bin/ with the same command surface as oa.ps1: status, key-setup, key-clear, un <bead-id> <role-name> [extra-prompt]. Port the role-name-to-agent-slug mapping (Get-AgentName at oa.ps1 lines 48-100) to POSIX shell-compatible syntax. Port the secret-handling DPAPI substitute to libsecret (Linux) and macOS keychain. Port Test-WrapperSelf to POSIX syntax (parse oa.sh with awk/grep). Update README Platform Support to remove the macOS/Linux exclusion and remove the F2 reference.

## Why This Is Useful
SocialHub is Linux-targeted in production (per AGENTS.md repo Boundaries), and future contributors may not use Windows. A Windows-only workflow blocks portability and excludes the most common code-author workstation OS. Closing F2 unlocks macOS/Linux contribution to the framework itself and aligns with the SocialHub product backend. It also forces a clean re-implementation of the secret-handling and self-check rules, which is an opportunity to harden them on Windows too.

## Flaw
The framework is bound to PowerShell 5.1 because oa.ps1 uses DPAPI SecureString conversion (lines 57-67 Get-SecretPlainText), PowerShell parse-based self-check (lines 167-197 Test-WrapperSelf), and PowerShell-specific scripting (here-strings, [Parameter()] blocks, [securestring] casts). None of these work in POSIX sh without re-implementation. The exclusion is documented but no implementation path is provided.

## Impact
If not fixed, the framework's contributor base is Windows-only. Any macOS or Linux contributor to SocialHub must either dual-boot Windows, run oa.ps1 under PowerShell Core / pwsh which has known DPAPI gaps, or operate outside the workflow. The framework cannot be adopted by non-Windows teams. Documentation Reviewer 21:38 acknowledged F2 as a real follow-up, not a documentation rot.

## Proposed Improvement
Add oa.sh under .orchestrated-agents/bin/ that mirrors the oa.ps1 interface. Implementation requirements: (1) role display-name to agent-slug mapping identical to Get-AgentName lines 50-76; (2) self-check that parses oa.sh and validates oa.cmd shim (or POSIX equivalent) and that every required role maps to a configured opencode.json agent; (3) secret-handling using secret-tool store (libsecret) on Linux and security add-generic-password on macOS, never echoing the secret value; (4) oa shim that detects Windows vs POSIX and invokes the right script; (5) README Platform Support section updated to remove the exclusion line and add a Compatibility section. The oa.ps1 stays as the Windows reference; oa.sh is the POSIX reference. Both must produce the same status object shape (role_agent_map, secret_present booleans, configuration paths).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role Selector debate runs on this follow-up bead before any implementation.
- Human-input gate runs to confirm POSIX workflow preferences (preferred shell, keychain access, preferred  d install path).
- Security Privacy Reviewer reviews the secret-handling portability (libsecret / keychain) before implementation.
- Workflow Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial Reviewer confirms the oa.sh interface parity with oa.ps1
- QA Strategist runs an end-to-end smoke-test on POSIX (status + run <bead-id> <role>) and confirms the audit trail matches the Windows flow.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and discoverable from epic socialhub-v8g.
design: Mirror the oa.ps1 interface: status (returns role_agent_map and secret-presence booleans), key-setup / key-clear (using libsecret / macOS keychain instead of DPAPI), run <bead-id> <role-name> [extra-prompt]. Replace PowerShell here-strings with POSIX sh-compatible syntax. Use rg / git status / git diff / bd family commands the same way. The wrapper must NOT do the role work itself - only set env vars (BEADS_ACTOR, OA_TARGET_BEAD, OA_ROLE_NAME) and spawn opencode.
acceptance_criteria: oa.sh script committed under .orchestrated-agents/bin/ with status / key-setup / key-clear / run commands; smoke-test on macOS passes; README Platform Support updated to remove the macOS/Linux exclusion
notes: Discovered during socialhub-v8g.4 audit. README Platform Support section (lines 70-81) explicitly states 'macOS and Linux are NOT supported by this version' and points to this follow-up. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 did NOT flag POSIX as out of scope, and F2 is not security-sensitive at the design level; once oa.sh exists, the secret-handling rules from oa.ps1 lines 57-143 must be ported with an equivalent keychain-backed SecureString.
close_reason: Removed from active backlog per user direction on 2026-07-15: clean development focus is now SocialHub LangGraph platform-agent product work, not the experimental orchestrated-agents workflow backlog. Historical audit trail retained in closed Beads.

value: Target: ONE visible conversational agent. Intent recognition is planning input, never the router - the agent loop is the controller. LangGraph is the durable harness (lifecycle, state, interrupts, task progress); the model does understanding/planning/tool selection; deterministic code keeps security, policy and execution. Deterministic provider work is a tool or adapter, never a sub-agent.

Never run bd init inside socialbackend or socialUI. One product = one Beads database = one cross-repo dependency graph. issues.jsonl is export/backup only, never the sync channel; use bd dolt push/pull.

Provider access/refresh tokens are written and read ONLY through app/services/credential_store.py (G1B.4). Provider services never encrypt. AES-256-GCM lives in app/core/credential_encryption.py; envelope ENC1:<key_version>:<b64>, key material only from PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS, never in the DB. Modes disabled/dual/encrypted_only/strict are the migration phases. A guard test fails if any module outside the boundary touches access_token, refresh_token or page_access_token - in dual mode a direct read keeps working and would only break in production later.

Backend is NEVER pushed to GitHub. Production deploy = approved SCP to /home/ubuntu/fb_agent/ then Docker rebuild, container socialhub-api, server env /home/ubuntu/fb_agent/.env. Frontend deploys via Vercel from its own repo. Follow AWS-DEPLOY-GUIDE.md.

Ask only when the missing information materially changes the action or makes execution unsafe. Enforce as an evaluation invariant, not prompt wording. clarification / choice / approval / connection / authentication are five DISTINCT stop reasons - never substitute clarification for approval on a fully specified consequential request.

The pre-LangGraph custom agent runtime is removed and approved for deletion. Do not reintroduce the class-based orchestrator, planner runtime, manual state store, or pre-thread command/confirm compatibility adapters. Graph nodes must not perform direct mutations.

Exactly one backend LLM gateway: app/services/agent_llm_gateway.py with model policy in app/config/glm_models.json. No provider branches, no per-agent hardcoded models, no user-facing model/provider/key controls. Never send secrets to the model.

REFINE, NOT REWRITE. Never delete main_routing.py and rebuild in one shot - 443 passing backend tests are the characterization net. New task runtime lands behind a feature flag beside the existing router (strangler), scenarios migrate one at a time, old routing is deleted only by G4.10 after shadow/canary passes. The failure to avoid is three runtimes: legacy REST + old LangGraph routing + new agent loop.

SocialHub = root socialAgent git repo + nested socialbackend and socialUI git repos (three separate remotes). Canonical Beads DB is root .beads. Nested .git boundaries stop bd discovery: use BEADS_DIR or bd -C <repo-root>. Docs referencing fb_agent/ or fb_dash/ are stale path names.

A capability is not migrated because an implementation exists. Close migration work only with evidence the ACTIVE production entrypoint calls it. Precedent: exactly-once scheduling was marked PASS while APScheduler still called the unguarded legacy path.

Alembic is the single schema authority. Import-time create_all(), ad hoc ALTER TABLE and any public DB-init endpoint are prohibited. Migrations, production schema/data, OAuth redirect URIs, production CORS, secrets and deployment all require explicit human approval.

Never place tokens, refresh tokens, API keys, cookies, authorization headers, DB sessions, ORM objects or service clients into prompts, graph state, checkpoints, long-term memory, traces, SSE, logs or user-visible responses. Service-layer print() bypasses the graph redaction layer.

Authenticated identity enters once at the auth boundary and is never re-derived. Never establish tenant from user_fb_id/fb_user_id query params, request body, OAuth state, or resource.user_id looked up from a client-supplied resource id.
